5.141.m: Then the goddess, having rubbed her own limbs thoroughly again and again, / and gathered all that scurf, then fashioned an elephant-faced one,

5.141.s:
caturhastaṃ mahākāyaṃ laṃbodarasamanvitam ..
sukautukakaraṃ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām .. 16 ..
5.141.d:
चतुर्हस्तं महाकायं लंबोदरसमन्वितम् ..
सुकौतुककरं तेषां सर्वेषां च दिवौकसाम् .. 16 ..
5.141.m: four-armed, huge-bodied, endowed with a pot-belly, / exciting great wonder among all those heaven-dwellers.

5.141.s:
tataḥ sa vinayādāha devīṃ śikharavāsinīm ..
yadarthamaṃba sṛṣṭo'haṃ tatkāryaṃ vada mā ciram .. 17 .
5.141.d:
ततः स विनयादाह देवीं शिखरवासिनीम् ..
यदर्थमंब सृष्टोऽहं तत्कार्यं वद मा चिरम् .. 17 .
5.141.m: Then he respectfully said to the goddess who dwells on the peak: / 'Tell me without delay, O Mother, the task for which I was created.

5.141.s: trailokye tvatprasādena nāsādhyaṃ vidyate mama .. .. 18 ..
5.141.d: त्रैलोक्ये त्वत्प्रसादेन नासाध्यं विद्यते मम .. .. 18 ..
5.141.m: In the three worlds, by your grace, nothing is impossible for me.'

5.141.s:
.. śrīdevyuvāca .. ..
martyaloke narā ye ca svargamokṣaparāḥ sadā ..
teṣāṃ vighnaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ śubhakṛtyeṣu caiva hi .. 19 ..
5.141.d:
.. श्रीदेव्युवाच .. ..
मर्त्यलोके नरा ये च स्वर्गमोक्षपराः सदा ..
तेषां विघ्नं त्वया कार्यं शुभकृत्येषु चैव हि .. 19 ..
5.141.m: The holy Goddess said: / Those men in the mortal world who are always intent upon heaven and liberation, / obstacles should be placed by you in their auspicious deeds.

5.141.s:
saritāṃ patayastriṃśacchaṃkavaḥ saptasaptatiḥ ..
mahāsarojaṣaṣṭiśca nikharvāṇāṃ ca viṃśatiḥ .. 6.142.20 ..
5.141.d:
सरितां पतयस्त्रिंशच्छंकवः सप्तसप्ततिः ..
महासरोजषष्टिश्च निखर्वाणां च विंशतिः .. 6.142.20 ..
5.141.m: Thirty 'lords of rivers' [oceans], seventy-seven śaṅkus, / sixty mahāsarojas, and twenty nikharvas,

5.141.s:
arbudāyutasaṃyuktāḥ koṭyo navatipañca ca ..
lakṣāśca paṃcapaṃcāśatsahasrāḥ paṃcaviṃśatiḥ..
śatāni navaṣaṣṭiśca gaṇāścānye'tra saṃsthitāḥ..21..
5.141.d:
अर्बुदायुतसंयुक्ताः कोट्यो नवतिपञ्च च ..
लक्षाश्च पंचपंचाशत्सहस्राः पंचविंशतिः..
शतानि नवषष्टिश्च गणाश्चान्येऽत्र संस्थिताः..21..
5.141.m: along with ninety-five crores, arbuda, and ayuta, / fifty-five lakhs, twenty-five thousand, / and six hundred and ninety other gaṇas reside here;

5.141.s:
yeṣāṃ nadī smṛtaḥ pūrvo mahākālastathā paraḥ..
te sarve vaśagāstubhyaṃ prabhavaṃtu gaṇottamāḥ..22..
5.141.d:
येषां नदी स्मृतः पूर्वो महाकालस्तथा परः..
ते सर्वे वशगास्तुभ्यं प्रभवंतु गणोत्तमाः..22..
5.141.m: of whom Nadī is remembered as the first and Mahākāla as the next, / may all those best of gaṇas become subject to your command.

5.141.s:
ādhipatyaṃ mayā dattaṃ tava vatsa kuruṣva tat ..
sarveṣāṃ gaṇavṛṃdānāmādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ ..23..
5.141.d:
आधिपत्यं मया दत्तं तव वत्स कुरुष्व तत् ..
सर्वेषां गणवृंदानामाधिपत्ये व्यवस्थितः ..23..
5.141.m: Sovereignty has been granted by me to you, O child; exercise it, / established in the sovereignty over all the multitudes of gaṇas.

5.141.s:
evamuktvātha sā devī samānīyauṣadhībhṛtān ..
hemakuṃbhānsutīrthāṃbhaḥ paripūrṇānmahodayān.. 24 ..
5.141.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ सा देवी समानीयौषधीभृतान् ..
हेमकुंभान्सुतीर्थांभः परिपूर्णान्महोदयान्.. 24 ..
5.141.m: Having spoken thus, the goddess then brought golden jars / containing medicinal herbs, filled with water from excellent sacred fords, auspicious and grand.

5.141.s:
tasyābhiṣecanaṃ cakre svayameva sureśvarī ..
gītavādyavinodena nṛtyamaṃgalajaiḥ svanaiḥ .. 25 ..
5.141.d:
तस्याभिषेचनं चक्रे स्वयमेव सुरेश्वरी ..
गीतवाद्यविनोदेन नृत्यमंगलजैः स्वनैः .. 25 ..
5.141.m: The mistress of the gods herself performed his consecration / to the delight of songs and instrumental music, with sounds arising from auspicious dancing.

5.141.s:
trayastriṃśatsmṛtāḥ koṭayo devānāṃ yāḥ sthitā divi ..
tāḥ sarvāstatra cāgatya tasya cakruśca maṃgalam .. 26 ..
5.141.d:
त्रयस्त्रिंशत्स्मृताः कोटयो देवानां याः स्थिता दिवि ..
ताः सर्वास्तत्र चागत्य तस्य चक्रुश्च मंगलम् .. 26 ..
5.141.m: The thirty-three crores of gods who, it is recorded, reside in heaven, / all of them, having arrived there, performed auspicious rites for him.

5.141.s:
atha tasya dadau tuṣṭo bhagavānvṛṣabhadhvajaḥ ..
kuṭhāraṃ niśitaṃ haste sadā vai śreṣṭhamāyudham .. 27 ..
5.141.d:
अथ तस्य ददौ तुष्टो भगवान्वृषभध्वजः ..
कुठारं निशितं हस्ते सदा वै श्रेष्ठमायुधम् .. 27 ..
5.141.m: Then, delighted, the Lord whose banner is a bull gave him / a sharp battle-axe into his hand, truly the supreme weapon for ever.

5.141.s:
pātraṃ modakasaṃpūrṇamakṣayaṃ caiva pārvatī ..
bhojanārthe mahābhāgā mātṛsnehaparāyaṇā .. 28 ..
5.141.d:
पात्रं मोदकसंपूर्णमक्षयं चैव पार्वती ..
भोजनार्थे महाभागा मातृस्नेहपरायणा .. 28 ..
5.141.m: And Pārvatī [gave him] an inexhaustible vessel full of sweetmeats / for the purpose of food, the illustrious one devoted to maternal love.

5.141.s:
mūṣakaṃ kārtikeyastu vāhanārthaṃ praharṣitaḥ ..
bhrātaraṃ manyamānastu bandhusnehena saṃyutaḥ .. 29 ..
5.141.d:
मूषकं कार्तिकेयस्तु वाहनार्थं प्रहर्षितः ..
भ्रातरं मन्यमानस्तु बन्धुस्नेहेन संयुतः .. 29 ..
5.141.m: And Kārtikeya, greatly delighted, [gave him] a mouse / to serve as his mount, regarding him as a brother, endowed with affection for his kin.

5.141.s:
jñānaṃ divyaṃ dadau brahmā tasmai hṛṣṭena cetasā ..
atītānāgataṃ caiva vartamānaṃ ca yadbhavet..6.142.30..
5.141.d:
ज्ञानं दिव्यं ददौ ब्रह्मा तस्मै हृष्टेन चेतसा ..
अतीतानागतं चैव वर्तमानं च यद्भवेत्..6.142.30..
5.141.m: With a joyful mind Brahmā gave him divine knowledge, / whatever may be of the past, future, and present.

5.141.s:
prajñāṃ viṣṇuḥ sahasrākṣaḥ saubhāgyaṃ cottamaṃ mahat..
saubhāgyaṃ kāmadevastu kubero vibhavādikam..31..
5.141.d:
प्रज्ञां विष्णुः सहस्राक्षः सौभाग्यं चोत्तमं महत्..
सौभाग्यं कामदेवस्तु कुबेरो विभवादिकम्..31..
5.141.m: Viṣṇu [gave] intellect; the thousand-eyed one [gave] supreme, great good fortune; / Kāmadeva gave good fortune; Kubera [gave] riches and the like;

5.141.s: pratāpaṃ bhagavānsūryaḥ kāṃtimagryāṃ niśākaraḥ..32..
5.141.d: प्रतापं भगवान्सूर्यः कांतिमग्र्यां निशाकरः..32..
5.141.m: the Lord Sūrya gave splendor; the moon-maker [Candra] gave prime radiance.

5.141.s:
tathānye vibudhāḥ sarve daduriṣṭāni bhūriśaḥ..
ātmīyāni pratuṣṭyarthaṃ devyā devasya ca prabhoḥ..33..
5.141.d:
तथान्ये विबुधाः सर्वे ददुरिष्टानि भूरिशः..
आत्मीयानि प्रतुष्ट्यर्थं देव्या देवस्य च प्रभोः..33..
5.141.m: So all the other deities gave many desired things / belonging to themselves, for the pleasure of the Goddess and the lordly God.

5.141.s:
evaṃ labdhavaraḥ so'tha gaṇanātho dvijottamāḥ ..
devakṛtyaparo nityaṃ cakre vighnāni bhūtale .. 34 ..
5.141.d:
एवं लब्धवरः सोऽथ गणनाथो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
देवकृत्यपरो नित्यं चक्रे विघ्नानि भूतले .. 34 ..
5.141.m: Having thus obtained boons, O best of brahmins, that lord of gaṇas, / ever devoted to the service of the gods, created obstacles on the surface of the earth

5.141.s:
dharmārthaṃ yatamānānāṃ mokṣāya sukṛtāya ca ..
tato bhūmitale'bhyetya gaṇeśastatra yaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 35 ..
5.141.d:
धर्मार्थं यतमानानां मोक्षाय सुकृताय च ..
ततो भूमितलेऽभ्येत्य गणेशस्तत्र यः स्मृतः .. 35 ..
5.141.m: for those striving for righteousness, for liberation, and for good deeds. / Then, having arrived on the surface of the earth, that Ganeśa who is commemorated there,

5.141.s:
vaimānikaiḥ samabhyetya sthāpitastatra sa dvijāḥ ..
yena svargārthino lokāḥ pūjāṃ tasya pracakrire ..
prathamaṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu vighnanāśāya tatparāḥ .. 36 ..
5.141.d:
वैमानिकैः समभ्येत्य स्थापितस्तत्र स द्विजाः ..
येन स्वर्गार्थिनो लोकाः पूजां तस्य प्रचक्रिरे ..
प्रथमं सर्वकृत्येषु विघ्ननाशाय तत्पराः .. 36 ..
5.141.m: having arrived, was installed there by those possessing aerial chariots, O brahmins, / whereby people desirous of heaven performed worship to him / first in all undertakings, intent upon the destruction of obstacles.

5.141.s:
etasminneva kāle ca camatkārapurodbhavaiḥ ..
brāhmaṇairbrahmavijñānatatparairmokṣahetubhiḥ ..
īśānaḥ sthāpitastatra mokṣado ya udāhṛtaḥ .. 37 ..
5.141.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले च चमत्कारपुरोद्भवैः ..
ब्राह्मणैर्ब्रह्मविज्ञानतत्परैर्मोक्षहेतुभिः ..
ईशानः स्थापितस्तत्र मोक्षदो य उदाहृतः .. 37 ..
5.141.m: At that very time, by the brahmins born in Camatkārapura, / intent upon the knowledge of Brahman, seeking liberation, / Īśāna, who is proclaimed as the granter of liberation, was installed there.

5.141.s:
svargaṃ vāñchadbhirevānyaiḥ svargadvārapradastathā ..
heraṃbaḥ sthāpitastatra satyanāmā yathoditaḥ .. 38 ..
5.141.d:
स्वर्गं वाञ्छद्भिरेवान्यैः स्वर्गद्वारप्रदस्तथा ..
हेरंबः स्थापितस्तत्र सत्यनामा यथोदितः .. 38 ..
5.141.m: By others desiring heaven, Heramba, the granter of the door to heaven, / was installed there as described, truly matching his name.

5.141.s:
tathānyairmartyado nāma gaṇaiśastatra yaḥ sthitaḥ..
yena svargāccyutā yāṃti na kadā narakādikam..
tiryaktvaṃ vā kṛmitvaṃ vā sthāvaratvamathāpi vā .. 39 ..
5.141.d:
तथान्यैर्मर्त्यदो नाम गणैशस्तत्र यः स्थितः..
येन स्वर्गाच्च्युता यांति न कदा नरकादिकम्..
तिर्यक्त्वं वा कृमित्वं वा स्थावरत्वमथापि वा .. 39 ..
5.141.m: Likewise, by others [was installed] the lord of gaṇas named 'Granter of Mortal Existence' stationed there, / through whom those fallen from heaven never go to hell and the like, / nor to the state of animals, or of worms, or of immovable beings.

5.141.s:
etasmātkāraṇāttatra kṣetre puṇye dvijottamāḥ ..
herambo martyado jātaḥ svargiṇāṃ martyadaḥ sadā .. 6.142.40 ..
5.141.d:
एतस्मात्कारणात्तत्र क्षेत्रे पुण्ये द्विजोत्तमाः ..
हेरम्बो मर्त्यदो जातः स्वर्गिणां मर्त्यदः सदा .. 6.142.40 ..
5.141.m: For this reason, in that holy sacred field, O best of brahmins, / Heramba became the granter of mortal existence, always the granter of mortal existence to the dwellers of heaven.

5.141.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ puṇyaṃ heraṃbasaṃbhavam ..
ākhyānaṃ sarvavighnāni yannihanti śrutaṃ nṛṇām .. 41 ..
5.141.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं पुण्यं हेरंबसंभवम् ..
आख्यानं सर्वविघ्नानि यन्निहन्ति श्रुतं नृणाम् .. 41 ..
5.141.m: This entire holy narrative concerning the origin of Heramba has been related to you, / which, when heard, destroys all obstacles for men.

5.141.s:
etanmāghacaturthāṃ? yaḥ śuklāyāṃ pūjayennaraḥ ..
na tasya vatsaraṃ yāvadvighnaṃ sañjāyate kvacit .. 42 ..
5.141.d:
एतन्माघचतुर्थां? यः शुक्लायां पूजयेन्नरः ..
न तस्य वत्सरं यावद्विघ्नं सञ्जायते क्वचित् .. 42 ..
5.141.m: Whatever person worships him on this fourth day of the bright half of Māgha, / no obstacle arises anywhere for him for a year.

5.141.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye gaṇapatitrayamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvicatvāriṃśaduttaraśata tamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 142 .. .. cha ..
5.141.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये गणपतित्रयमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्विचत्वारिंशदुत्तरशत तमोऽध्यायः .. 142 .. .. छ ..
5.141.m: Thus ends the one hundred and forty-second chapter, named 'The Description of the Māhātmya of the Three Gaṇapatis', in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.142.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti devaścitreśvaro dvijāḥ ..
citrapīṭhasya madhyasthaścitrasaukhyaprado nṛṇām .. 1 ..
5.142.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्योऽपि च तत्रास्ति देवश्चित्रेश्वरो द्विजाः ..
चित्रपीठस्य मध्यस्थश्चित्रसौख्यप्रदो नृणाम् .. 1 ..
5.142.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is also another deity there, Citreśvara, O brahmins, / seated in the middle of Citrapīṭha, granting varied happiness to men;

5.142.s:
yaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjayitvā ca snāpayitvāthavā naraḥ ..
mucyate paradārotthaiḥ pātakaiścopapātakaiḥ .. 2 ..
5.142.d:
यं दृष्ट्वा पूजयित्वा च स्नापयित्वाथवा नरः ..
मुच्यते परदारोत्थैः पातकैश्चोपपातकैः .. 2 ..
5.142.m: whom having seen, worshipped, or bathed, a person / is freed from sins and secondary sins arising from [adultery with] another's wife,

5.142.s:
dharṣayitvā guroḥ patnīṃ kanyāṃ vā nijavaṃśajām ..
nīcāṃ vā vratayuktāṃ vā kāmāsaktena cetasā .. 3 ..
5.142.d:
धर्षयित्वा गुरोः पत्नीं कन्यां वा निजवंशजाम् ..
नीचां वा व्रतयुक्तां वा कामासक्तेन चेतसा .. 3 ..
5.142.m: [such as] having violated the guru's wife, or a maiden born in one's own family, / or a low-caste woman, or one observing a vow, with a mind attached to lust.

5.142.s:
caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ yastaṃ pūjayate naraḥ ..
sa tatpāpaṃ nihatyāśu svargalokaṃ tato vrajet .. 4 ..
5.142.d:
चैत्रशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां यस्तं पूजयते नरः ..
स तत्पापं निहत्याशु स्वर्गलोकं ततो व्रजेत् .. 4 ..
5.142.m: The man who worships it on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra / destroys that sin quickly and then goes to heaven. (4)

5.142.s:
tathā citrāṃgadastatra jābālisahito nṛpaḥ ..
kumāryā sahitaḥ sārddhaṃ nagnayā tatsamutthayā ..
santiṣṭhate tadagre tu śapto jābālinā purā .. 5 ..
5.142.d:
तथा चित्रांगदस्तत्र जाबालिसहितो नृपः ..
कुमार्या सहितः सार्द्धं नग्नया तत्समुत्थया ..
सन्तिष्ठते तदग्रे तु शप्तो जाबालिना पुरा .. 5 ..
5.142.m: Likewise, King Citrāṅgada stays there together with Jābāli, / accompanied by his naked daughter who was born of him; / indeed, he stands before him, having been cursed by Jābāli in the past. (5)

5.142.s:
trayāṇāmapi yasteṣāṃ tasminnahani nirvapet ..
sa iṣṭāṃ labhate nārīṃ siddhiṃ ca manasi sthitām .. 6 ..
5.142.d:
त्रयाणामपि यस्तेषां तस्मिन्नहनि निर्वपेत् ..
स इष्टां लभते नारीं सिद्धिं च मनसि स्थिताम् .. 6 ..
5.142.m: Whoever makes offerings for all three of them on that day / obtains the desired woman and the accomplishment set in his mind. (6)

5.142.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kasmājjābālinā śaptaḥ pūrvaṃ citrāṃgado yuvā ..
sā ca tattanayā kasmātkumārī vastravarjitā .. 7 ..
5.142.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कस्माज्जाबालिना शप्तः पूर्वं चित्रांगदो युवा ..
सा च तत्तनया कस्मात्कुमारी वस्त्रवर्जिता .. 7 ..
5.142.m: The seers said: / Why was the youth Citrāṅgada cursed by Jābāli in the past? / And why is that maiden, his daughter, stripped of garments? (7)

5.142.s:
adyāpi tiṣṭhate tatra viruddhaṃ rūpamāśritā ..
janahāsya karaṃ nityaṃ tasmātsūta vadasva naḥ .. 8 ..
5.142.d:
अद्यापि तिष्ठते तत्र विरुद्धं रूपमाश्रिता ..
जनहास्य करं नित्यं तस्मात्सूत वदस्व नः .. 8 ..
5.142.m: Even today she remains there, having assumed a contradictory form / that constantly provokes laughter among people. Therefore, Sūta, tell us! (8)

5.142.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ārsotpūrvaṃ munirnāmnā jābāliriti viśrutaḥ ..
kaumārabrahmacaryeṇa yena cīrṇaṃ tapaḥ sadā .. 9 ..
5.142.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
आर्सोत्पूर्वं मुनिर्नाम्ना जाबालिरिति विश्रुतः ..
कौमारब्रह्मचर्येण येन चीर्णं तपः सदा .. 9 ..
5.142.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, there was a sage known by the name Jābāli, / by whom austerity was constantly performed with lifelong celibacy. (9)

5.142.s:
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ samāsādya sa saddvijāḥ ..
bālye'pi vayasi prāpte samārebhe mahattapaḥ .. 6.143.10 ..
5.142.d:
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं समासाद्य स सद्द्विजाः ..
बाल्येऽपि वयसि प्राप्ते समारेभे महत्तपः .. 6.143.10 ..
5.142.m: Having reached the sacred field originating from Hāṭakeśvara, O good brahmins, / he undertook great austerity even when he had reached his childhood age. (10)

5.142.s:
kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādīni pārākāṇi śanaiḥśanaiḥ ..
kurvatā tena te devāḥ saṃnītā bhayagocaram .. 11 ..
5.142.d:
कृच्छ्रचांद्रायणादीनि पाराकाणि शनैःशनैः ..
कुर्वता तेन ते देवाः संनीता भयगोचरम् .. 11 ..
5.142.m: As he gradually performed the kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa, and other parāka penances, / the gods were brought into the range of fear by him. (11)

5.142.s:
tataḥ śakrādayo devāḥ saṃtrastā merumūrdhani ..
militvā cakrire maṃtraṃ tasya vighnakṛte mithaḥ ..12..
5.142.d:
ततः शक्रादयो देवाः संत्रस्ता मेरुमूर्धनि ..
मिलित्वा चक्रिरे मंत्रं तस्य विघ्नकृते मिथः ..12..
5.142.m: Then the gods, led by Śakra, terrified on the summit of Meru, / gathered together and took counsel with one another to cause him an obstacle: (12)

5.142.s:
yadyasya tapaso vṛddhirevaṃ yāsyati nityaśaḥ ..
cyāvayiṣyati tannūnaṃ svargarājyācchatakratum ..13..
5.142.d:
यद्यस्य तपसो वृद्धिरेवं यास्यति नित्यशः ..
च्यावयिष्यति तन्नूनं स्वर्गराज्याच्छतक्रतुम् ..13..
5.142.m: “If the increase of his austerity continues in this way constantly, / he will surely depose Śatakratu from the kingdom of heaven. (13)

5.142.s:
tasmādgacchatu raṃbhākhyā tatpārśve 'psarasāṃ varā ..
brahmacaryavighātāya tasyarṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ .. 14 ..
5.142.d:
तस्माद्गच्छतु रंभाख्या तत्पार्श्वे ऽप्सरसां वरा ..
ब्रह्मचर्यविघाताय तस्यर्षेर्भावितात्मनः .. 14 ..
5.142.m: Therefore, let the best of apsarases, named Rambhā, go to his side / for the destruction of the celibacy of that cultivated seer. (14)

5.142.s:
brahmacaryaṃ tapomūlaṃ yataḥ saṃkīrtitaṃ dvijaiḥ ..
tasyābhāvātparikleśaḥ kevalaṃ na phalaṃ vrate .. 15 ..
5.142.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं तपोमूलं यतः संकीर्तितं द्विजैः ..
तस्याभावात्परिक्लेशः केवलं न फलं व्रते .. 15 ..
5.142.m: For celibacy is proclaimed by brahmins to be the root of austerity; / in its absence, there is mere distress, without fruit in the vow.” (15)

5.142.s:
evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā samāhūya tataḥ param ..
raṃbhāmūcurmaheṃdreṇa sarve devāstadādarāt .. 16 ..
5.142.d:
एवं ते निश्चयं कृत्वा समाहूय ततः परम् ..
रंभामूचुर्महेंद्रेण सर्वे देवास्तदादरात् .. 16 ..
5.142.m: Having made this decision, after that / all the gods, along with Mahendra, summoned Rambhā and respectfully said to her: (16)

5.142.s:
gaccha śīghraṃ mahābhāge jābāliryatra tiṣṭhati ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre tapovighnāya tasya vai .. 17 ..
5.142.d:
गच्छ शीघ्रं महाभागे जाबालिर्यत्र तिष्ठति ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे तपोविघ्नाय तस्य वै .. 17 ..
5.142.m: “Go quickly, O fortunate one, to where Jābāli stays / in the sacred field originating from Hāṭakeśvara, to cause an obstacle to his austerity! (17)

5.142.s:
te te bhāvāḥ prayoktavyāḥ kathāstāstā manoharāḥ ..
vardhayaṃtī tathā citte tasya kāmaṃ nirargalam .. 18 .. ..
5.142.d:
ते ते भावाः प्रयोक्तव्याः कथास्तास्ता मनोहराः ..
वर्धयंती तथा चित्ते तस्य कामं निरर्गलम् .. 18 .. ..
5.142.m: Various expressions are to be employed, and various charming stories, / thereby increasing unrestrained passion in his heart.” (18)

5.142.s:
.. raṃbhovāca .. ..
sa munirna vijānāti kāmadharmaṃ sureśvara ..
arasajñaṃ kathaṃ deva kariṣyāmi smarānvitam.. 19 ..
5.142.d:
.. रंभोवाच .. ..
स मुनिर्न विजानाति कामधर्मं सुरेश्वर ..
अरसज्ञं कथं देव करिष्यामि स्मरान्वितम्.. 19 ..
5.142.m: Rambhā said: / “That sage does not know the nature of passion, O lord of the gods. / How, O god, shall I make one who has no taste for pleasure possessed by love?” (19)

5.142.s:
.. indra uvāca .. ..
eṣa yāsyati madvākyādvasaṃtastasya sannidhau ..
asya saṃdarśanādeva bhaviṣyati sa sasmaraḥ .. 6.143.20 ..
5.142.d:
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
एष यास्यति मद्वाक्याद्वसंतस्तस्य सन्निधौ ..
अस्य संदर्शनादेव भविष्यति स सस्मरः .. 6.143.20 ..
5.142.m: Indra said: / “At my word, this Spring will go into his presence; / merely upon seeing him, he will become possessed of love. (20)

5.142.s:
tasmādgaccha drutaṃ tatra sahānena varānane ..
saṃsiddhirjāyate yena devakṛtyaṃ bhaveddrutam .. 21 ..
5.142.d:
तस्माद्गच्छ द्रुतं तत्र सहानेन वरानने ..
संसिद्धिर्जायते येन देवकृत्यं भवेद्द्रुतम् .. 21 ..
5.142.m: Therefore, go quickly there along with him, O fair-faced one, / so that success may arise and the task of the gods may be accomplished swiftly.” (21)

5.142.s:
atha sā taṃ praṇamyoccaiḥ prasthitā dharaṇītalam..
vasaṃtena samāyuktā jābāliryatra tiṣṭhati .. 22 ..
5.142.d:
अथ सा तं प्रणम्योच्चैः प्रस्थिता धरणीतलम्..
वसंतेन समायुक्ता जाबालिर्यत्र तिष्ठति .. 22 ..
5.142.m: Then, having bowed deeply to him, she departed for the surface of the earth, / accompanied by Spring, to where Jābāli stayed. (22)

5.142.s:
athākasmādaśokasya saṃjātaḥ puṣpasaṃcayaḥ ..
tilakasya ca cūtasya maṃjaryaḥ samupasthitāḥ .. 23 ..
5.142.d:
अथाकस्मादशोकस्य संजातः पुष्पसंचयः ..
तिलकस्य च चूतस्य मंजर्यः समुपस्थिताः .. 23 ..
5.142.m: Then suddenly there arose an abundance of flowers on the aśoka tree, / and blossoms appeared on the tilaka and mango trees. (23)

5.142.s:
śiśire ca sarojāni vikāsaṃ prāpureva hi ..
vavau ca surabhirvāyurdākṣiṇātyaḥ sukāmadaḥ .. 24 ..
5.142.d:
शिशिरे च सरोजानि विकासं प्रापुरेव हि ..
ववौ च सुरभिर्वायुर्दाक्षिणात्यः सुकामदः .. 24 ..
5.142.m: And even in the cool season lotuses truly bloomed, / and the fragrant southern wind, inspiring desire, blew. (24)

5.142.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāptā raṃbhā tatra varāpsarāḥ ..
salilāśayatīrastho jābāliryatra tiṣṭhati ... .. 25 ..
5.142.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्ता रंभा तत्र वराप्सराः ..
सलिलाशयतीरस्थो जाबालिर्यत्र तिष्ठति ... .. 25 ..
5.142.m: In the meantime, that excellent apsaras Rambhā arrived there, / where Jābāli was standing on the shore of a reservoir of water, (25)

5.142.s:
akṣamālādhṛtakaro japanmaṃtramanekadhā ..
abhīṣṭaṃ śraddhayā yukto vidhāya pitṛtarpaṇam .. 26 ..
atha saṃpaśyatastasya muktvā vastraparigraham ..1
5.142.d:
अक्षमालाधृतकरो जपन्मंत्रमनेकधा ..
अभीष्टं श्रद्धया युक्तो विधाय पितृतर्पणम् .. 26 ..
अथ संपश्यतस्तस्य मुक्त्वा वस्त्रपरिग्रहम् ..1
5.142.m:
holding a rosary in his hand, reciting various mantras, / filled with faith after having performed the desired water offering to the ancestors. (26)
Then, while he was looking on, having abandoned her clothes, (27a)

5.142.s: snānārthaṃ tajjalaṃ sā'tha praviveśa varāpsarāḥ .. 27 ..
5.142.d: स्नानार्थं तज्जलं साऽथ प्रविवेश वराप्सराः .. 27 ..
5.142.m: that excellent apsaras then entered that water in order to bathe. (27b)

5.142.s:
vivastrāṃ tāṃ samālokya so'pi yauvanaśālinīm..
yāmyānilena ca spṛṣṭaḥ kāmasya vaśago 'bhavat .. 28 ..
5.142.d:
विवस्त्रां तां समालोक्य सोऽपि यौवनशालिनीम्..
याम्यानिलेन च स्पृष्टः कामस्य वशगो ऽभवत् .. 28 ..
5.142.m: Beholding her disrobed and possessing youthfulness, / and touched by the southern wind, he too fell under the sway of desire. (28)

5.142.s:
tatastasyābhavatkaṃpastatkṣaṇādeva sanmune ..
akṣamālā karāgrācca papāta dharaṇītale .. 29 ..
5.142.d:
ततस्तस्याभवत्कंपस्तत्क्षणादेव सन्मुने ..
अक्षमाला कराग्राच्च पपात धरणीतले .. 29 ..
5.142.m: Then trembling arose in that good sage at that very moment, / and the rosary fell from the tip of his hand to the surface of the earth. (29)

5.142.s:
pulakaḥ sarvagātreṣu saṃjajñe'tīva dāruṇaḥ ..
aśrupātāḥ pataṃti sma koṣṇāḥ plāvitabhūtalāḥ .. 30 ..
5.142.d:
पुलकः सर्वगात्रेषु संजज्ञेऽतीव दारुणः ..
अश्रुपाताः पतंति स्म कोष्णाः प्लावितभूतलाः .. 30 ..
5.142.m: An intense bristling of hairs arose all over his limbs; / warm tears fell, inundating the ground. (30)

5.142.s:
atha taṃ kṣubhitaṃ jñātvā cittajñā sā varāpsarāḥ ..
nirgatya salilāttasmāccakre vastraparigraham.. .. 31 ..
5.142.d:
अथ तं क्षुभितं ज्ञात्वा चित्तज्ञा सा वराप्सराः ..
निर्गत्य सलिलात्तस्माच्चक्रे वस्त्रपरिग्रहम्.. .. 31 ..
5.142.m: Then, knowing him to be agitated, that excellent apsaras, skilled in reading the mind, / came out of that water and put on her clothes. (31)

5.142.s:
tatastasyāṃtike gatvā praṇipatya kṛtādarā ..
provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ varddhaṃtī tasya tanmatam .. 32 ..
āśrame sakalaṃ brahmankaccitte kuśalaṃ mune ..
svādhyāye tapasi prājña śiṣyeṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu .. 3_3 ..
.. muniruvāca.. .. 9..
5.142.d:
ततस्तस्यांतिके गत्वा प्रणिपत्य कृतादरा ..
प्रोवाच मधुरं वाक्यं वर्द्धंती तस्य तन्मतम् .. 32 ..
आश्रमे सकलं ब्रह्मन्कच्चित्ते कुशलं मुने ..
स्वाध्याये तपसि प्राज्ञ शिष्येषु मृगपक्षिषु .. 3_3 ..
.. मुनिरुवाच.. .. 9..
5.142.m:
Then, having approached his presence and bowed with respect, / she spoke sweet words, nurturing his disposition: (32)
“O brahmin, is all well in your hermitage, O sage? / In your Vedic study, in your austerity, O wise one, among your disciples, deer, and birds?” / The sage said: (33)

5.142.s:
kuśalaṃ me varārohe sarvatraivādhunā sthitam..
viśeṣeṇātra saṃprāptā sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitā..34..
5.142.d:
कुशलं मे वरारोहे सर्वत्रैवाधुना स्थितम्..
विशेषेणात्र संप्राप्ता सर्वलक्षणलक्षिता..34..
5.142.m: “All is well with me everywhere now, O woman of fair hips, / especially since you, marked with all auspicious marks, have arrived here. (34)

5.142.s:
kā tvaṃ vada mahābhāge mama manmathavardhanī..
kiṃ devī vāsurī vā kiṃ pannagī kiṃ tu mānuṣī..35..
5.142.d:
का त्वं वद महाभागे मम मन्मथवर्धनी..
किं देवी वासुरी वा किं पन्नगी किं तु मानुषी..35..
5.142.m: Tell me, who are you, O fortunate one, who increase my desire? / Are you a goddess, or an asura woman, or a nāga woman, or indeed a human? (35)

5.142.s:
nivedaya śarīre me kiṃ na paśyasi vepathum..
nirargalaśca romāṃco bāṣpapūraśca netrajaḥ..36..
5.142.d:
निवेदय शरीरे मे किं न पश्यसि वेपथुम्..
निरर्गलश्च रोमांचो बाष्पपूरश्च नेत्रजः..36..
5.142.m: Explain to me: do you not see the trembling in my body, / the unrestrained bristling of hairs, and the flood of tears arising from my eyes?” (36)

5.142.s:
raṃbhovāca..
kiṃ te gātrasvabhāvo'yam kiṃ vānyo vyādhisaṃbhavaḥ ..
kaccideva na te svāsthyaṃ prapaśyāmi śarīrajam .. 37 ..
5.142.d:
रंभोवाच..
किं ते गात्रस्वभावोऽयम् किं वान्यो व्याधिसंभवः ..
कच्चिदेव न ते स्वास्थ्यं प्रपश्यामि शरीरजम् .. 37 ..
5.142.m: Rambhā said: / “Is this natural to your limbs, or does it arise from some other disease? / Indeed, I do not see health in your body.” (37)

5.142.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
na me gātrasvabhāvo na vyādhibhiśca sulocane ..
śṛṇuṣva kāraṇaṃ kṛtsnaṃ yenedṛksaṃsthitaṃ vapuḥ .. 38 ..
5.142.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
न मे गात्रस्वभावो न व्याधिभिश्च सुलोचने ..
शृणुष्व कारणं कृत्स्नं येनेदृक्संस्थितं वपुः .. 38 ..
5.142.m: The sage said: / “It is not natural to my limbs, nor is it due to diseases, O fair-eyed one. / Hear the entire cause on account of which my body has become such: (38)

5.142.s:
yāvatī vartate velā tava darśanasaṃbhavā ..
tāvatkālamidaṃ rūpaṃ mama gātrasamudbhavam .. 30. ..
tadahaṃ manmathāviṣṭo darśanāttava śobhane ..
brahmacaryaparopītthaṃ mahāvratadharo'pi ca .. 6.143.40 ..
5.142.d:
यावती वर्तते वेला तव दर्शनसंभवा ..
तावत्कालमिदं रूपं मम गात्रसमुद्भवम् .. 30. ..
तदहं मन्मथाविष्टो दर्शनात्तव शोभने ..
ब्रह्मचर्यपरोपीत्थं महाव्रतधरोऽपि च .. 6.143.40 ..
5.142.m: For as much time as has passed since seeing you, / for that long this state has arisen in my limbs. / Therefore, I am overcome by love from the sight of you, O fair one, / even though I am devoted to celibacy and uphold great vows.” (39–40)

5.142.s:
.. raṃbhovāca . ..
yadyevaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha māṃ bhajasva yathāsukham ..
nātra kaścidbhaveddoṣaḥ paṇyanārī yato'smyaham .. 41 ..
5.142.d:
.. रंभोवाच . ..
यद्येवं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ मां भजस्व यथासुखम् ..
नात्र कश्चिद्भवेद्दोषः पण्यनारी यतोऽस्म्यहम् .. 41 ..
5.142.m: Rambhā said: / “If it is so, O best of brahmins, enjoy me as you please! / No fault could occur here, since I am a courtesan. (41)

5.142.s:
sādhāraṇā vayaṃ vipra yataḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā ..
sarveṣāmeva lokānāṃ viśeṣeṇa dvijanmanām .. 42 ..
5.142.d:
साधारणा वयं विप्र यतः सृष्टाः स्वयंभुवा ..
सर्वेषामेव लोकानां विशेषेण द्विजन्मनाम् .. 42 ..
5.142.m: For we were created common to all by the self-born [Brahmā], O brahmin, / for all the worlds, and especially for the twice-born. (42)

5.142.s:
ahaṃ cāpi samālokya tvāṃ mune manmathopamam .
hatā kāmaśaraistīkṣṇairna ca gaṃtuṃ samutsahe .. .. 43 ..
5.142.d:
अहं चापि समालोक्य त्वां मुने मन्मथोपमम् .
हता कामशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्न च गंतुं समुत्सहे .. .. 43 ..
5.142.m: And I too, beholding you resembling the god of love, O sage, / am struck by the sharp arrows of love and am unable to depart. (43)

5.142.s:
mayā dṛṣṭāḥ surāḥ pūrvaṃ yakṣā vidyādharāstathā ..
siddhāśca kiṃnarā nāgā guhyakāḥ kimu mānuṣāḥ .. 44 ..
5.142.d:
मया दृष्टाः सुराः पूर्वं यक्षा विद्याधरास्तथा ..
सिद्धाश्च किंनरा नागा गुह्यकाः किमु मानुषाः .. 44 ..
5.142.m: I have previously seen gods, yakṣas, vidyādharas, / siddhas, kinnaras, nāgas, and guhyakas, not to speak of humans. (44)

5.142.s:
nedṛgrūpaṃ vapusteṣāmekasyāpi vilokitam ..
madhye brāhmaṇaśārdūla tasmādbhaktāṃ bhajasva mām .. 45 ..
5.142.d:
नेदृग्रूपं वपुस्तेषामेकस्यापि विलोकितम् ..
मध्ये ब्राह्मणशार्दूल तस्माद्भक्तां भजस्व माम् .. 45 ..
5.142.m: A bodily form such as this has not been seen in any one of them / among them, O tiger among brahmins; therefore, enjoy me who am devoted to you!” (45)

5.142.s:
yo nārīṃ kāmasaṃtaptāṃ svayaṃ prāptāṃ parityajet ..
sa mūrkhaḥ pacyate ghore narake śāśvatīḥ samāḥ .. 46 ..
5.142.d:
यो नारीं कामसंतप्तां स्वयं प्राप्तां परित्यजेत् ..
स मूर्खः पच्यते घोरे नरके शाश्वतीः समाः .. 46 ..
5.142.m: "He who abandons a woman burning with desire who has come to him of her own accord— / that fool burns in a terrible hell for eternal years."

5.142.s:
evamuktvā tayā so'tha pariṣvakto mahāmuniḥ ..
anicchannapi vākyena hṛdayena ca saspṛhaḥ .. 47 ..
5.142.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तया सोऽथ परिष्वक्तो महामुनिः ..
अनिच्छन्नपि वाक्येन हृदयेन च सस्पृहः .. 47 ..
5.142.m: Having spoken thus, she embraced that great sage, / who, though refusing with his words, was full of longing in his heart.

5.142.s:
tato latāni kuṃje taṃ samānīya munīśvaram .
kāmaśāstroditairbhāvai rarāma kṛtrimairmunim .. 48 ..
5.142.d:
ततो लतानि कुंजे तं समानीय मुनीश्वरम् .
कामशास्त्रोदितैर्भावै रराम कृत्रिमैर्मुनिम् .. 48 ..
5.142.m: Then, leading that lord of sages into a bower of creepers, / she sported with the sage through artificial moods spoken of in the Kāmaśāstra.

5.142.s:
evaṃ tayā samaṃ tatra sthito yāvaddinakṣayam ..
kāmadharmasamāsaktaḥ saṃtyaktāśeṣakarmakaḥ .. 49 ..
5.142.d:
एवं तया समं तत्र स्थितो यावद्दिनक्षयम् ..
कामधर्मसमासक्तः संत्यक्ताशेषकर्मकः .. 49 ..
5.142.m: Thus he remained there with her until the close of day, / entirely attached to the duty of passion, having abandoned every single ritual action.

5.142.s:
tato niṣkāmatāṃ prāpto lajjayā parivāritaḥ ..
visasarja ca tāṃ raṃbhāṃ śaucaṃ cakre tataḥ param .. 6.143.50 ..
5.142.d:
ततो निष्कामतां प्राप्तो लज्जया परिवारितः ..
विससर्ज च तां रंभां शौचं चक्रे ततः परम् .. 6.143.50 ..
5.142.m: Then, having lost his desire, surrounded with shame, / he dismissed Rambhā and afterward performed his ritual purification.

5.142.s:
sāpi tena vinirmuktā kṛtakṛtyā vilāsinī .
prahṛṣṭā prayayau tatra yatra devāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 51 ..
5.142.d:
सापि तेन विनिर्मुक्ता कृतकृत्या विलासिनी .
प्रहृष्टा प्रययौ तत्र यत्र देवाः सवासवाः .. 51 ..
5.142.m: Released by him, having achieved her purpose, that charming woman / departed overjoyed to where the gods were, along with Indra.

5.142.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye jābālikṣobhaṇonāma tricatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 143 ..
5.142.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां सहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये जाबालिक्षोभणोनाम त्रिचत्वारिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 143 ..
5.142.m: Thus ends the one hundred and forty-third chapter, named 'The Agitation of Jābāli,' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.143.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sā gatvā tridivaṃ paścātsahasrākṣaṃ surairyutam ..
provāca bhagavandiṣṭyā kṣobhito'sau mahāmuniḥ .. 1 ..
5.143.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
सा गत्वा त्रिदिवं पश्चात्सहस्राक्षं सुरैर्युतम् ..
प्रोवाच भगवन्दिष्ट्या क्षोभितोऽसौ महामुनिः .. 1 ..
5.143.m: Sūta said: / Having gone to heaven, she then approached the thousand-eyed [Indra], who was accompanied by the gods, / and said, "O Blessed One, by good fortune that great sage has been agitated!

5.143.s:
tapastasya hataṃ kṛtsnaṃ yatkṛcchreṇa samācitam ..
tathā nistejasatvaṃ ca nītastvaṃ sukhabhāgbhava .. 2 ..
5.143.d:
तपस्तस्य हतं कृत्स्नं यत्कृच्छ्रेण समाचितम् ..
तथा निस्तेजसत्वं च नीतस्त्वं सुखभाग्भव .. 2 ..
5.143.m: "All his austerity, which had been accumulated with difficulty, is destroyed, / and he has been rendered lusterless; now partake of your happiness!"

5.143.s:
evamuktvā'tha sā raṃbhā śaṃsitā nikhilaiḥ suraiḥ ..
amogharetasastasya dadhre garbhaṃ nijodare . 3 .
5.143.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽथ सा रंभा शंसिता निखिलैः सुरैः ..
अमोघरेतसस्तस्य दध्रे गर्भं निजोदरे . 3 .
5.143.m: Having spoken thus, Rambhā, praised by all the gods, / carried in her womb the child of that [sage] whose semen is never fruitless.

5.143.s:
jābālirapi kṛtvā ca paścāttāpamanekadhā ..
bhūyastu tapasi sthitvā sthitastatraiva cāśrame .. 4 ..
5.143.d:
जाबालिरपि कृत्वा च पश्चात्तापमनेकधा ..
भूयस्तु तपसि स्थित्वा स्थितस्तत्रैव चाश्रमे .. 4 ..
5.143.m: Jābāli too, having felt remorse in many ways, / stood again in austerity and stayed right there in that hermitage.

5.143.s:
tatastu daśame māsi saṃprāpte suṣuve śubhām ..
kanyāṃ sarojapatrākṣīṃ divyalakṣaṇalakṣitām .. 5 ..
5.143.d:
ततस्तु दशमे मासि संप्राप्ते सुषुवे शुभाम् ..
कन्यां सरोजपत्राक्षीं दिव्यलक्षणलक्षिताम् .. 5 ..
5.143.m: Then, when the tenth month had arrived, she gave birth to an auspicious / girl with eyes like lotus petals, marked with divine characteristics.

5.143.s:
atha tāṃ mānuṣodbhūtāṃ matvā tasyaiva cāśramam ..
gatvā mumoca pratyakṣaṃ tasyarṣeścedamabravīt .. 6 ..
5.143.d:
अथ तां मानुषोद्भूतां मत्वा तस्यैव चाश्रमम् ..
गत्वा मुमोच प्रत्यक्षं तस्यर्षेश्चेदमब्रवीत् .. 6 ..
5.143.m: Then, considering her to be born of a mortal, she went to that very hermitage of his, / released her before the sage's eyes, and said to him:

5.143.s:
tava vīryasamudbhūtāmenāṃ majjaṭharoṣitām ..
kanyakāṃ muniśārdūla tasmātpālaya sāṃpratam .. 7 ..
5.143.d:
तव वीर्यसमुद्भूतामेनां मज्जठरोषिताम् ..
कन्यकां मुनिशार्दूल तस्मात्पालय सांप्रतम् .. 7 ..
5.143.m: "This girl was born of your seed and dwelt in my womb, / therefore, O tiger among sages, protect her now!

5.143.s:
na svarge vidyate vāso mānuṣāṇāṃ kathaṃcana ..
etasmātkāraṇāttubhyaṃ mayā brahmansamarpitā .. 8 ..
5.143.d:
न स्वर्गे विद्यते वासो मानुषाणां कथंचन ..
एतस्मात्कारणात्तुभ्यं मया ब्रह्मन्समर्पिता .. 8 ..
5.143.m: "There is in no way any dwelling in heaven for mortals; / for this reason, O brahmin, she has been handed over to you by me."

5.143.s:
evamuktvā yayau raṃbhā satvaraṃ tridaśālayam ..
jābālirapi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyakāṃ snehamāviśat .. 9 ..
5.143.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ रंभा सत्वरं त्रिदशालयम् ..
जाबालिरपि तां दृष्ट्वा कन्यकां स्नेहमाविशत् .. 9 ..
5.143.m: Having spoken thus, Rambhā went swiftly to the abode of the gods; / and Jābāli, seeing that little girl, was filled with affection.

5.143.s:
tatastāṃ kanyakāṃ kṛtvā suṣṭhu gupte latāgṛhe ..
rasairmiṣṭaphalodbhūtaiḥ pupoṣa ca divāniśam .. 6.144.10 ..
5.143.d:
ततस्तां कन्यकां कृत्वा सुष्ठु गुप्ते लतागृहे ..
रसैर्मिष्टफलोद्भूतैः पुपोष च दिवानिशम् .. 6.144.10 ..
5.143.m: Then, placing that little girl in a well-concealed bower of creepers, / he nourished her day and night with juices born of sweet fruits.

5.143.s:
sāpi kanyā parāṃ vṛddhiṃ śanairyāti dinedine .
śuklapakṣaṃ samāsādya yathā candrakalā divi .. 11 ..
5.143.d:
सापि कन्या परां वृद्धिं शनैर्याति दिनेदिने .
शुक्लपक्षं समासाद्य यथा चन्द्रकला दिवि .. 11 ..
5.143.m: That girl too slowly attained great growth day by day, / just like the crescent moon in the sky when it enters the bright fortnight.

5.143.s:
yathāyathātha sā yāti vṛddhiṃ kamalalocanā ..
tathātathāsya susneho jābālerapyavardhata . 12 .
5.143.d:
यथायथाथ सा याति वृद्धिं कमललोचना ..
तथातथास्य सुस्नेहो जाबालेरप्यवर्धत . 12 .
5.143.m: Just as that lotus-eyed girl grew, / so too did Jābāli's deep affection for her increase.

5.143.s:
sā śiśutve mṛgaiḥ sārddhaṃ pakṣibhiśca suśobhanā ..
krīḍāṃ cakre suviśrabdhairvardhayaṃtī munermudam .. 13 ..
5.143.d:
सा शिशुत्वे मृगैः सार्द्धं पक्षिभिश्च सुशोभना ..
क्रीडां चक्रे सुविश्रब्धैर्वर्धयंती मुनेर्मुदम् .. 13 ..
5.143.m: In her childhood, that very beautiful girl played with the deer / and birds, who were completely trusting, increasing the joy of the sage.

5.143.s:
tato bālyaṃ parityaktvā valkalāvṛtagātrikā ..
tasyarṣeḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu sāhāyyaṃ prakaroti ca .. 14 ..
5.143.d:
ततो बाल्यं परित्यक्त्वा वल्कलावृतगात्रिका ..
तस्यर्षेः सर्वकृत्येषु साहाय्यं प्रकरोति च .. 14 ..
5.143.m: Then, leaving childhood behind, her limbs covered in bark garments, / she would assist that seer in all his duties.

5.143.s:
samitkuśādi yatkiṃcitphalapuṣpasamanvitam ..
vanāttadānayāmāsa tasya prītimavardhayat .. .. 15 ..
5.143.d:
समित्कुशादि यत्किंचित्फलपुष्पसमन्वितम् ..
वनात्तदानयामास तस्य प्रीतिमवर्धयत् .. .. 15 ..
5.143.m: Whatever [she could find], sacrificial twigs, kuśa grass, and the like, along with fruits and flowers, / she brought from the forest, increasing his pleasure.

5.143.s:
tataḥ katipayāhasya phalārthaṃ sā mṛgekṣaṇā ..
nidāghasamaye dūraṃ svāśramātprajagāma ha .. 16 ..
5.143.d:
ततः कतिपयाहस्य फलार्थं सा मृगेक्षणा ..
निदाघसमये दूरं स्वाश्रमात्प्रजगाम ह .. 16 ..
5.143.m: Then, some days later, in the summer season, that deer-eyed girl / went far from her hermitage for the sake of fruit.

5.143.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra vimānavaramāśritaḥ ..
prāptaścitrāṃgadonāma gandharvastridivaukasām .. 17 ..
5.143.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र विमानवरमाश्रितः ..
प्राप्तश्चित्रांगदोनाम गन्धर्वस्त्रिदिवौकसाम् .. 17 ..
5.143.m: At that moment, riding a splendid aerial chariot, / a gandharva of the dwellers of heaven named Citrāṅgada arrived there.

5.143.s:
tena sā vijane bālā pūrṇacandranibhānanā ..
dṛṣṭā cāṃdramasī lekhā patiteva dharātale .. 18 ..
5.143.d:
तेन सा विजने बाला पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना ..
दृष्टा चांद्रमसी लेखा पतितेव धरातले .. 18 ..
5.143.m: He saw that girl in the solitude, her face like the full moon, / like a digit of the moon fallen upon the surface of the earth.

5.143.s:
tataḥ kāmaparītāṃgaḥ sovatīrya dharātalam..
vimānānmadhurairvākyaistāmuvāca kṛtāṃjaliḥ .. 19 ..
5.143.d:
ततः कामपरीतांगः सोवतीर्य धरातलम्..
विमानान्मधुरैर्वाक्यैस्तामुवाच कृतांजलिः .. 19 ..
5.143.m: Then, his body overcome with love, he descended to the earth / from his aerial chariot, and with joined palms addressed her in sweet words:

5.143.s:
kā tvaṃ kamalagarbhābhā nirjane'tha mahāvane ..
bhramasyekākinī bāle vanamadhye sulocane .. 6.144.20 ..
5.143.d:
का त्वं कमलगर्भाभा निर्जनेऽथ महावने ..
भ्रमस्येकाकिनी बाले वनमध्ये सुलोचने .. 6.144.20 ..
5.143.m: "Who are you, radiant as the womb of a lotus, / wandering alone, O fair-eyed maiden, in the midst of this desolate, great forest?"

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
ahaṃ phalavatīnāma jābālerduhitā mune ..
phalapuṣpārthamāyātā tadarthamiha kānane .. 21 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
अहं फलवतीनाम जाबालेर्दुहिता मुने ..
फलपुष्पार्थमायाता तदर्थमिह कानने .. 21 ..
5.143.m: The girl said: / "I am named Phalavatī, the daughter of the sage Jābāli; / I have come here into the forest for the sake of fruits and flowers, for his sake."

5.143.s:
.. citrāṃgada uvāca .. ..
kumārabrahmacārī sa śrūyate munisattamaḥ ..
tatkathaṃ tasya vāmoru tvaṃ jātā bhāryayā vinā .. 22 ..
5.143.d:
.. चित्रांगद उवाच .. ..
कुमारब्रह्मचारी स श्रूयते मुनिसत्तमः ..
तत्कथं तस्य वामोरु त्वं जाता भार्यया विना .. 22 ..
5.143.m: Citrāṅgada said: / "That best of sages is heard to be a lifelong celibate; / how then, O woman of lovely thighs, were you born to him without a wife?"

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
satyametanmahābhāga nāsti dāraparigrahaḥ ..
tasyarṣeḥ kiṃ tu saṃjātā yathā tanme'vadhāraya .. 23 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
सत्यमेतन्महाभाग नास्ति दारपरिग्रहः ..
तस्यर्षेः किं तु संजाता यथा तन्मेऽवधारय .. 23 ..
5.143.m: The girl said: / "This is true, O noble one, that seer has taken no wife; / but listen to me concerning how I was born:

5.143.s:
raṃbhā nāmāpsarāstena purā dṛṣṭā surāṃganā ..
tataḥ kāmaparītena sevitā ca yathāsukham..24 ..
5.143.d:
रंभा नामाप्सरास्तेन पुरा दृष्टा सुरांगना ..
ततः कामपरीतेन सेविता च यथासुखम्..24 ..
5.143.m: "Long ago, an apsaras named Rambhā, a celestial maiden, was seen by him; / then, overcome with desire, he enjoyed her at his pleasure.

5.143.s:
tatastadudarājjātā devaloke mahattare ..
tayāpi ceha tasyarṣerbhūya eva niyojitā .. 25 ..
5.143.d:
ततस्तदुदराज्जाता देवलोके महत्तरे ..
तयापि चेह तस्यर्षेर्भूय एव नियोजिता .. 25 ..
5.143.m: "Then I was born from her womb in the great world of the gods; / and by her I was once again brought here to that seer.

5.143.s:
evaṃ sa me pitā jāto jābālirmunisattamaḥ ..
poṣitā'haṃ tatastena nānāphalasamudravaiḥ .. 26 ..
5.143.d:
एवं स मे पिता जातो जाबालिर्मुनिसत्तमः ..
पोषिताऽहं ततस्तेन नानाफलसमुद्रवैः .. 26 ..
5.143.m: "Thus Jābāli, the best of sages, became my father, / and then I was nourished by him with the yields of various fruits.

5.143.s:
tataḥ phalavatī nāma kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā ..
mamānurūpametaddhi yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi .. 27 ..
5.143.d:
ततः फलवती नाम कृतं तेन महात्मना ..
ममानुरूपमेतद्धि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि .. 27 ..
5.143.m: "Then the name Phalavatī was given to me by that great soul; / this is appropriate for me, about which you are inquiring of me."

5.143.s:
.. citrāṃgada uvāca .. ..
tava rūpaṃ samālokya kāmasyāhaṃ vaśaṃ gataḥ ..
tasmādbhajasva māṃ bhīru no cedyāsyāmi saṃkṣayam .. 28 ..
5.143.d:
.. चित्रांगद उवाच .. ..
तव रूपं समालोक्य कामस्याहं वशं गतः ..
तस्माद्भजस्व मां भीरु नो चेद्यास्यामि संक्षयम् .. 28 ..
5.143.m: Citrāṅgada said: / "Beholding your beauty, I have fallen under the power of love; / therefore, accept me, O timid one, otherwise I will perish!

5.143.s:
ahaṃ citrāṃgadonāma gandharvastridivaukasām ..
tīrthayātrākṛte prāptaḥ kṣetre'smiñchraddhayā'nvitaḥ .. 29 ..
5.143.d:
अहं चित्रांगदोनाम गन्धर्वस्त्रिदिवौकसाम् ..
तीर्थयात्राकृते प्राप्तः क्षेत्रेऽस्मिञ्छ्रद्धयाऽन्वितः .. 29 ..
5.143.m: "I am a gandharva of the heaven-dwellers named Citrāṅgada; / I have arrived at this sacred field filled with faith for the purpose of a pilgrimage to sacred fords."

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
kumāradharmiṇī cāhamadyāpi vaśagā pituḥ ..
kāmadharmaṃ na jānāmi citrāṃgada kathaṃcana .. .. 6.144.30 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
कुमारधर्मिणी चाहमद्यापि वशगा पितुः ..
कामधर्मं न जानामि चित्रांगद कथंचन .. .. 6.144.30 ..
5.143.m: The girl said: / "I am still a virgin and even now subject to my father; / I do not know the ways of passion in any way, O Citrāṅgada.

5.143.s:
tasmātprārthaya me tātaṃ sa māṃ tubhyaṃ pradāsyati ..
anurūpāya yogyāya taruṇāya manasvinīm ..31 ..
5.143.d:
तस्मात्प्रार्थय मे तातं स मां तुभ्यं प्रदास्यति ..
अनुरूपाय योग्याय तरुणाय मनस्विनीम् ..31 ..
5.143.m: "Therefore, ask my father; he will give me, a sensible maiden, / to you, who are suitable, worthy, and young.

5.143.s:
mamāpi rucitaṃ citte tava vākyamidaṃ śubham ..
dhanyāhaṃ yadi te kaṇṭhamāliṃgāmi yathecchayā .. 32 ..
5.143.d:
ममापि रुचितं चित्ते तव वाक्यमिदं शुभम् ..
धन्याहं यदि ते कण्ठमालिंगामि यथेच्छया .. 32 ..
5.143.m: "These agreeable words of yours are pleasing to my heart as well; / I would be fortunate if I might embrace your neck as I wish."

5.143.s:
.. citrāṃgada uvāca .. ..
na śaknomi mahābhāge tāvatkālaṃ pratīkṣitum ..
māṃ dahatyeṣa gātrotthaḥ sumahānkāmapāvakaḥ .. 33 ..
5.143.d:
.. चित्रांगद उवाच .. ..
न शक्नोमि महाभागे तावत्कालं प्रतीक्षितुम् ..
मां दहत्येष गात्रोत्थः सुमहान्कामपावकः .. 33 ..
5.143.m: Citrāṅgada said: / "I am not able, O noble lady, to wait for that much time; / this immense fire of love arising from my body burns me.

5.143.s:
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ me ratidānena śobhane ..
ko jānāti hi taccittaṃ kīdṛgrūpaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 34 .. ..
5.143.d:
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं मे रतिदानेन शोभने ..
को जानाति हि तच्चित्तं कीदृग्रूपं भविष्यति .. 34 .. ..
5.143.m: "Therefore, grant me your favor by bestowing sexual pleasure, O fair one; / for who knows what the nature of his mind will be?"

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
evaṃ te vartamānasya mama tātaḥ prakopataḥ ..
dahiṣyati na saṃdehaḥ śāpaṃ dattvā sudāruṇam.. 35 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
एवं ते वर्तमानस्य मम तातः प्रकोपतः ..
दहिष्यति न संदेहः शापं दत्त्वा सुदारुणम्.. 35 ..
5.143.m: The girl said: / "If you behave in this manner, my father, out of great anger, / will burn you, having uttered a terrible curse, there is no doubt!"

5.143.s:
.. citrāṃgada uvāca .. ..
tava tātaḥ sa kālena māṃ dahiṣyati mānade ..
kāmānalaḥ punaḥ sadya eṣa bhasma kariṣyati ..36..
5.143.d:
.. चित्रांगद उवाच .. ..
तव तातः स कालेन मां दहिष्यति मानदे ..
कामानलः पुनः सद्य एष भस्म करिष्यति ..36..
5.143.m:
Citrāṅgada said:
Your father, O proud maiden, might burn me in the future, / but this fire of desire will burn me to ashes immediately. (36)

5.143.s:
evamuktvā'tha tāṃ bālāṃ vepamānāṃ trapāvatīm ..
gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe pāṇau praviveśa surālayam .. 37 ..
5.143.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽथ तां बालां वेपमानां त्रपावतीम् ..
गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे पाणौ प्रविवेश सुरालयम् .. 37 ..
5.143.m: Having spoken thus to that trembling and bashful girl, / he took her right hand and entered the abode of the gods. (37)

5.143.s:
tatra tāṃ ramayāmāsa tadā kāmaprapīḍitaḥ ..
tatkālajātarāgāṃdhāṃ nirlajjatvamupāgatām .. .. 38 ..
5.143.d:
तत्र तां रमयामास तदा कामप्रपीडितः ..
तत्कालजातरागांधां निर्लज्जत्वमुपागताम् .. .. 38 ..
5.143.m: Afflicted by desire, he then made love to her there, / who had become blind with freshly aroused passion and had cast off all shame. (38)

5.143.s:
evaṃ tasyāḥ samaṃ tena sthitāyā divaso gataḥ ..
nimeṣavanmuniśreṣṭhāstataścāstaṃ gato raviḥ .. 39 ..
5.143.d:
एवं तस्याः समं तेन स्थिताया दिवसो गतः ..
निमेषवन्मुनिश्रेष्ठास्ततश्चास्तं गतो रविः .. 39 ..
5.143.m: As she remained together with him in this manner, the day passed / like a mere blinking of the eye, O best of sages; and then the sun set. (39)

5.143.s:
etasminnaṃtare vipro jābālirduḥkha saṃyutaḥ ..
anāyātāṃ sutāṃ jñātvā paribabhrāma sarvataḥ .. 6.144.40 ..
5.143.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे विप्रो जाबालिर्दुःख संयुतः ..
अनायातां सुतां ज्ञात्वा परिबभ्राम सर्वतः .. 6.144.40 ..
5.143.m: Meanwhile, the brahmin Jābāli, filled with sorrow, / realizing that his daughter had not returned, wandered everywhere [in search of her]. (40)

5.143.s:
aho sā duhitā mahyaṃ kimu vyālaiḥ prabhakṣitā ..
vṛkṣaṃ kaṃcitsamārūḍhā patitā dharaṇī tale .. 41 ..
5.143.d:
अहो सा दुहिता मह्यं किमु व्यालैः प्रभक्षिता ..
वृक्षं कंचित्समारूढा पतिता धरणी तले .. 41 ..
5.143.m: [Thinking:] “Alas, has my daughter been devoured by serpents? / Has she climbed some tree and fallen down upon the surface of the earth? (41)

5.143.s:
kiṃ vā jalāśayaṃ kaṃcitprāpya gādhamajānatī ..
nimagnā tatra sā bālā saṃpraviṣṭā jalārthinī .. 42 ..
5.143.d:
किं वा जलाशयं कंचित्प्राप्य गाधमजानती ..
निमग्ना तत्र सा बाला संप्रविष्टा जलार्थिनी .. 42 ..
5.143.m: Or having reached some body of water and not knowing its depth, / did that girl, seeking water, enter and drown in it?” (42)

5.143.s:
evaṃ sa pralapanvipro babhrāma gahane vane ..
kuśakaṇṭakaviddhāṃgaḥ kṣutpipāsāsamākulaḥ .. 43 ..
5.143.d:
एवं स प्रलपन्विप्रो बभ्राम गहने वने ..
कुशकण्टकविद्धांगः क्षुत्पिपासासमाकुलः .. 43 ..
5.143.m: Lamenting thus, the brahmin wandered in the dense forest, / his limbs pierced by kuśa-grass and thorns, overwhelmed by hunger and thirst. (43)

5.143.s:
yaṃyaṃ śṛṇoti śabdaṃ sa mṛgapakṣisamudbhavam ..
rajanyāṃ tatra niryāti matvā phalavatīṃ ca tām .. 44 ..
5.143.d:
यंयं शृणोति शब्दं स मृगपक्षिसमुद्भवम् ..
रजन्यां तत्र निर्याति मत्वा फलवतीं च ताम् .. 44 ..
5.143.m: Whenever he heard any sound arising from beasts or birds / during the night, he went there, thinking that [search] might bear fruit. (44)

5.143.s:
atha kramātsamāyāto haraharmyaṃ sa sanmuniḥ ..
yatra citrāṃgadopetā sā saṃtiṣṭhati kanyakā .. 45 ..
5.143.d:
अथ क्रमात्समायातो हरहर्म्यं स सन्मुनिः ..
यत्र चित्रांगदोपेता सा संतिष्ठति कन्यका .. 45 ..
5.143.m: Then gradually that virtuous sage arrived at the mansion of Hara / where that maiden remained, together with Citrāṅgada, (45)

5.143.s:
niḥśaṃkā jalpamānā ca rāgavākyānyanekaśaḥ ..
anarhāṇi kumārīṇāṃ brahmajānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 46 ..
5.143.d:
निःशंका जल्पमाना च रागवाक्यान्यनेकशः ..
अनर्हाणि कुमारीणां ब्रह्मजानां विशेषतः .. 46 ..
5.143.m: fearlessly uttering words of passion again and again— / [words] entirely unworthy of maidens, especially those born of brahmins. (46)

5.143.s:
tataḥ sa suciraṃ śrutvā dūrastho vismayānvitaḥ ..
kumāryāśceṣṭitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ .. 47 ..
5.143.d:
ततः स सुचिरं श्रुत्वा दूरस्थो विस्मयान्वितः ..
कुमार्याश्चेष्टितं दृष्ट्वा कोपसंरक्तलोचनः .. 47 ..
5.143.m: Having listened for a long time from a distance, filled with astonishment / and seeing the conduct of his maiden [daughter], his eyes turned blood-red with rage. (47)

5.143.s:
atha dudrāva vegena gṛhya kāṣṭhasamuccayam ..
dvābhyāmeva vināśāya bhartsamāno muhurmuhuḥ .. 48 ..
5.143.d:
अथ दुद्राव वेगेन गृह्य काष्ठसमुच्चयम् ..
द्वाभ्यामेव विनाशाय भर्त्समानो मुहुर्मुहुः .. 48 ..
5.143.m: Then, seizing a bundle of sticks, he rushed forward swiftly, / repeatedly rebuking them so as to destroy them both: (48)

5.143.s:
dhigdhikpāpasamācāre kaumāryaṃ dūṣitaṃ tvayā ..
lāṃchanaṃ ca samānītaṃ mama lokatraye'pi ca .. 49 ..
5.143.d:
धिग्धिक्पापसमाचारे कौमार्यं दूषितं त्वया ..
लांछनं च समानीतं मम लोकत्रयेऽपि च .. 49 ..
5.143.m: “Fie, fie upon your sinful conduct! You have defiled your virginity, / and you have brought disgrace upon me even in the three worlds! (49)

5.143.s:
nitarāṃ patimāsādya karmaṇānena cādhame ..
tasmādanena pāpena yuktāṃ tvāṃ nāśayāmyaham .. 6.144.50 ..
5.143.d:
नितरां पतिमासाद्य कर्मणानेन चाधमे ..
तस्मादनेन पापेन युक्तां त्वां नाशयाम्यहम् .. 6.144.50 ..
5.143.m: By this deed, O vile girl, you have utterly degraded yourself before obtaining a husband! / Therefore, I shall destroy you who are laden with this sin!” (50)

5.143.s:
evamuktvā prahāraṃ sa yāvatkṣipati sanmuniḥ ..
tāvaccitrāṃgado naṣṭo vyomamārgeṇa satvaram .. 51 ..
5.143.d:
एवमुक्त्वा प्रहारं स यावत्क्षिपति सन्मुनिः ..
तावच्चित्रांगदो नष्टो व्योममार्गेण सत्वरम् .. 51 ..
5.143.m: Having spoken thus, just as that virtuous sage cast a blow, / Citrāṅgada quickly vanished through the path of the sky. (51)

5.143.s:
vivastrā sāpi tatraiva khinnāṃgī kāmasevayā ..
na śaśāka kvacidgaṃtuṃ samutthāya tataḥ kṣitau .. 52 ..
5.143.d:
विवस्त्रा सापि तत्रैव खिन्नांगी कामसेवया ..
न शशाक क्वचिद्गंतुं समुत्थाय ततः क्षितौ .. 52 ..
5.143.m: She too remained right there, naked, her limbs exhausted from the pursuit of love, / and standing up from the ground, she was unable to go anywhere. (52)

5.143.s:
tataḥ kāṣṭhaprahāroghairhatvā tāṃ patitāṃ kṣitau..
mṛtāmiti parijñāya sa krodhaparivāritaḥ .. 53 ..
5.143.d:
ततः काष्ठप्रहारोघैर्हत्वा तां पतितां क्षितौ..
मृतामिति परिज्ञाय स क्रोधपरिवारितः .. 53 ..
5.143.m: Then, having struck her with a flurry of blows with the stick as she fell to the ground, / and perceiving that she was dead, overcome by rage, (53)

5.143.s:
tataścitrāṃgadasyāpi dadau śāpaṃ sudāruṇam ..
sa dṛṣṭvā''kāśamārgeṇa gacchamānaṃ bhayāturam .. 54 ..
5.143.d:
ततश्चित्रांगदस्यापि ददौ शापं सुदारुणम् ..
स दृष्ट्वा'ऽकाशमार्गेण गच्छमानं भयातुरम् .. 54 ..
5.143.m: he then pronounced a terrible curse upon Citrāṅgada as well, / seeing him fleeing through the pathway of the sky, frantic with fear: (54)

5.143.s:
ya eṣa kanyakāṃ mahyaṃ dharṣayitvā samutpatet ..
sa patatvacirātpāpaśchinnapakṣa ivāṃḍajaḥ .. 55 ..
5.143.d:
य एष कन्यकां मह्यं धर्षयित्वा समुत्पतेत् ..
स पतत्वचिरात्पापश्छिन्नपक्ष इवांडजः .. 55 ..
5.143.m: “Let this wicked one, who has flown up after violating my daughter, / fall down without delay, like a bird with clipped wings, (55)

5.143.s:
kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktaścalituṃ naiva ca kṣamaḥ ..
etasminnantare bhūmau sa papāta nabhastalāt .. 56 ..
5.143.d:
कुष्ठव्याधिसमायुक्तश्चलितुं नैव च क्षमः ..
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भूमौ स पपात नभस्तलात् .. 56 ..
5.143.m: afflicted with the disease of leprosy and utterly unable to move!” / In that very moment, he fell to the earth from the vault of heaven, (56)

5.143.s:
kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktaḥ sa ca citrāṃgado yuvā ..
tatastaṃ sa muniḥ prāha kāṣṭhodyatakaraḥ krudhā .. 57 ..
5.143.d:
कुष्ठव्याधिसमायुक्तः स च चित्रांगदो युवा ..
ततस्तं स मुनिः प्राह काष्ठोद्यतकरः क्रुधा .. 57 ..
5.143.m: and the young Citrāṅgada was afflicted with the disease of leprosy. / Then the sage, raising the stick in his hand in anger, said to him: (57)

5.143.s:
kastvaṃ pāpasamācāra yena me dharṣitā balāt ..
kumārī tannayāmyeṣa tvāmadya yama śāsanam .. 58 ..
5.143.d:
कस्त्वं पापसमाचार येन मे धर्षिता बलात् ..
कुमारी तन्नयाम्येष त्वामद्य यम शासनम् .. 58 ..
5.143.m: “Who are you of sinful conduct by whom my maiden was violated by force? / Therefore I will send you today to the realm of Yama!” (58)

5.143.s:
.. citrāṃgada uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ citrāṃgadonāma gandharvastridivaukasām ..
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena kṣetre'sminsamupāgataḥ .. 59 ..
5.143.d:
.. चित्रांगद उवाच .. ..
अहं चित्रांगदोनाम गन्धर्वस्त्रिदिवौकसाम् ..
तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन क्षेत्रेऽस्मिन्समुपागतः .. 59 ..
5.143.m:
Citrāṅgada said:
“I am a gandharva of the heavenly denizens named Citrāṅgada. / On the occasion of a pilgrimage to sacred fords, I arrived at this sacred field. (59)

5.143.s: tatastu kanyakāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmadevavaśaṃ gataḥ .. 6.144.60 ..
5.143.d: ततस्तु कन्यकां दृष्ट्वा कामदेववशं गतः .. 6.144.60 ..
5.143.m: Then, beholding the maiden, I fell under the power of Kāmadeva. (60)

5.143.s:
tataḥ sevitavānatra latāharmye janacyute ..
tasmātkuru kṣamāṃ mahyaṃ dīnasya praṇatasya ca .. 61 ..
5.143.d:
ततः सेवितवानत्र लताहर्म्ये जनच्युते ..
तस्मात्कुरु क्षमां मह्यं दीनस्य प्रणतस्य च .. 61 ..
5.143.m: Then I enjoyed her here in this bower of creepers, deserted by people. / Therefore show forgiveness to me, miserable and bowed down [before you]. (61)

5.143.s:
yathā vyādherbhavennāśo yathā syādgagane gatiḥ ..
bhūyo'pi tvatprasādena svalpaḥ kopo hi sādhuṣu .. 62 ..
5.143.d:
यथा व्याधेर्भवेन्नाशो यथा स्याद्गगने गतिः ..
भूयोऽपि त्वत्प्रसादेन स्वल्पः कोपो हि साधुषु .. 62 ..
5.143.m: By your favor, may there be destruction of the disease, and may I once again move / through the sky; for the anger of the virtuous is indeed short-lived.” (62)

5.143.s:
.. jābāliruvāca .. ..
īdṛgrūpadharastvaṃ hi mama vākyādbhaviṣyasi ..
eṣāpi matsutā pāpā vastrahīnā sadedṛśī .. 63 ..
5.143.d:
.. जाबालिरुवाच .. ..
ईदृग्रूपधरस्त्वं हि मम वाक्याद्भविष्यसि ..
एषापि मत्सुता पापा वस्त्रहीना सदेदृशी .. 63 ..
5.143.m:
Jābāli said:
“Bearing such a form you shall indeed remain by my word! / And this sinful daughter of mine likewise, constantly devoid of garments, (63)

5.143.s:
bhaviṣyati na saṃdeho jīvayiṣyati cetkvacit ..
yadyeṣā dhāsyati kvāpi vastraṃ gātre nije kvacit .. 64 ..
5.143.d:
भविष्यति न संदेहो जीवयिष्यति चेत्क्वचित् ..
यद्येषा धास्यति क्वापि वस्त्रं गात्रे निजे क्वचित् .. 64 ..
5.143.m: shall remain without doubt, if she should revive at any time. / If she should ever put a garment on her own body anywhere, (64)

5.143.s:
tannūnaṃ ca śiro'pyasyāḥ phaliṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ..
evamuktvā vikopaśca sa jagāma nijāśramam .. 65 ..
5.143.d:
तन्नूनं च शिरोऽप्यस्याः फलिष्यति न संशयः ..
एवमुक्त्वा विकोपश्च स जगाम निजाश्रमम् .. 65 ..
5.143.m: then her head will surely burst into pieces, of this there is no doubt!” / Having spoken thus, his anger subsided, and he went to his own hermitage. (65)

5.143.s:
citrāṃgado'pi tatraiva tayā sārdhaṃ tathā sthitaḥ ..
kasyacittvatha kālasya tatra kṣetre samāyayau .. 66 ..
5.143.d:
चित्रांगदोऽपि तत्रैव तया सार्धं तथा स्थितः ..
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य तत्र क्षेत्रे समाययौ .. 66 ..
5.143.m: Citrāṅgada too stayed right there with her in that condition. / After some time, there came to that sacred field, (66)

5.143.s:
caitraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ bhagavāñchaśiśekharaḥ ..
gantuṃ citreśvare pīṭhe gaṇai raudraiḥ samāvṛtaḥ ..
yoginībhiḥ pracaṇḍābhiḥ sārdhaṃ prāpte niśāmukhe .. 67 ..
5.143.d:
चैत्रशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां भगवाञ्छशिशेखरः ..
गन्तुं चित्रेश्वरे पीठे गणै रौद्रैः समावृतः ..
योगिनीभिः प्रचण्डाभिः सार्धं प्राप्ते निशामुखे .. 67 ..
5.143.m: on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Caitra, the Lord who bears the moon on his crest, / surrounded by fierce gaṇas, to go to the Citreśvara seat / along with the terrifying yoginīs, as the night set in. (67)

5.143.s:
atha prāpte niśārdhe tu yoginyastāḥ sudāruṇāḥ ..
mahāmāṃsaṃ mahāmāṃsamityūcurbhakṣaṇāya vai ..68..
5.143.d:
अथ प्राप्ते निशार्धे तु योगिन्यस्ताः सुदारुणाः ..
महामांसं महामांसमित्यूचुर्भक्षणाय वै ..68..
5.143.m: Then, when midnight arrived, those dread yoginīs / indeed cried out for food: “Human flesh! Human flesh!” (68)

5.143.s:
nṛtyamānāḥ purastasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
saspardhā gaṇamukhyaistairnartamānaiḥ samaṃtataḥ ..69 ..
5.143.d:
नृत्यमानाः पुरस्तस्य देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
सस्पर्धा गणमुख्यैस्तैर्नर्तमानैः समंततः ..69 ..
5.143.m: dancing in front of the trident-bearing God of gods, / in competition with those chiefs of gaṇas who were dancing all around. (69)

5.143.s:
yastatra samaye tāsāṃ mahāmāṃsaṃ prayacchati ..
maṃtrapūtaṃ sa saṃsiddhiṃ samavāpnoti vāṃchitām .. 6.144.70 ..
5.143.d:
यस्तत्र समये तासां महामांसं प्रयच्छति ..
मंत्रपूतं स संसिद्धिं समवाप्नोति वांछिताम् .. 6.144.70 ..
5.143.m: Whoever gives them human flesh sanctified by mantras at that time / attains his desired accomplishment. (70)

5.143.s:
madyaṃ māṃsaṃ tathā cānyannaivedyaṃ vā phalādikam ..
tasya siddhiḥ samādiṣṭā yathā svahṛdaye sthitā .. 71 ..
5.143.d:
मद्यं मांसं तथा चान्यन्नैवेद्यं वा फलादिकम् ..
तस्य सिद्धिः समादिष्टा यथा स्वहृदये स्थिता .. 71 ..
5.143.m: Or wine, meat, and other offerings, or fruits and the like— / an accomplishment is proclaimed for him in accordance with what is in his heart. (71)

5.143.s:
etasminnaṃtare kanyā sā jābālisamudbhavā ..
sa ca citrāṃgadastatra gatvā provāca sādaram .. 72..
5.143.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे कन्या सा जाबालिसमुद्भवा ..
स च चित्रांगदस्तत्र गत्वा प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 72..
5.143.m: In the meantime, that maiden born of Jābāli / and Citrāṅgada went there and respectfully said: (72)

5.143.s:
asmadīyamidaṃ māṃsaṃ yoginyo harṣasaṃyutāḥ ..
bhakṣayantu yathāsaukhyaṃ svayameva prakalpitam .. 73 ..
5.143.d:
अस्मदीयमिदं मांसं योगिन्यो हर्षसंयुताः ..
भक्षयन्तु यथासौख्यं स्वयमेव प्रकल्पितम् .. 73 ..
5.143.m: “Let the yoginīs, filled with joy, consume this flesh of ours, / offered by ourselves, as they please.” (73)

5.143.s:
atha taṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kuṣṭhavyādhisamāvṛtam ..
vivastrāṃ kanyakāṃ tāṃ ca sarvāstā vismayānvitāḥ .. 74 ..
5.143.d:
अथ तं पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा कुष्ठव्याधिसमावृतम् ..
विवस्त्रां कन्यकां तां च सर्वास्ता विस्मयान्विताः .. 74 ..
5.143.m: Then, seeing that man afflicted with the disease of leprosy / and that maiden devoid of clothing, all of them were filled with wonder. (74)

5.143.s:
te ca sarve gaṇā raudrāḥ sa ca devastrilocanaḥ ..
papraccha kautukāviṣṭastatra citrāṃgadaṃ prabhuḥ .. 75 ..
5.143.d:
ते च सर्वे गणा रौद्राः स च देवस्त्रिलोचनः ..
पप्रच्छ कौतुकाविष्टस्तत्र चित्रांगदं प्रभुः .. 75 ..
5.143.m: All those fierce gaṇas and that three-eyed God, / the Lord, filled with curiosity, asked Citrāṅgada there: (75)

5.143.s:
kastvaṃ dhairyasamāyukto mahatsattve vyavasthitaḥ ..
yaḥ prayacchasi jīvaṃ tvaṃ kīṭasyāpi suvallabham .. 76 ..
5.143.d:
कस्त्वं धैर्यसमायुक्तो महत्सत्त्वे व्यवस्थितः ..
यः प्रयच्छसि जीवं त्वं कीटस्यापि सुवल्लभम् .. 76 ..
5.143.m: “Who are you, endowed with fortitude and established in great noble resolve, / who offer your life, which is very dear even to a worm? (76)

5.143.s:
keyaṃ ca vasanaiṃrhīnā tvayā sārdhaṃ gatavyathā ..
prayacchati nijaṃ dehaṃ yaddeyaṃ naiva kasyacit .. 77 ..
5.143.d:
केयं च वसनैंर्हीना त्वया सार्धं गतव्यथा ..
प्रयच्छति निजं देहं यद्देयं नैव कस्यचित् .. 77 ..
5.143.m: And who is this [woman], stripped of garments, who along with you is freed from anguish / and offers her own body, which should never be given to anyone?” (77)

5.143.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa sarvamātmaviceṣṭitam ..
yathā kanyāsamaṃ saṃgaḥ kṛtaḥ śāpaśca sanmuneḥ .. 78 ..
5.143.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततः स कथयामास सर्वमात्मविचेष्टितम् ..
यथा कन्यासमं संगः कृतः शापश्च सन्मुनेः .. 78 ..
5.143.m:
Sūta said:
Then he related all of his own doings: / how his union with the maiden took place, and the curse of the virtuous sage. (78)

5.143.s:
tataścitrāṃgadaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa gandharvaṃ divaukasām ..
tathārūpaṃ kṛpāviṣṭastataḥ provāca śaṃkaraḥ .. 79 ..
5.143.d:
ततश्चित्रांगदं दृष्ट्वा स गन्धर्वं दिवौकसाम् ..
तथारूपं कृपाविष्टस्ततः प्रोवाच शंकरः .. 79 ..
5.143.m: Then, seeing Citrāṅgada, that gandharva of the celestials, / in such a state, filled with compassion, Śaṃkara spoke: 79

5.143.s:
mama saṃdarśanaṃ prāpya na mṛtyurjāyate kvacit ..
na vṛthā darśanaṃ caitattasmātprārthaya sādaram .. 6.144.80 ..
5.143.d:
मम संदर्शनं प्राप्य न मृत्युर्जायते क्वचित् ..
न वृथा दर्शनं चैतत्तस्मात्प्रार्थय सादरम् .. 6.144.80 ..
5.143.m: "Having attained the sight of me, death never comes to anyone anywhere; / and this darśana is not in vain, so make your petition with respect." 80

5.143.s:
.. citrāṃgada uvāca ... ..
vyādhinā'haṃ sunirviṇṇastena devātra cāgataḥ ..
yena vyādhikṣayo bhāvī dehanāśena śaṃkara .. 81 ..
5.143.d:
.. चित्रांगद उवाच ... ..
व्याधिनाऽहं सुनिर्विण्णस्तेन देवात्र चागतः ..
येन व्याधिक्षयो भावी देहनाशेन शंकर .. 81 ..
5.143.m: Citrāṅgada said: / "I am utterly despondent on account of this disease; therefore, O god, I came here, / O Śaṃkara, thinking the destruction of my disease would come through the destruction of my body. 81

5.143.s:
tasmātkuru kṣayaṃ vyādheryadi yacchasi me varam ..
khecaratvaṃ punardehi yena svargaṃ vrajāmyaham .. 82 ..
5.143.d:
तस्मात्कुरु क्षयं व्याधेर्यदि यच्छसि मे वरम् ..
खेचरत्वं पुनर्देहि येन स्वर्गं व्रजाम्यहम् .. 82 ..
5.143.m: Therefore bring about the destruction of my disease, if you will grant me a boon. / Give me back the ability to move through the sky, so that I may go to heaven." 82

5.143.s:
.. śrīśaṃkara uvāca .. ..
tvaṃ sthāpayātra malliṃgaṃ pīṭhe gandharvasattama ..
tataścārādhaya prītyā yāvadvarṣamupasthitam .. 83 ..
5.143.d:
.. श्रीशंकर उवाच .. ..
त्वं स्थापयात्र मल्लिंगं पीठे गन्धर्वसत्तम ..
ततश्चाराधय प्रीत्या यावद्वर्षमुपस्थितम् .. 83 ..
5.143.m: The venerable Śaṃkara said: / "Set up my liṅga here upon this seat, O best of gandharvas; / then worship it with love for the duration of a full year. 83

5.143.s:
yathāyathā supūjāṃ tvaṃ malliṃgasya kariṣyasi ..
dinedine tathā vyādhestava nāśo bhaviṣyati .. 84 ..
5.143.d:
यथायथा सुपूजां त्वं मल्लिंगस्य करिष्यसि ..
दिनेदिने तथा व्याधेस्तव नाशो भविष्यति .. 84 ..
5.143.m: In proportion as you perform excellent worship of my liṅga, / day by day the destruction of your disease will come to pass. 84

5.143.s:
tatastu khe gatiṃ prāpya punaḥ svargaṃ prayāsyasi ..
matprasādānna sandehaḥ satyametanmayoditam .. 85 ..
5.143.d:
ततस्तु खे गतिं प्राप्य पुनः स्वर्गं प्रयास्यसि ..
मत्प्रसादान्न सन्देहः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 85 ..
5.143.m: Then, attaining movement through the sky, you will return to heaven. / Through my grace there is no doubt; this is the truth spoken by me. 85

5.143.s:
eṣāpi kanyakā yasmātpraviṣṭā pīṭhamadhyataḥ ..
tasmātphalavatīnāma yoginī sambhaviṣyati .. 86 ..
5.143.d:
एषापि कन्यका यस्मात्प्रविष्टा पीठमध्यतः ..
तस्मात्फलवतीनाम योगिनी सम्भविष्यति .. 86 ..
5.143.m: And since this maiden has entered into the midst of the seat, / she will become a yoginī named Phalavatī. 86

5.143.s:
anenaiva tu rūpeṇa nagnatvena vyavasthitā ..
mukhyāmavāpsyate pūjāṃ vāṃchitaṃ ca pradāsyati ..
pūjakānāṃ sthitaṃ citte śatasaṃkhyaguṇaṃ tadā .. 87 ..
5.143.d:
अनेनैव तु रूपेण नग्नत्वेन व्यवस्थिता ..
मुख्यामवाप्स्यते पूजां वांछितं च प्रदास्यति ..
पूजकानां स्थितं चित्ते शतसंख्यगुणं तदा .. 87 ..
5.143.m: Standing in this very form, in a state of nakedness, / she will receive foremost worship and will grant what is desired / to the minds of her worshippers, magnified a hundredfold at that time. 87

5.143.s:
etāṃ saṃpūjayenmartyaḥ pīṭhametattataḥ param..
pūjayiṣyati tasyeṣṭā siddhirevaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 88 ..
5.143.d:
एतां संपूजयेन्मर्त्यः पीठमेतत्ततः परम्..
पूजयिष्यति तस्येष्टा सिद्धिरेवं भविष्यति .. 88 ..
5.143.m: A mortal should worship her, and after that, this seat; / he who worships will attain his desired perfection in this manner." 88

5.143.s:
evamuktvā tataḥ sā'tha harṣeṇa mahatā'nvitā ..
yoginīvṛṃdamadhyasthā nṛtyaṃ cakre tataḥ param .. 89
5.143.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततः साऽथ हर्षेण महताऽन्विता ..
योगिनीवृंदमध्यस्था नृत्यं चक्रे ततः परम् .. 89
5.143.m: Having said this, she, filled with immense joy, / standing in the midst of the assembly of yoginīs, then performed a dance. 89

5.143.s:
evaṃ babhūva sā tatra yoginī ca varāṃganā ..
tathā cakre paraṃ nṛtyaṃ yathā tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ .. 6.144.90 ..
5.143.d:
एवं बभूव सा तत्र योगिनी च वरांगना ..
तथा चक्रे परं नृत्यं यथा तुष्टो महेश्वरः .. 6.144.90 ..
5.143.m: Thus she, the fair woman, became a yoginī there. / She danced a supreme dance, such that Maheśvara was pleased. 90

5.143.s:
tataḥ provāca tāṃ hṛṣṭaḥ sarvayoginisaṃnidhau ..
anena tava nṛtyena gītena ca viśeṣataḥ .. 91 ..
5.143.d:
ततः प्रोवाच तां हृष्टः सर्वयोगिनिसंनिधौ ..
अनेन तव नृत्येन गीतेन च विशेषतः .. 91 ..
5.143.m: Delighted, he then said to her in the presence of all the yoginīs: / "By this dance of yours, and especially by your song, 91

5.143.s:
parituṣṭosmi te vatse tasmācchṛṇu vaco mama ..
niśīthe'dya dine prāpte yaste pūjāṃ kariṣyati .. 92 ..
5.143.d:
परितुष्टोस्मि ते वत्से तस्माच्छृणु वचो मम ..
निशीथेऽद्य दिने प्राप्ते यस्ते पूजां करिष्यति .. 92 ..
5.143.m: I am exceedingly pleased with you, child; therefore hear my words. / Whoever worships you when midnight arrives on this day, 92

5.143.s:
surā māṃsānnasatkārairmaṃtrairāgamasaṃbhavaiḥ ..
sa bhaviṣyati tatkālaṃ śāpānugrahaśaktimān .. 93 ..
5.143.d:
सुरा मांसान्नसत्कारैर्मंत्रैरागमसंभवैः ..
स भविष्यति तत्कालं शापानुग्रहशक्तिमान् .. 93 ..
5.143.m: with offerings of liquor and meat-food, with mantras originating from the Āgamas, / he will at that moment possess the power to curse and to bless. 93

5.143.s:
baṃdhanaṃ mohanaṃ cāpi śatroruccāṭanaṃ tathā ..
kariṣyati na sandeho vaśīkaraṇameva ca .. 94 ..
5.143.d:
बंधनं मोहनं चापि शत्रोरुच्चाटनं तथा ..
करिष्यति न सन्देहो वशीकरणमेव च .. 94 ..
5.143.m: Binding, bewitching, and also the expulsion of an enemy— / he will accomplish these without doubt, as well as subjugation. 94

5.143.s:
trikoṇaṃ kuṇḍamāsthāya diśāṃ pālānprapūjayet .
kṣetrapālaṃ ca sarvāstā devatā gamanodbhavāḥ .. 95 ..
5.143.d:
त्रिकोणं कुण्डमास्थाय दिशां पालान्प्रपूजयेत् .
क्षेत्रपालं च सर्वास्ता देवता गमनोद्भवाः .. 95 ..
5.143.m: Establishing a triangular fire-pit, he should worship the guardians of the directions, / and the Kṣetrapāla, and all those deities born of motion. 95

5.143.s:
tathā catvarapūjāṃ ca prakṛtvā vidhipūrvakam ..
paścāttvāṃ pūjayitvā ca homaṃ yaśca kariṣyati .. 96 ..
5.143.d:
तथा चत्वरपूजां च प्रकृत्वा विधिपूर्वकम् ..
पश्चात्त्वां पूजयित्वा च होमं यश्च करिष्यति .. 96 ..
5.143.m: And having thus worshipped the crossway according to the prescribed rules, / whoever afterwards worships you and performs a fire-offering— 96

5.143.s:
śatruvāmapadotthena spṛṣṭena rajasā'thavā ..
guggulena sahasrāṃtaṃ staṃbhanaṃ ca kariṣyati .. 97 ..
5.143.d:
शत्रुवामपदोत्थेन स्पृष्टेन रजसाऽथवा ..
गुग्गुलेन सहस्रांतं स्तंभनं च करिष्यति .. 97 ..
5.143.m: he will effect immobilization, using dust raised from the left foot of an enemy / or touched [by him], or using bdellium, up to a thousand times. 97

5.143.s:
yaśca śatruṃ hṛdi sthāpya śatrūdvartanasaṃbhavam ..
malaṃ dhātrīphalaiḥ sārdhaṃ mohanaṃ sa kariṣyati .. 98 ..
5.143.d:
यश्च शत्रुं हृदि स्थाप्य शत्रूद्वर्तनसंभवम् ..
मलं धात्रीफलैः सार्धं मोहनं स करिष्यति .. 98 ..
5.143.m: And whoever, placing the enemy in his heart, [offers] the dirt produced / by rubbing the enemy's body along with myrobalan fruits, will effect bewitchment. 98

5.143.s:
yaḥ śatroḥ snānajaṃ toyaṃ gṛhītvā cātha kardamam ..
śivanirmālyasaṃyuktaṃ juhvayiṣyati pāvake .. 99 ..
5.143.d:
यः शत्रोः स्नानजं तोयं गृहीत्वा चाथ कर्दमम् ..
शिवनिर्माल्यसंयुक्तं जुह्वयिष्यति पावके .. 99 ..
5.143.m: He who, having taken the bath-water and the mud of an enemy, / offers it in the fire together with the cast-off floral offerings of Śiva, 99

5.143.s:
tavāgre sa naro nūnaṃ śatrumuccāṭayiṣyati ..
eṣopi tava saṃgena tava citrāṃgadaḥ priyaḥ ..
saṃprāpsyati ca satpūjāmanuṣaṃgāttvadudbhavāt .. 6.144.100 ..
5.143.d:
तवाग्रे स नरो नूनं शत्रुमुच्चाटयिष्यति ..
एषोपि तव संगेन तव चित्रांगदः प्रियः ..
संप्राप्स्यति च सत्पूजामनुषंगात्त्वदुद्भवात् .. 6.144.100 ..
5.143.m: that man will surely expel his enemy in your presence. / This beloved Citrāṅgada of yours, too, through union with you, / will also attain true worship as an adjunct arising from you." 100

5.143.s:
.. phalavatyuvāca .. ..
yadi deva prasanno me tathānyamapi sadvaram..101..
5.143.d:
.. फलवत्युवाच .. ..
यदि देव प्रसन्नो मे तथान्यमपि सद्वरम्..101..
5.143.m: Phalavatī said: / "If the god is pleased with me, then grant another true boon as well, 101

5.143.s:
hṛdisthaṃ dehi me saukhyaṃ yena saṃjāyate'khilam ..
pitā mamaiṣa jābālirnirmukto vasanaiḥ sadā .. 102 ..
5.143.d:
हृदिस्थं देहि मे सौख्यं येन संजायतेऽखिलम् ..
पिता ममैष जाबालिर्निर्मुक्तो वसनैः सदा .. 102 ..
5.143.m: which rests in my heart, by which total happiness may arise for me: / May this father of mine, Jābāli, stripped of his garments forever, 102

5.143.s:
ahaṃ yathā tathātraiva saṃtiṣṭhatu divāniśam .
yena saṃtāpamāyāti paśyanmama virodhinīm .. 103 ..
5.143.d:
अहं यथा तथात्रैव संतिष्ठतु दिवानिशम् .
येन संतापमायाति पश्यन्मम विरोधिनीम् .. 103 ..
5.143.m: remain right here day and night just as I do, / so that he feels distress, seeing me engaged in sport 103

5.143.s:
krīḍāṃ brāhmaṇavaṃśasya madyamāṃsasamudbhavām ..
madyagandhaṃ samāghrāti māṃsaṃ paśyati saṃskṛtam ..
māṃ svacchaṃdaratāṃ nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ yāti dinedine .. 104 ..
5.143.d:
क्रीडां ब्राह्मणवंशस्य मद्यमांससमुद्भवाम् ..
मद्यगन्धं समाघ्राति मांसं पश्यति संस्कृतम् ..
मां स्वच्छंदरतां नित्यं दुःखं याति दिनेदिने .. 104 ..
5.143.m: contrary to the brahmin lineage, born of liquor and meat! / Let him smell the odour of liquor, let him behold cooked meat; / seeing me always enjoying self-will, let him suffer grief day by day." 104

5.143.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
evaṃ bhaviṣyati proktaṃ saṃjātaṃ cādhunā śubhe ..
ahaṃ yāsyāmi kailāsaṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭhātra yathoditā .. 105 ..
5.143.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
एवं भविष्यति प्रोक्तं संजातं चाधुना शुभे ..
अहं यास्यामि कैलासं त्वं तिष्ठात्र यथोदिता .. 105 ..
5.143.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "So shall it be, as was spoken, and so it has come to pass now, O auspicious one. / I shall go to Kailāsa; remain you here as spoken." 105

5.143.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ sa bhagavānproktvā gataścādarśanaṃ haraḥ ..
yoginyaścaiva tāḥ sarvāḥ svesve sthāne vyavasthitāḥ .. 106 ..
5.143.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं स भगवान्प्रोक्त्वा गतश्चादर्शनं हरः ..
योगिन्यश्चैव ताः सर्वाः स्वेस्वे स्थाने व्यवस्थिताः .. 106 ..
5.143.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Hara vanished from sight; / and all those yoginīs remained in their respective places. 106

5.143.s:
citrāṃgadopi tatraiva kṛtvā prāsādamuttamam ..
liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa devadevasya śūlinaḥ .. 107 ..
5.143.d:
चित्रांगदोपि तत्रैव कृत्वा प्रासादमुत्तमम् ..
लिंगं संस्थापयामास देवदेवस्य शूलिनः .. 107 ..
5.143.m: Citrāṅgada too, having built an excellent temple right there, / installed a liṅga of the god of gods, the trident-bearer. 107

5.143.s: tataścārādhayāmāsa divārātramataṃdritaḥ .. 108 ..
5.143.d: ततश्चाराधयामास दिवारात्रमतंद्रितः .. 108 ..
5.143.m: Then he worshipped it day and night, unwearied. 108

5.143.s:
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte vyādhimuktaḥ surūpadhṛk ..
vimānavaramārūḍho jagāma tridaśālayam ..
so'pi jābālināmātha vivastra samapadyata .. 109 ..
5.143.d:
ततः संवत्सरस्यांते व्याधिमुक्तः सुरूपधृक् ..
विमानवरमारूढो जगाम त्रिदशालयम् ..
सोऽपि जाबालिनामाथ विवस्त्र समपद्यत .. 109 ..
5.143.m: Then, at the end of a year, freed from disease and possessed of a handsome form, / mounted upon an excellent aerial chariot, he went to the abode of the thirty [gods]. / And he too, the one named Jābāli, became stripped of clothes. 109

5.143.s:
janahāsyakaro loke sthitastatraiva sarvadā ..
paśyamāno vikārāṃstānduḥkhitaḥ svasutodbhavān .. 6.144.110 ..
5.143.d:
जनहास्यकरो लोके स्थितस्तत्रैव सर्वदा ..
पश्यमानो विकारांस्तान्दुःखितः स्वसुतोद्भवान् .. 6.144.110 ..
5.143.m: Making himself a laughing-stock to the world, he remained right there always, / grieved as he witnessed those unnatural changes arising in his daughter. 110

5.143.s:
tataśca garhayāmāsa strīṇāṃ janma mahāmuniḥ ..
tasminpīṭhe samāsādya duḥkhena mahatā'nvitaḥ .. 111 ..
5.143.d:
ततश्च गर्हयामास स्त्रीणां जन्म महामुनिः ..
तस्मिन्पीठे समासाद्य दुःखेन महताऽन्वितः .. 111 ..
5.143.m: Then the great sage condemned the birth of women; / having arrived at that seat, filled with immense sorrow, [he said:] 111

5.143.s:
aho pāpātmanāṃ puṃsāṃ saṃbhaviṣyaṃti yoṣitaḥ ..
yāsāmīdṛksamācāro dvijavaṃśodbhavāsvapi .. 112 ..
5.143.d:
अहो पापात्मनां पुंसां संभविष्यंति योषितः ..
यासामीदृक्समाचारो द्विजवंशोद्भवास्वपि .. 112 ..
5.143.m: "Ah! Women will be born to sinful men— / women whose conduct is such, even among those born of a twice-born lineage! 112

5.143.s:
sakṛdeva mayā saṃgaḥ kṛto nāryā samanvitaḥ ..
ājanmamaraṇaṃ yāvatpāpaṃ prāptaṃ yathedṛśam .. 113 ..
5.143.d:
सकृदेव मया संगः कृतो नार्या समन्वितः ..
आजन्ममरणं यावत्पापं प्राप्तं यथेदृशम् .. 113 ..
5.143.m: Only once was union with a woman engaged in by me, / and such sin has been incurred, lasting from birth until death! 113

5.143.s:
ye punastāsu saṃsaktāḥ sadaiva puruṣādhamāḥ ..
kā teṣāṃ jāyate loke gatirvedmi na ciṃtayan .. 114 ..
5.143.d:
ये पुनस्तासु संसक्ताः सदैव पुरुषाधमाः ..
का तेषां जायते लोके गतिर्वेद्मि न चिंतयन् .. 114 ..
5.143.m: What destination will come to pass in this world for those vile men / who are constantly attached to them? Reflecting on this, I do not know." 114

5.143.s:
evaṃ tasya bruvāṇasya yoginyastāḥ krudhānvitāḥ ..
tamūcurbrāhmaṇaṃ tatra ghṛṇayā parivāritam.. 115 ..
5.143.d:
एवं तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य योगिन्यस्ताः क्रुधान्विताः ..
तमूचुर्ब्राह्मणं तत्र घृणया परिवारितम्.. 115 ..
5.143.m: While he was speaking thus, those yoginīs, filled with wrath, / spoke to that brahmin who was enveloped in disgust there. 115

5.143.s:
.. yoginya ūcuḥ ..
mā niṃdāṃ kuru mūḍhātmaṃstvaṃ strīṇāṃ yogamāśritaḥ ..
etaccarācaraṃ viśvaṃ strībhiḥ saṃdhāryate yataḥ .. 116 ..
5.143.d:
.. योगिन्य ऊचुः ..
मा निंदां कुरु मूढात्मंस्त्वं स्त्रीणां योगमाश्रितः ..
एतच्चराचरं विश्वं स्त्रीभिः संधार्यते यतः .. 116 ..
5.143.m: The yoginīs said: / "Do not censure women, O foolish-minded one, resorting to [mere] yoga; / for this universe of the moving and unmoving is sustained by women! 116

5.143.s:
yābhiḥ saṃjanitaḥ śeṣaḥ kūrmaśca tadanaṃtaram ..
yābhyāṃ saṃdhāryate pṛthvī yasyāṃ viśvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam .. 117 ..
5.143.d:
याभिः संजनितः शेषः कूर्मश्च तदनंतरम् ..
याभ्यां संधार्यते पृथ्वी यस्यां विश्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् .. 117 ..
5.143.m: By whom Śeṣa was brought forth, and the Tortoise immediately thereafter, / by which two the earth is sustained, upon which the universe is established. 117

5.143.s:
dhanyeyaṃ te sutā mūḍha yā prāptā yogamuttamam ..
prāptā ca paramaṃ sthānaṃ stokairevātra vāsaraiḥ .. 118...
5.143.d:
धन्येयं ते सुता मूढ या प्राप्ता योगमुत्तमम् ..
प्राप्ता च परमं स्थानं स्तोकैरेवात्र वासरैः .. 118...
5.143.m: Blessed is this daughter of yours, O fool, who has attained supreme yoga, / and has attained the supreme abode in just a few days here! 118

5.143.s:
tvaṃ punarmūrkhatāṃ prāptaśchāṃdasaṃ mārgamāsthitaḥ ..
avidyayā samāyuktaḥ saṃsāre'tra bhramiṣyasi .. 119 ..
5.143.d:
त्वं पुनर्मूर्खतां प्राप्तश्छांदसं मार्गमास्थितः ..
अविद्यया समायुक्तः संसारेऽत्र भ्रमिष्यसि .. 119 ..
5.143.m: You, on the other hand, have reached foolishness, adhering to the Vedic path; / conjoined with ignorance, you will wander in this cycle of existence!" 119

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca ..
striyo niṃdyatamāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāvasthāsu duḥkhadāḥ ..
ihaloke pare caiva tābhyaḥ saukhyaṃ na labhyate .. 6.144.120 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच ..
स्त्रियो निंद्यतमाः सर्वाः सर्वावस्थासु दुःखदाः ..
इहलोके परे चैव ताभ्यः सौख्यं न लभ्यते .. 6.144.120 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
All women are most contemptible; they bring sorrow in every circumstance.
Neither in this world nor in the next is happiness obtained from them.

5.143.s:
yadarthaṃ nihataḥ śumbho niśumbhaśca mahāsuraḥ ..
rāvaṇo daṇḍabhūpaśca tathānye'pi sahasraśaḥ .. 121 ..
5.143.d:
यदर्थं निहतः शुम्भो निशुम्भश्च महासुरः ..
रावणो दण्डभूपश्च तथान्येऽपि सहस्रशः .. 121 ..
5.143.m:
For whose sake Śumbha and the great asura Niśumbha were slain,
as well as Rāvaṇa, King Daṇḍa, and thousands of others too.

5.143.s:
prāpya tādṛgdvijaṃ kāṃtaṃ gautamaṃ strīsvabhāvataḥ ..
ahilyā śakramāsādya cakame śīlavarjitā .. 122 .. ..
5.143.d:
प्राप्य तादृग्द्विजं कांतं गौतमं स्त्रीस्वभावतः ..
अहिल्या शक्रमासाद्य चकमे शीलवर्जिता .. 122 .. ..
5.143.m:
Having obtained such a twice-born husband as Gautama, by the very nature of women,
Ahalyā approached Indra and lusted [for him], devoid of good conduct.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
yacca niṃdasi mūḍhātmansaṃti niṃdyāśca yoṣitaḥ ..
tadvadasva mayā sārdhaṃ yena tvāṃ bodhayāmyaham .. 123 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
यच्च निंदसि मूढात्मन्संति निंद्याश्च योषितः ..
तद्वदस्व मया सार्धं येन त्वां बोधयाम्यहम् .. 123 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
As to why you revile them, O foolish-minded one, saying that women are blameworthy,
speak about that with me, so that I may instruct you.

5.143.s:
na te'sti hṛdaye buddhirna lajjā na dayā mune ..
kimaṃtyajo'pi tatkarma kurute yattvayā kṛtam .. 124 ..
5.143.d:
न तेऽस्ति हृदये बुद्धिर्न लज्जा न दया मुने ..
किमंत्यजोऽपि तत्कर्म कुरुते यत्त्वया कृतम् .. 124 ..
5.143.m:
In your heart there is no intelligence, no shame, no compassion, O sage.
Does even an outcaste do such an act as you have done?

5.143.s:
ahaṃ tāvatprahāreṇa tvayā vyāpāditā'dhama ..
strīhatyodbhavapāpasya na cintā vidhṛtā hṛdi .. 125 ..
5.143.d:
अहं तावत्प्रहारेण त्वया व्यापादिताऽधम ..
स्त्रीहत्योद्भवपापस्य न चिन्ता विधृता हृदि .. 125 ..
5.143.m:
First of all, I was struck dead by you, O vile man!
You did not hold in your heart any concern for the sin arising from killing a woman,

5.143.s:
viśeṣeṇa sutāyāśca kopāviṣṭena cetasā ..
gacchaṃti pātakānyatra prāyaścittaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ .. .. 126 ..
5.143.d:
विशेषेण सुतायाश्च कोपाविष्टेन चेतसा ..
गच्छंति पातकान्यत्र प्रायश्चित्तैः पृथग्विधैः .. .. 126 ..
5.143.m:
especially of a daughter, with a mind possessed by wrath!
Sins here are removed by various kinds of expiations;

5.143.s:
strīvadhotthaṃ punaryāti yadi tattvaṃ prakīrtaya ..
etanme na ca duḥkhaṃ syādyaddhatāsmi dvijādhama .. 127 ..
5.143.d:
स्त्रीवधोत्थं पुनर्याति यदि तत्त्वं प्रकीर्तय ..
एतन्मे न च दुःखं स्याद्यद्धतास्मि द्विजाधम .. 127 ..
5.143.m:
if that which arises from killing a woman goes away, proclaim that truth!
And this would not be my grief, that I was killed, O lowest of the twice-born;

5.143.s:
yacchaptā nagnasadbhāvaṃ nītā tatpātakaṃ ca te ..
kalpāṃte'pi sudurbuddhe na saṃyāsyati kutracit .. 128 ..
5.143.d:
यच्छप्ता नग्नसद्भावं नीता तत्पातकं च ते ..
कल्पांतेऽपि सुदुर्बुद्धे न संयास्यति कुत्रचित् .. 128 ..
5.143.m:
the sin of yours—that I was cursed and brought to a state of nakedness—
shall not pass away anywhere, O severely evil-minded one, even at the end of an aeon!

5.143.s:
tasmādbhuṃkṣva suduḥkhārtaḥ sthito'traiva mayā saha ..
na bhūyo niṃdasi prāyo na ca vyāpādayiṣyasi .. 129 ..
5.143.d:
तस्माद्भुंक्ष्व सुदुःखार्तः स्थितोऽत्रैव मया सह ..
न भूयो निंदसि प्रायो न च व्यापादयिष्यसि .. 129 ..
5.143.m:
Therefore, afflicted by great sorrow, remain right here and suffer along with me;
you will not likely revile again, nor will you kill [anyone].

5.143.s:
aniṃdyā yoṣitaḥ sarvā naitā duṣyaṃti karhicit ..
māsimāsi rajo hyāsāṃ duṣkṛtānyapakarṣati .. 6.144.130 ..
5.143.d:
अनिंद्या योषितः सर्वा नैता दुष्यंति कर्हिचित् ..
मासिमासि रजो ह्यासां दुष्कृतान्यपकर्षति .. 6.144.130 ..
5.143.m:
All women are blameless; they are never corrupted.
For month by month their menses removes their misdeeds.

5.143.s:
.. muni ruvāca .. ..
striyaḥ pāpasamācārā naitāḥ śudhyaṃti karhicit ..
parakāṃte ratiryāsāmaṃtyajatvaṃ prayacchati .. 131 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनि रुवाच .. ..
स्त्रियः पापसमाचारा नैताः शुध्यंति कर्हिचित् ..
परकांते रतिर्यासामंत्यजत्वं प्रयच्छति .. 131 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Women are of sinful conduct; they are never purified.
Their desire is for another's lover, which reduces them to the status of an outcaste.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
mā maivaṃ vada mūḍhātmannamedhyā iti yoṣitaḥ ..
atra ślokaḥ purā gīto manunā taṃ nibodha me .. 132 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
मा मैवं वद मूढात्मन्नमेध्या इति योषितः ..
अत्र श्लोकः पुरा गीतो मनुना तं निबोध मे .. 132 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Do not, do not speak thus, O foolish-minded one, that women are impure!
A verse was sung anciently by Manu in this regard; learn it from me:

5.143.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ pādato medhyā gāvo medhyāstu pṛṣṭhataḥ ..
ajāśvā mukhato medhyā striyo medhyāśca sarvataḥ .. 133 ..
5.143.d:
ब्राह्मणाः पादतो मेध्या गावो मेध्यास्तु पृष्ठतः ..
अजाश्वा मुखतो मेध्या स्त्रियो मेध्याश्च सर्वतः .. 133 ..
5.143.m:
"Brahmins are pure from the feet; cows are pure from the back;
goats and horses are pure from the mouth; and women are pure all over."

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
brāhmaṇāḥ sarvato medhyā gāvo medhyāśca sarvataḥ ..
ajāśvā mukhato medhyā na medhyāśca striyaḥ kvacit .. 134 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
