ब्राह्मणाः सर्वतो मेध्या गावो मेध्याश्च सर्वतः ..
अजाश्वा मुखतो मेध्या न मेध्याश्च स्त्रियः क्वचित् .. 134 ..

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
tasya ciṃtāmaṇirhaste tasya kalpadrumo gṛhe ..
kuberaḥ kiṃkarastasya yasya syātkāminī gṛhe .. 135 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
तस्य चिंतामणिर्हस्ते तस्य कल्पद्रुमो गृहे ..
कुबेरः किंकरस्तस्य यस्य स्यात्कामिनी गृहे .. 135 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
In his hand is the wish-fulfilling jewel, in his house is the wishing tree,
and Kubera is his servant, in whose house there is a beloved woman.

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
tasyāpado'khilā duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tasyākhilaṃ gṛhe ..
narakaḥ sarvatastasya yasya syātkāminīgṛhe .. 136 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
तस्यापदोऽखिला दुःखं दुःखं तस्याखिलं गृहे ..
नरकः सर्वतस्तस्य यस्य स्यात्कामिनीगृहे .. 136 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
All calamities are his, sorrow—all sorrow is in his house,
and hell is on all sides of him, in whose house there is a beloved woman.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
yāni kānyatra saukhyāni bhogasthānāni yāni ca ..
dharmārthakāmajātāni tāni strībhyo bhavaṃti hi .. 137 ..
.. muniruvāca .. ..
yāni kāni suduḥkhāni kleśāni yāni dehinām ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
यानि कान्यत्र सौख्यानि भोगस्थानानि यानि च ..
धर्मार्थकामजातानि तानि स्त्रीभ्यो भवंति हि .. 137 ..
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
यानि कानि सुदुःखानि क्लेशानि यानि देहिनाम् ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Whatever joys and whatever spheres of enjoyment there are in this world,
arising from righteousness, wealth, and pleasure—they indeed come from women.
The sage said:
Whatever great sorrows and whatever afflictions there are for embodied beings,

5.143.s: yāni kaṣṭānyaniṣṭāni strībhyastāni bhavaṃti ca .. 138 ..
5.143.d: यानि कष्टान्यनिष्टानि स्त्रीभ्यस्तानि भवंति च .. 138 ..
5.143.m: and whatever difficulties and undesirable things—they too come from women.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
dharmārthakāmamokṣānstrī caturo'pi catasṛbhiḥ ..
vahnipradakṣiṇābhistānvivāhe'pi pradarśayet .. 139 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षान्स्त्री चतुरोऽपि चतसृभिः ..
वह्निप्रदक्षिणाभिस्तान्विवाहेऽपि प्रदर्शयेत् .. 139 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Even in marriage, a woman demonstrates all four aims of life—
righteousness, wealth, pleasure, and liberation—through the four circumambulations of the fire.

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
saṃsārabhramaṇaṃ nārī prathame'pi samāgame ..
vahnipradakṣiṇānyāyavyājenaiva pradarśayet .. 6.144.140 .. ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
संसारभ्रमणं नारी प्रथमेऽपि समागमे ..
वह्निप्रदक्षिणान्यायव्याजेनैव प्रदर्शयेत् .. 6.144.140 .. ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Even at the very first meeting, a woman demonstrates
wandering in worldly existence, under the pretext of the custom of circumambulating the fire.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
ke nāma na virajyaṃti jñānāḍhyā api mānavāḥ ..
karṇāṃtalagnanetrāṃtāṃ dṛṣṭvā pīna payodharām .. 141 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
के नाम न विरज्यंति ज्ञानाढ्या अपि मानवाः ..
कर्णांतलग्ननेत्रांतां दृष्ट्वा पीन पयोधराम् .. 141 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Who indeed does not become impassioned, even men rich in knowledge,
upon seeing a woman with corner-of-the-eye glances reaching to her ears, and full breasts?

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
ke nāma na vinaśyaṃti mūḍhajñānā nitaṃbinīm ..
ramyabuddhyopasarpaṃti ye jvālāḥ śalabhā iva .. 142 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
के नाम न विनश्यंति मूढज्ञाना नितंबिनीम् ..
रम्यबुद्ध्योपसर्पंति ये ज्वालाः शलभा इव .. 142 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Who indeed does not perish, whose intellect is bewildered by a shapely woman?
Those who approach her with thoughts of pleasure are like moths to flames.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
nirmukhau ca kaṭhorau ca proddhatau ca manoramau ..
strīstanau sevate dhanyo madhumāṃse viśeṣataḥ ..143..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
निर्मुखौ च कठोरौ च प्रोद्धतौ च मनोरमौ ..
स्त्रीस्तनौ सेवते धन्यो मधुमांसे विशेषतः ..143..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Featureless, firm, erect, and delightful—
a fortunate man enjoys a woman's breasts, especially during spring and amid wine and meat.

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
ābhoginau maṃḍalinau tatkṣaṇānmuktakaṃcukau..
varamāśīviṣau spṛṣṭau na tu patnyāḥ payodharau .. 144 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
आभोगिनौ मंडलिनौ तत्क्षणान्मुक्तकंचुकौ..
वरमाशीविषौ स्पृष्टौ न तु पत्न्याः पयोधरौ .. 144 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Curved, round, and suddenly shedding their bodice—
it is better to touch two venomous serpents than a wife's breasts!

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
na cāsāṃ racanāmātraṃ kevalaṃ ramyamaṃgibhiḥ .
pariṣvaṃgo'pi rāmāṇāṃ saukhyāya pulakāya ca .. 145 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
न चासां रचनामात्रं केवलं रम्यमंगिभिः .
परिष्वंगोऽपि रामाणां सौख्याय पुलकाय च .. 145 ..

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
na cāsāṃ racanāmātraṃ ramyaṃ syātpāpadaṃ dṛśaḥ ..
vapuḥ spṛṣṭaṃ vināśāya strīṇāṃ pretya narakāya ca .. 146 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
न चासां रचनामात्रं रम्यं स्यात्पापदं दृशः ..
वपुः स्पृष्टं विनाशाय स्त्रीणां प्रेत्य नरकाय च .. 146 ..

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
ko nāma na sukhī loke ko nāma sukṛtī na ca ..
spṛhaṇīyatamaḥ ko na strījano yasya rajyate .. 147 .. ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
को नाम न सुखी लोके को नाम सुकृती न च ..
स्पृहणीयतमः को न स्त्रीजनो यस्य रज्यते .. 147 .. ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Who indeed in this world is not happy, who indeed is not meritorious,
and who is not most enviable, to whom women are devoted?

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
ko na muktiṃ vrajettatra ko na śasyataro bhavet ..
ko na syātkṣemasaṃyuktaḥ strījane yo na rajyate .. 148 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
को न मुक्तिं व्रजेत्तत्र को न शस्यतरो भवेत् ..
को न स्यात्क्षेमसंयुक्तः स्त्रीजने यो न रज्यते .. 148 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Who there would not attain liberation, who would not become more praiseworthy,
and who would not be endowed with well-being, who does not become attached to women?

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
saṃsārāṃtaḥ prasuptasya kīṭasyāpi prarocate ..
strīśarīraṃ narasyātra kiṃ punarna vivekinaḥ .. 149 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
संसारांतः प्रसुप्तस्य कीटस्यापि प्ररोचते ..
स्त्रीशरीरं नरस्यात्र किं पुनर्न विवेकिनः .. 149 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Even to a worm asleep inside the world of transmigration, a woman's body
is pleasing; why would it not be so in this world to a man endowed with discernment?

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
amedhyajā tasya yathā tathā tadrocanaṃ kṛmeḥ ..
tathā saṃsārasūtasya strīśarīraṃ ca kāminaḥ .. 6.144.150 ..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
अमेध्यजा तस्य यथा तथा तद्रोचनं कृमेः ..
तथा संसारसूतस्य स्त्रीशरीरं च कामिनः .. 6.144.150 ..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Just as that which arises from impurity is pleasing to a worm,
so a woman's body, born of transmigration, is pleasing to a lustful man.

5.143.s:
.. kanyovāca .. ..
saukhyasthānaṃ nṛṇāṃ kiṃcidvedhasā 'nyadapaśyatā ..
śāśvataṃ ciṃtayitvātha strīratnamidamāhṛtam .. 151 ..
5.143.d:
.. कन्योवाच .. ..
सौख्यस्थानं नृणां किंचिद्वेधसा ऽन्यदपश्यता ..
शाश्वतं चिंतयित्वाथ स्त्रीरत्नमिदमाहृतम् .. 151 ..
5.143.m:
The maiden said:
Seeing no other place of happiness for mortals,
the Creator, after contemplating what is eternal, brought forth this jewel of a woman.

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
baṃdhanaṃ jagataḥ kiṃcidvedhasā'nyadapaśyatā ..
strīrūpeṇa tataḥ kopi pāśo'yaṃ strīmayaḥ kṛtaḥ .. 152 .
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
बंधनं जगतः किंचिद्वेधसाऽन्यदपश्यता ..
स्त्रीरूपेण ततः कोपि पाशोऽयं स्त्रीमयः कृतः .. 152 .
5.143.m:
The sage said:
Seeing no other bondage for the world,
the Creator then fashioned in the form of a woman this snare consisting of woman.

5.143.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ sa muniśārdūlastayātīva samāgame ..
niruttarīkṛto yāvattataḥ prāha nijāṃ sutām .. 153 ..
5.143.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं स मुनिशार्दूलस्तयातीव समागमे ..
निरुत्तरीकृतो यावत्ततः प्राह निजां सुताम् .. 153 ..
5.143.m:
Sūta said:
When that tiger among sages had thus been rendered completely answerless
by her in their encounter, he then addressed his own daughter:

5.143.s:
.. muniruvāca .. ..
tvayā saha na saṃvādo mayā kāryo'dhunā kvacit ..
yā tvaṃ bālāpi māmevaṃ niṣedhayasi sarvataḥ..154..
5.143.d:
.. मुनिरुवाच .. ..
त्वया सह न संवादो मया कार्योऽधुना क्वचित् ..
या त्वं बालापि मामेवं निषेधयसि सर्वतः..154..
5.143.m:
The sage said:
I must no longer engage in debate with you anywhere,
since you, though a girl, thus refute me at every turn.

5.143.s:
tasmāddhanyataraṃ manye ahamātmānamadya vai ..
yasya me tvaṃ sutā īdṛgīdṛkchāstravicakṣaṇā .. 155 ..
5.143.d:
तस्माद्धन्यतरं मन्ये अहमात्मानमद्य वै ..
यस्य मे त्वं सुता ईदृगीदृक्छास्त्रविचक्षणा .. 155 ..
5.143.m:
Therefore, I consider myself indeed most fortunate today,
in that I have such a daughter, so skilled in the scriptures.

5.143.s:
tasmānna me mahābhāge kopaḥ svalpo'pi vidyate ..
tasmādyathecchayā krīḍāṃ kuru yoginimadhyagā .. 156 ..
5.143.d:
तस्मान्न मे महाभागे कोपः स्वल्पोऽपि विद्यते ..
तस्माद्यथेच्छया क्रीडां कुरु योगिनिमध्यगा .. 156 ..
5.143.m:
Therefore, O highly fortunate one, not even the slightest anger remains in me;
hence, sport as you wish, standing in the midst of the yoginīs.

5.143.s:
tataḥ sā lajjitā dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ snehavatsalam .
praṇipatya punaḥprāha yoginīmadhyasaṃsthitā .. 157 ..
5.143.d:
ततः सा लज्जिता दृष्ट्वा पितरं स्नेहवत्सलम् .
प्रणिपत्य पुनःप्राह योगिनीमध्यसंस्थिता .. 157 ..
5.143.m:
Then she, feeling bashful upon seeing her father full of affectionate tenderness,
bowed down and spoke again, standing in the midst of the yoginīs:

5.143.s:
ajñānādyadi vā jñānāttvaṃ niṣiddho mayā prabho ..
kṣaṃtavyaṃ sakalaṃ me'dya vālikāyā viśeṣataḥ .. 158..
5.143.d:
अज्ञानाद्यदि वा ज्ञानात्त्वं निषिद्धो मया प्रभो ..
क्षंतव्यं सकलं मेऽद्य वालिकाया विशेषतः .. 158..
5.143.m: "Whether out of ignorance or indeed with knowledge, I was forbidden by you, O lord; / everything should be forgiven me today, especially as I am a young girl.

5.143.s:
atra pīṭhe samāgatya prathamaṃ te dvijottamāḥ ..
pūjāṃ sarve kariṣyaṃti mānavā bhaktitatparāḥ ..
paścācca sarvapīṭhasya yāsyaṃti ca parāṃ gatim.. 159 ..
5.143.d:
अत्र पीठे समागत्य प्रथमं ते द्विजोत्तमाः ..
पूजां सर्वे करिष्यंति मानवा भक्तितत्पराः ..
पश्चाच्च सर्वपीठस्य यास्यंति च परां गतिम्.. 159 ..
5.143.m: Coming to this sacred seat, O foremost of the twice-born, all those men devoted to bhakti / will first worship you, / and afterwards the whole sacred seat, and they will attain the highest goal."

5.143.s:
evaṃ sā tatra saṃjātā jābālimunisaṃbhavā ..
jābāliśca muniśreṣṭhastathā citrāṃgadeśvaraḥ .. 6.144.160 ..
5.143.d:
एवं सा तत्र संजाता जाबालिमुनिसंभवा ..
जाबालिश्च मुनिश्रेष्ठस्तथा चित्रांगदेश्वरः .. 6.144.160 ..
5.143.m: Thus she came into being there, born from the sage Jābāli, / and Jābāli is the best of sages, and likewise Citrāṅgadeśvara.

5.143.s:
trayāṇāmapi yasteṣāṃ pūjāṃ martyaḥ samācaret..
divasedivase tatra sa siddhiṃ samavāpnuyāt .. 161 ..
5.143.d:
त्रयाणामपि यस्तेषां पूजां मर्त्यः समाचरेत्..
दिवसेदिवसे तत्र स सिद्धिं समवाप्नुयात् .. 161 ..
5.143.m: Whatever mortal performs the worship of these three / day after day there, he shall attain perfection.

5.143.s:
nāsādhyaṃ vidyate kiṃcittāvadatra dharātale ..
pūjyate bhūmipālādyairbhogāndivyāṃstathā labhet .. 162 ..
5.143.d:
नासाध्यं विद्यते किंचित्तावदत्र धरातले ..
पूज्यते भूमिपालाद्यैर्भोगान्दिव्यांस्तथा लभेत् .. 162 ..
5.143.m: Nothing at all is impossible for him on the surface of the earth; / he is worshipped by kings and the like, and he obtains celestial enjoyments.

5.143.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena sa muniḥ sā ca kanyakā ..
pūjanīyā viśeṣeṇa sa devo'tha maheśvaraḥ .. 163 ..
5.143.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन स मुनिः सा च कन्यका ..
पूजनीया विशेषेण स देवोऽथ महेश्वरः .. 163 ..
5.143.m: Therefore, by every effort, that sage and that maiden / should be worshipped especially, and so should the god, the great lord.

5.143.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātamākhyānaṃ sarvakāmadam ..
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva ihaloke paratra ca .. 164
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye citrāṃgadeśvaraphalavatījābālyākhyānavarṇanaṃnāma catuścatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 144 .. .. cha ..
5.143.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातमाख्यानं सर्वकामदम् ..
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव इहलोके परत्र च .. 164
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये चित्रांगदेश्वरफलवतीजाबाल्याख्यानवर्णनंनाम चतुश्चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः .. 144 .. .. छ ..
5.143.m:
All this narrative, granting all desires, has been told to you / for those who recite and hear it, both in this world and in the next.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fourth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Story of Citrāṅgadeśvara, Phalavatī, and Jābāli', in the māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara sacred field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.144.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yattvayā kathitaṃ sūta na mṛtā sā kumārikā ..
hatā raudraprahāraiśca kautukaṃ tanmahattaram .. 1 ..
5.144.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यत्त्वया कथितं सूत न मृता सा कुमारिका ..
हता रौद्रप्रहारैश्च कौतुकं तन्महत्तरम् .. 1 ..
5.144.m: The seers said: / That which was told by you, O Sūta, that the young girl did not die / when struck with violent blows, is a very great wonder;

5.144.s:
yato bhūyaḥ prasaṃjātā yoginī haratuṣṭidā ..
yattvārthaṃ sarvamācakṣva kāraṇaṃ ca tadadbhutam .. 2 ..
5.144.d:
यतो भूयः प्रसंजाता योगिनी हरतुष्टिदा ..
यत्त्वार्थं सर्वमाचक्ष्व कारणं च तदद्भुतम् .. 2 ..
5.144.m: since she was born again as a yoginī who brings delight to Hara. / Explain to us the entire matter and that wondrous cause.

5.144.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sā praviṣṭā samaṃ tena supuṇyamamareśvaram ..
māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ na mṛtyuryatra vidyate .. 3 ..'
5.144.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
सा प्रविष्टा समं तेन सुपुण्यममरेश्वरम् ..
माघकृष्णचतुर्दश्यां न मृत्युर्यत्र विद्यते .. 3 ..'
5.144.m: Sūta said: / Together with him, she entered the holy Amareśvara / on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, where death does not exist,

5.144.s:
api caivāyuṣaḥ śeṣe kimutākālato dvijāḥ..
tena no nidhanaṃ prāptā hatāpi sudṛḍhaṃ tadā .. 4..
5.144.d:
अपि चैवायुषः शेषे किमुताकालतो द्विजाः..
तेन नो निधनं प्राप्ता हतापि सुदृढं तदा .. 4..
5.144.m: even at the end of life's span, O twice-born ones, to say nothing of an untimely [death]! / Therefore she did not meet death, even though she was struck very hard at that time.

5.144.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
amareśvara ityukto yo devo hyamaratvadaḥ ..
kena saṃsthāpito hyatra kiṃprabhāvaśca kīrtaya .. 5 ..
5.144.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः ..
अमरेश्वर इत्युक्तो यो देवो ह्यमरत्वदः ..
केन संस्थापितो ह्यत्र किंप्रभावश्च कीर्तय .. 5 ..
5.144.m: The seers said: / The god called Amareśvara, who bestows immortality— / by whom was he established here, and what is his power? Proclaim this!

5.144.s:
..sūta uvāca .. ..
aditiśca ditiścaiva prajāpatisute śubhe..
kṛte purātirūpāḍhye kaśyapena mahātmanā..6..
5.144.d:
..सूत उवाच .. ..
अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव प्रजापतिसुते शुभे..
कृते पुरातिरूपाढ्ये कश्यपेन महात्मना..6..
5.144.m: Sūta said: / Aditi and Diti, the auspicious daughters of the Prajāpati, / were married formerly by the high-souled Kaśyapa, being richly endowed with great beauty.

5.144.s:
adityāṃ vibudhā jātā diteścaiva tu daityapāḥ...
teṣāṃ sāpatnyabhāvena mahadvairamupasthitam..
atha daityaiḥ surā dhvastāḥ kṛtāścānye parāṅmukhāḥ ..
anye tu bhayasaṃtrastā diśo jagmuḥ kṣatāṃgakāḥ ..8..
5.144.d:
अदित्यां विबुधा जाता दितेश्चैव तु दैत्यपाः...
तेषां सापत्न्यभावेन महद्वैरमुपस्थितम्..
अथ दैत्यैः सुरा ध्वस्ताः कृताश्चान्ये पराङ्मुखाः ..
अन्ये तु भयसंत्रस्ता दिशो जग्मुः क्षतांगकाः ..8..
5.144.m: From Aditi the gods were born, and from Diti the rulers of the Daityas. / Great enmity arose among them through rivalry between co-wives. / Then the gods were destroyed by the Daityas, and others were put to flight; / others, terrified by fear, fled in all directions with wounded limbs.

5.144.s:
tato duḥkhasamāyuktā devamātātra saṃsthitā ..
tapaścakre divānaktaṃ śivadhyānaparāyaṇā .. 9 ..
5.144.d:
ततो दुःखसमायुक्ता देवमातात्र संस्थिता ..
तपश्चक्रे दिवानक्तं शिवध्यानपरायणा .. 9 ..
5.144.m: Then, filled with grief, the mother of the gods remained here / and performed austerity day and night, intent on meditating upon Śiva.

5.144.s:
evaṃ tasyāstapaḥsthāyā gate yugacatuṣṭaye ..
nirbhidya dharaṇīpṛṣṭhaṃ śivaliṃgaṃ samutthitam .. 6.145.10 ..
5.144.d:
एवं तस्यास्तपःस्थाया गते युगचतुष्टये ..
निर्भिद्य धरणीपृष्ठं शिवलिंगं समुत्थितम् .. 6.145.10 ..
5.144.m: As she was thus engaged in austerity and four yugas passed, / a Śivaliṅga arose, bursting through the surface of the earth.

5.144.s:
tatastasmai kṛtānandā stutvā stotraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ ..
aṣṭāṃgapraṇipātena namaścakre samāhitā .. 11 ..
5.144.d:
ततस्तस्मै कृतानन्दा स्तुत्वा स्तोत्रैः पृथग्विधैः ..
अष्टांगप्रणिपातेन नमश्चक्रे समाहिता .. 11 ..
5.144.m: Then, filled with joy, having praised it with various hymns, / she bowed down in focused devotion with an eightfold prostration.

5.144.s:
etasminnaṃtare vāṇī saṃjātā gaganāṃgaṇe ..
śarīrarahitā divyā meghagambhīraniḥsvanā .. 12 ..
5.144.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे वाणी संजाता गगनांगणे ..
शरीररहिता दिव्या मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वना .. 12 ..
5.144.m: In the meantime, a divine incorporeal voice arose / in the courtyard of the sky, with a sound deep as a thundercloud:

5.144.s:
varaṃ prārthaya kalyāṇi yaste hṛdi vyavasthitaḥ ..
prasanno'haṃ pradāsyāmi tavādya śaśiśekharaḥ .. 13 ..
5.144.d:
वरं प्रार्थय कल्याणि यस्ते हृदि व्यवस्थितः ..
प्रसन्नोऽहं प्रदास्यामि तवाद्य शशिशेखरः .. 13 ..
5.144.m: "Request a boon, O auspicious lady, that which is in your heart; / pleased am I, the moon-crested lord, and I will grant it to you today."

5.144.s:
.. aditiruvāca .. ..
mama putrāḥ suraśreṣṭha hanyante yudhi dānavaiḥ..
tatkuruṣva gatāyāsānavadhyānraṇamūrdhani .. 14 ..
5.144.d:
.. अदितिरुवाच .. ..
मम पुत्राः सुरश्रेष्ठ हन्यन्ते युधि दानवैः..
तत्कुरुष्व गतायासानवध्यान्रणमूर्धनि .. 14 ..
5.144.m: Aditi said: / "O best of gods, my sons are being slain in battle by the Dānavas; / therefore, make them free of fatigue and unslayable at the forefront of battle!"

5.144.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
etalliṃgaṃ madīyaṃ ye spṛṣṭvā yāsyaṃti saṃyuge ..
avadhyāste bhaviṣyanti yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ śubhe .. 15 ..
5.144.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
एतल्लिंगं मदीयं ये स्पृष्ट्वा यास्यंति संयुगे ..
अवध्यास्ते भविष्यन्ति यावत्संवत्सरं शुभे .. 15 ..
5.144.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "Those who touch this liṅga of mine and go into battle / will be unslayable for a whole year, O auspicious lady.

5.144.s:
anyo'pi mānavo yo'tra caturdaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ ..
māghamāsasya kṛṣṇāyāṃ prakariṣyati jāgaram .. ..16..
5.144.d:
अन्योऽपि मानवो योऽत्र चतुर्दश्यां समाहितः ..
माघमासस्य कृष्णायां प्रकरिष्यति जागरम् .. ..16..
5.144.m: Any other man, too, who keeps vigil here with a concentrated mind / on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Māgha,

5.144.s:
so'pi saṃvatsaraṃ yāvadbhaviṣyati nirāmayaḥ ..
api mṛtyudine prāpte yo'sminnāyatane śubhe .. 17 ..
5.144.d:
सोऽपि संवत्सरं यावद्भविष्यति निरामयः ..
अपि मृत्युदिने प्राप्ते योऽस्मिन्नायतने शुभे .. 17 ..
5.144.m: he too shall be free from illness for a year. / Even if the day of death has arrived, whoever comes to this auspicious sanctuary

5.144.s:
āgamiṣyati taṃ mṛtyurdūrātparihariṣyati ..
evamuktvātha sā vāṇī virarāma tataḥ param .. 18 ..
5.144.d:
आगमिष्यति तं मृत्युर्दूरात्परिहरिष्यति ..
एवमुक्त्वाथ सा वाणी विरराम ततः परम् .. 18 ..
5.144.m: will be avoided from afar by Death." / Having spoken thus, that voice fell silent thereafter.

5.144.s:
aditiścāpi santuṣṭā hataśeṣānsutāṃstataḥ ..
samānīyātha talliṃgaṃ teṣāmeva nyadarśayat ..
kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ māhātmyaṃ yadvaroditam .. 19 ..
5.144.d:
अदितिश्चापि सन्तुष्टा हतशेषान्सुतांस्ततः ..
समानीयाथ तल्लिंगं तेषामेव न्यदर्शयत् ..
कथयामास तत्सर्वं माहात्म्यं यद्वरोदितम् .. 19 ..
5.144.m: Aditi, too, highly pleased, brought her surviving sons / and showed them that very liṅga; / she told them all that māhātmya as it had been declared in the boon.

5.144.s:
tataste vibudhāḥ sarve talliṃgaṃ praṇipatya ca ..
pratijagmustuṣṭiyuktāḥ śastrāṇyādāya tānprati.. 6.145.20 ..
5.144.d:
ततस्ते विबुधाः सर्वे तल्लिंगं प्रणिपत्य च ..
प्रतिजग्मुस्तुष्टियुक्ताः शस्त्राण्यादाय तान्प्रति.. 6.145.20 ..
5.144.m: Then all those gods bowed down to that liṅga / and, filled with satisfaction, taking up their weapons, set out against them,

5.144.s:
yatra te dānavā hṛṣṭāḥ sthitāḥ śakrapade śubhe ..
svargabhogasamāyuktā nandanāṃtarvyavasthitāḥ .. 21 ..
5.144.d:
यत्र ते दानवा हृष्टाः स्थिताः शक्रपदे शुभे ..
स्वर्गभोगसमायुक्ता नन्दनांतर्व्यवस्थिताः .. 21 ..
5.144.m: where those Dānavas, rejoiced, were situated in the auspicious position of Śakra, / endowed with the pleasures of heaven, staying within the Nandana garden.

5.144.s:
atha te dānavā dṛṣṭvā saṃprāptāṃstridivaukasaḥ ..
sahasā saṃgarārthāya nānāśastradharānbahūn .. 22 ..
5.144.d:
अथ ते दानवा दृष्ट्वा संप्राप्तांस्त्रिदिवौकसः ..
सहसा संगरार्थाय नानाशस्त्रधरान्बहून् .. 22 ..
5.144.m: Then those Dānavas, seeing that the many gods had arrived / all at once for battle, bearing various weapons,

5.144.s:
rathavaryānsamāruhya dhṛtaśastrāstravarmaṇaḥ ..
yuddhārthaṃ sammukhā jagmurgarjamānā ghanā iva .. 23 ..
5.144.d:
रथवर्यान्समारुह्य धृतशस्त्रास्त्रवर्मणः ..
युद्धार्थं सम्मुखा जग्मुर्गर्जमाना घना इव .. 23 ..
5.144.m: mounted excellent chariots, holding weapons, missiles, and armour, / and marched forward for battle, roaring like clouds.

5.144.s:
tataḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha ..
roṣapreritacittānāṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam .. 24 ..
5.144.d:
ततः समभवद्युद्धं देवानां दानवैः सह ..
रोषप्रेरितचित्तानां मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम् .. 24 ..
5.144.m: Then a battle took place between the gods and the Dānavas, / whose minds were driven by rage, refusing to turn back except by death.

5.144.s:
tataste vibudhāḥ sarve haralabdhavarāstadā ..
jaghnurdaityānasaṃkhyātācchitaiḥ śastrairanekadhā .. 25 ..
5.144.d:
ततस्ते विबुधाः सर्वे हरलब्धवरास्तदा ..
जघ्नुर्दैत्यानसंख्याताच्छितैः शस्त्रैरनेकधा .. 25 ..
5.144.m: Then all those gods, who had received boons from Hara at that time, / slew innumerable Daityas in many ways with sharp weapons.

5.144.s:
hataśeṣāśca ye teṣāṃ te tyaktvā tridaśālayam ..
palāyanakṛtotsāhāḥ praviṣṭā makarālayam .. 26 ..
5.144.d:
हतशेषाश्च ये तेषां ते त्यक्त्वा त्रिदशालयम् ..
पलायनकृतोत्साहाः प्रविष्टा मकरालयम् .. 26 ..
5.144.m: Those among them who were left unslain abandoned the abode of the thirty [gods] / and, eager to flee, entered the abode of the sea-monsters.

5.144.s:
tataḥ śakraḥ samāpede svarājyaṃ dānavairhṛtam ..
yadāsītpūrvakāle tatsamagraṃ hatakaṇṭakam .. 27 ..
5.144.d:
ततः शक्रः समापेदे स्वराज्यं दानवैर्हृतम् ..
यदासीत्पूर्वकाले तत्समग्रं हतकण्टकम् .. 27 ..
5.144.m: Then Śakra regained his kingdom that had been seized by the Dānavas, / exactly as it had been in earlier times, completely freed of thorns.

5.144.s:
tataste dānavāḥ śeṣā jñātvā talliṃgasaṃbhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ vṛṣanāthasya kṣetrasyāsyodbhavasya ca .. 28 ..
5.144.d:
ततस्ते दानवाः शेषा ज्ञात्वा तल्लिंगसंभवम् ..
माहात्म्यं वृषनाथस्य क्षेत्रस्यास्योद्भवस्य च .. 28 ..
5.144.m: Then the remaining Dānavas learned of the power of that liṅga, / the māhātmya of the Lord of the Bull, and the origin of this sacred field,

5.144.s:
śukreṇa kathitaṃ sarvaṃ māghakṛṣṇe niśāgame ..
caturdaśyāṃ śucirbhūtvā yastalliṃgaṃ prapūjayet ..
kālāghrāto'pi na prāṇaiḥ sa pumāṃstyajyate kvacit ..29..
5.144.d:
शुक्रेण कथितं सर्वं माघकृष्णे निशागमे ..
चतुर्दश्यां शुचिर्भूत्वा यस्तल्लिंगं प्रपूजयेत् ..
कालाघ्रातोऽपि न प्राणैः स पुमांस्त्यज्यते क्वचित् ..29..
5.144.m: as all was told by Śukra: "Whoever, becoming pure, worships that liṅga / on the arrival of night on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of Māgha, / though sniffed by Death, he is never abandoned by his life-breaths.

5.144.s:
tasmādyūyaṃ samāsādya talliṃgaṃ taddine niśi ..
pūjayadhvaṃ mahābhāgā yena syurmṛtyuvarjitāḥ .. 6.145.30 ..
5.144.d:
तस्माद्यूयं समासाद्य तल्लिंगं तद्दिने निशि ..
पूजयध्वं महाभागा येन स्युर्मृत्युवर्जिताः .. 6.145.30 ..
5.144.m: Therefore, O fortunate ones, approach that liṅga on that day at night / and worship it, so that you may be free from death

5.144.s:
yāvatsaṃvatsarasyātaṃ satyametanmayoditam ..
yathā te devasaṃghāśca tatprabhāvādasaṃśayam .. 31 ..
5.144.d:
यावत्संवत्सरस्यातं सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् ..
यथा ते देवसंघाश्च तत्प्रभावादसंशयम् .. 31 ..
5.144.m: until the end of the year; this has been truthfully declared by me, / just as the hosts of gods [became], through its power, without a doubt."

5.144.s:
atha taṃ dānavendrāṇāṃ maṃtraṃ jñātvā sureśvaraḥ ..
nāradādbrāhmaṇaḥ putrādbhayatrastamanāstataḥ .. 32 ..
5.144.d:
अथ तं दानवेन्द्राणां मंत्रं ज्ञात्वा सुरेश्वरः ..
नारदाद्ब्राह्मणः पुत्राद्भयत्रस्तमनास्ततः .. 32 ..
5.144.m: Then the lord of the gods, learning of that counsel of the lords of the Dānavas / from Nārada, the son of Brahmā, became terrified in mind;

5.144.s:
maṃtraṃ cakre samaṃ devaistatra devasya rakṣaṇe ..
yathā syādudyamaḥ samyaktasminnahani sarvadā .. 33 ..
5.144.d:
मंत्रं चक्रे समं देवैस्तत्र देवस्य रक्षणे ..
यथा स्यादुद्यमः सम्यक्तस्मिन्नहनि सर्वदा .. 33 ..
5.144.m: he held counsel together with the gods for guarding the god there, / so that there would be a proper effort on that day always.

5.144.s:
koṭayastu trayastriṃśaddevānāṃ sāyudhāstataḥ ..
rakṣārthaṃ tasya liṃgasya tasminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ ..
māghakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ susaṃnaddhāḥ prahāriṇaḥ .. 34 ..
5.144.d:
कोटयस्तु त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवानां सायुधास्ततः ..
रक्षार्थं तस्य लिंगस्य तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे व्यवस्थिताः ..
माघकृष्णचतुर्दश्यां सुसंनद्धाः प्रहारिणः .. 34 ..
5.144.m:
Then thirty-three crores of gods, bearing weapons,
stationed themselves in that sacred field to protect that liṅga,
fully armed and ready to strike on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha.

5.144.s:
atha te dānavā dṛṣṭvā tāndevāṃstatra saṃsthitān ..
bhayasaṃtrastamanaso dudruvuḥ sarvato diśam .. 35 ..
5.144.d:
अथ ते दानवा दृष्ट्वा तान्देवांस्तत्र संस्थितान् ..
भयसंत्रस्तमनसो दुद्रुवुः सर्वतो दिशम् .. 35 ..
5.144.m:
Then those Dānavas, seeing those gods stationed there,
their minds terrified with fear, fled in all directions.

5.144.s:
atha prabhāte vimale prodgate ravimaṇḍale ..
bhūya eva surāḥ sarve maṃtraṃ cakruḥ parasparam .. 36 ..
5.144.d:
अथ प्रभाते विमले प्रोद्गते रविमण्डले ..
भूय एव सुराः सर्वे मंत्रं चक्रुः परस्परम् .. 36 ..
5.144.m:
Then, when the morning was bright and the sun's orb had risen,
all the gods took counsel among themselves once more:

5.144.s:
yadyetatkṣetramutsṛjya gamiṣyāmaḥ surālayam ..
liṃgametatsamabhyetya pūjayiṣyaṃti dānavāḥ .. 37 ..
5.144.d:
यद्येतत्क्षेत्रमुत्सृज्य गमिष्यामः सुरालयम् ..
लिंगमेतत्समभ्येत्य पूजयिष्यंति दानवाः .. 37 ..
5.144.m:
"If we abandon this sacred field and go to the abode of the gods,
the Dānavas will approach this liṅga and worship it.

5.144.s:
tato'vadhyā bhaviṣyaṃti te'pi sarve yathā vayam ..
tasmādatraiva tiṣṭhāmastrayastriṃśatpranāyakāḥ .. 38 ..
5.144.d:
ततोऽवध्या भविष्यंति तेऽपि सर्वे यथा वयम् ..
तस्मादत्रैव तिष्ठामस्त्रयस्त्रिंशत्प्रनायकाः .. 38 ..
5.144.m:
Then they too will all become invulnerable, just as we are.
Therefore, let us, the thirty-three leaders,

5.144.s:
koṭīnāmeva sarveṣāṃ śeṣā gacchantu tatra ca ..
sahasrākṣeṇa saṃyuktāḥ svarge svapararakṣakāḥ .. 39 ..
tato'ṣṭau vasavastatra dvādaśārkāstathaiva ca ..
ekādaśāpare rudrā nāsatyau dvau ca sundarau ..6.145.4...
5.144.d:
कोटीनामेव सर्वेषां शेषा गच्छन्तु तत्र च ..
सहस्राक्षेण संयुक्ताः स्वर्गे स्वपररक्षकाः .. 39 ..
ततोऽष्टौ वसवस्तत्र द्वादशार्कास्तथैव च ..
एकादशापरे रुद्रा नासत्यौ द्वौ च सुन्दरौ ..6.145.4...
5.144.m:
of all the crores, remain right here; and let the rest go there
with the thousand-eyed [Indra] to heaven, guarding their own and others."
Then the eight Vasus [stayed] there, and likewise the twelve Ādityas,
eleven other Rudras, and the two handsome Nāsatyas;

5.144.s:
ete talliṃgarakṣārthaṃ tasminkṣetre vyavasthitāḥ..
śeṣāḥ śakrasamāyuktāḥ prajagmustridaśālayam .. 41 ..
5.144.d:
एते तल्लिंगरक्षार्थं तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे व्यवस्थिताः..
शेषाः शक्रसमायुक्ताः प्रजग्मुस्त्रिदशालयम् .. 41 ..
5.144.m:
these remained stationed in that sacred field to protect that liṅga;
the rest, accompanied by Śakra, went to the abode of the thirty [gods].

5.144.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ prabhāvaṃ liṃgaṃ tu devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
bhavadbhiḥ paripṛṣṭaṃ yadadityā sthāpitaṃ purā .. 42 ..
5.144.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं प्रभावं लिंगं तु देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
भवद्भिः परिपृष्टं यददित्या स्थापितं पुरा .. 42 ..
5.144.m:
Sūta said:
Such was the power of the liṅga of the god of gods, the trident-bearer,
about which you asked, which had formerly been installed by Aditi.

5.144.s:
yasmānna vidyate mṛtyustena dṛṣṭena dehinām ..
amarākhyaṃ tato liṃgaṃ vikhyātaṃ bhuvanatraye .. 43 ..
5.144.d:
यस्मान्न विद्यते मृत्युस्तेन दृष्टेन देहिनाम् ..
अमराख्यं ततो लिंगं विख्यातं भुवनत्रये .. 43 ..
5.144.m:
Because mortals see no death upon beholding it,
the liṅga is therefore renowned in the three worlds by the name 'Amara'.

5.144.s:
yasmindeśe'pi sā kanyā hatā tena dvijanmanā ..
jābālinā sukruddhena tasya devasya maṃdire .. .. 44 ..
5.144.d:
यस्मिन्देशेऽपि सा कन्या हता तेन द्विजन्मना ..
जाबालिना सुक्रुद्धेन तस्य देवस्य मंदिरे .. .. 44 ..
5.144.m:
In which place, also, that maiden was struck down by that twice-born,
by the furiously enraged Jābāli, in the temple of that god;

5.144.s:
āsīttatra dine kṛṣṇā māghamāsa caturdaśī ..
tena no nidhanaṃ prāptā suhatā'pi tapasvinī .. 45 ..
5.144.d:
आसीत्तत्र दिने कृष्णा माघमास चतुर्दशी ..
तेन नो निधनं प्राप्ता सुहताऽपि तपस्विनी .. 45 ..
5.144.m:
on that day was the fourteenth [day] of the dark fortnight of the month of Māgha;
therefore she did not meet destruction, though struck down severely, ascetic as she was.

5.144.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ tasya liṃgasya sambhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam .. 46 ..
5.144.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं तस्य लिंगस्य सम्भवम् ..
माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 46 ..
5.144.m:
All this origin of that liṅga has been told to you,
its māhātmya that destroys all sins, O best of brahmins.

5.144.s:
yaścaitatpaṭhate bhaktyā tasya liṃgasya saṃnidhau ..
apamṛtyubhayaṃ tasya kathaṃcinnaiva jāyate .. 47 ..
5.144.d:
यश्चैतत्पठते भक्त्या तस्य लिंगस्य संनिधौ ..
अपमृत्युभयं तस्य कथंचिन्नैव जायते .. 47 ..
5.144.m:
And whoever recites this with devotion in the presence of that liṅga,
no fear of untimely death arises for him in any way.

5.144.s:
tasyāgre'sti śubhaṃ kuṇḍaṃ pūritaṃ svacchavāriṇā .
adityā nirmitaṃ devyā snānārthaṃ cātmanaḥ kṛte .. 48 ..
5.144.d:
तस्याग्रेऽस्ति शुभं कुण्डं पूरितं स्वच्छवारिणा .
अदित्या निर्मितं देव्या स्नानार्थं चात्मनः कृते .. 48 ..
5.144.m:
In front of it there is an auspicious pool filled with pure water,
fashioned by goddess Aditi for her own ritual bath.

5.144.s:
snānaṃ kṛtvā narastasminyastalliṃgaṃ prapaśyati ..
karoti jāgaraṃ rātrau tasminneva dinedine ..
so'dyāpi vatsaraṃ yāvannāpamṛtyumavāpnuyāt .. 49 ..
5.144.d:
स्नानं कृत्वा नरस्तस्मिन्यस्तल्लिंगं प्रपश्यति ..
करोति जागरं रात्रौ तस्मिन्नेव दिनेदिने ..
सोऽद्यापि वत्सरं यावन्नापमृत्युमवाप्नुयात् .. 49 ..
5.144.m:
A person who, having bathed in it, beholds that liṅga,
and keeps vigil at night, on that very day year after year,
even today will not meet with an untimely death for a year.

5.144.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'marakeśvarakṣetramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma paṃcacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ .. 145 .. .. cha ..
5.144.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽमरकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम पंचचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः .. 145 .. .. छ ..
5.144.m: Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Amarakeśvara' in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.145.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
ādityānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vasurudrādikāśvinām ..
pratyekaśaḥ samācakṣva nāmāni tvaṃ mahāmate .. 1 ..
5.145.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
आदित्यानां च सर्वेषां वसुरुद्रादिकाश्विनाम् ..
प्रत्येकशः समाचक्ष्व नामानि त्वं महामते .. 1 ..
5.145.m:
The seers said:
Of all the Ādityas, and of the Vasus, Rudras, and the Aśvins,
declare the names individually, O high-minded one!

5.145.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
vṛṣadhvajaśca śarvaśca mṛgavyādhastṛtīyakaḥ ..
ajaikapādahirbudhnyaḥ pinākī ṣaṣṭha eva hi .. 2 ..
5.145.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
वृषध्वजश्च शर्वश्च मृगव्याधस्तृतीयकः ..
अजैकपादहिर्बुध्न्यः पिनाकी षष्ठ एव हि .. 2 ..

5.145.s:
dahanaśceśvaraścaiva kapālī navamastathā ..
vṛṣākapistu daśamo rudrastryaṃbaka eva ca .. 3 ..
5.145.d:
दहनश्चेश्वरश्चैव कपाली नवमस्तथा ..
वृषाकपिस्तु दशमो रुद्रस्त्र्यंबक एव च .. 3 ..
5.145.m:
Dahana, Īśvara, and Kapālin as the ninth,
Vṛṣākapi as the tenth, and Rudra Tryambaka.

5.145.s:
dhuro dhruvaśca somaśca makhaścaivānilo'nalaḥ ..
pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ .. 4 ..
5.145.d:
धुरो ध्रुवश्च सोमश्च मखश्चैवानिलोऽनलः ..
प्रत्यूषश्च प्रभासश्च वसवोऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः .. 4 ..
5.145.m:
Dhura, Dhruva, Soma, Makha, Anila, Anala,
Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa: these are proclaimed the eight Vasus.

5.145.s:
varuṇaśca tathā sūryo bhānuḥ khyātaśca tāpanaḥ ..
iṃdraścaivāryamā caiva dhātā caiva bhagastathā .. 5 ..
5.145.d:
वरुणश्च तथा सूर्यो भानुः ख्यातश्च तापनः ..
इंद्रश्चैवार्यमा चैव धाता चैव भगस्तथा .. 5 ..
5.145.m:
Varuṇa, Sūrya, Bhānu, and the renowned Tāpana,
Indra, Aryaman, Dhātṛ, and Bhaga;

5.145.s:
gabhastirdharmarājaśca svarṇaretā divākaraḥ ..
mitraśca vāsudevaśca dvādaśaite ca bhāskarāḥ .. 6 ..
5.145.d:
गभस्तिर्धर्मराजश्च स्वर्णरेता दिवाकरः ..
मित्रश्च वासुदेवश्च द्वादशैते च भास्कराः .. 6 ..
5.145.m:
Gabhasti, Dharmarāja, Svarṇaretas, Divākara,
Mitra, and Vāsudeva: these are the twelve suns.

5.145.s:
nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca khyātāvetau tathāśvinau ..
devavaidyau mahābhāgau tvāṣṭrīgarbhasamudbhavau .. 7 ..
5.145.d:
नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च ख्यातावेतौ तथाश्विनौ ..
देववैद्यौ महाभागौ त्वाष्ट्रीगर्भसमुद्भवौ .. 7 ..
5.145.m:
Nāsatya and Dasra: these two are renowned as the Aśvins,
the physicians of the gods, highly fortunate, born of the womb of Tvaṣṭṛ's daughter.

5.145.s:
trayastriṃśatsamākhyātā ete ye suranāyakāḥ ..
kṣetre'traivāsthitā nityaṃ dānavānāṃ vadhāya ca ..8..
5.145.d:
त्रयस्त्रिंशत्समाख्याता एते ये सुरनायकाः ..
क्षेत्रेऽत्रैवास्थिता नित्यं दानवानां वधाय च ..8..
5.145.m:
These thirty-three leaders of the gods who have been declared,
stay always in this very sacred field for the destruction of the Dānavas.

5.145.s:
yastānsaṃpūjayedbhaktyā puruṣaḥ saṃyateṃdriyaḥ..
yathoktadivase prāpte nāpamṛtyuḥ prajāyate .. 9 ..
5.145.d:
यस्तान्संपूजयेद्भक्त्या पुरुषः संयतेंद्रियः..
यथोक्तदिवसे प्राप्ते नापमृत्युः प्रजायते .. 9 ..
5.145.m:
The man of restrained senses who worships them with devotion
when the prescribed day arrives, no untimely death occurs for him.

5.145.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ rudrāḥ pūjyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ ..
tasminkṣetre viśeṣeṇa vāṃchadbhiḥ paramaṃ padam ..6.146.10...
5.145.d:
अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां रुद्राः पूज्या विचक्षणैः ..
तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे विशेषेण वांछद्भिः परमं पदम् ..6.146.10...
5.145.m:
The Rudras are to be worshipped on the eighth and the fourteenth [lunar days] by the wise,
especially in that sacred field, by those who desire the supreme state.

5.145.s:
daśamyāṃ vasavaḥ pūjyāstathāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
svargaṃ samīhamānaiśca vilāsairvividhaistathā .. 11 ..
5.145.d:
दशम्यां वसवः पूज्यास्तथाष्टम्यां विशेषतः ..
स्वर्गं समीहमानैश्च विलासैर्विविधैस्तथा .. 11 ..
5.145.m:
The Vasus are to be worshipped on the tenth, and especially on the eighth,
by those who desire heaven along with its various delights.

5.145.s:
saptamyāmatha ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca pūjanīyā divākarāḥ ..
ye vāṃchanti narāḥ sattvaṃ paripaṃthivivarjitam .. 12 ..
5.145.d:
सप्तम्यामथ षष्ठ्यां च पूजनीया दिवाकराः ..
ये वांछन्ति नराः सत्त्वं परिपंथिविवर्जितम् .. 12 ..
5.145.m:
On the seventh and the sixth, the suns are to be worshipped
by men who desire strength free from adversaries.

5.145.s:
devavaidyau tathā pūjyau dvādaśyāṃ vyādhisaṃkṣayam ..
ye vāṃchanti sadā martyā nīrujā sambhavaṃti te .. 13 ..
5.145.d:
देववैद्यौ तथा पूज्यौ द्वादश्यां व्याधिसंक्षयम् ..
ये वांछन्ति सदा मर्त्या नीरुजा सम्भवंति ते .. 13 ..
5.145.m:
Likewise, the two physicians of the gods are to be worshipped on the twelfth by mortals
who always desire the destruction of disease; they become free from sickness.

5.145.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'mareśvarakuṇḍamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 146 .. ..
5.145.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽमरेश्वरकुण्डमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षट्चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः .. 146 .. ..
5.145.m: Thus ends the one hundred and forty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Pool of Amareśvara' in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.146.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti devaḥ putraprado nṛṇām ..
vaṭikeśvara nāmā ca sarvapāpaharo haraḥ .. 1 ..
5.146.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्योऽपि च तत्रास्ति देवः पुत्रप्रदो नृणाम् ..
वटिकेश्वर नामा च सर्वपापहरो हरः .. 1 ..

5.146.s:
yasminvaṭikayā pūrvaṃ tapastaptaṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
prāptā putraṃ śuke yāte vanaṃ vyāsātkapiṃjalam .. 2 ..
5.146.d:
यस्मिन्वटिकया पूर्वं तपस्तप्तं द्विजोत्तमाः ..
प्राप्ता पुत्रं शुके याते वनं व्यासात्कपिंजलम् .. 2 ..
5.146.m:
where formerly, O best of the twice-born, austerity was performed by Vaṭikā,
who obtained a son, Kapiñjala, from Vyāsa when Śuka had departed to the forest.

5.146.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kasyāsau vaṭikā tatra kathaṃ taptavatī tapaḥ ..
kasmādgṛhaṃ parityaktvā śuko'pi vanamāśritaḥ .. 3 ..
5.146.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कस्यासौ वटिका तत्र कथं तप्तवती तपः ..
कस्माद्गृहं परित्यक्त्वा शुकोऽपि वनमाश्रितः .. 3 ..
5.146.m:
The seers said:
Whose [daughter or wife] was that Vaṭikā there? How did she perform austerity?
For what reason did Śuka also abandon home and resort to the forest?

5.146.s: kathaṃ kapijalaṃ putraṃ vyāsāllebhe śucismitā .. 4 ..
5.146.d: कथं कपिजलं पुत्रं व्यासाल्लेभे शुचिस्मिता .. 4 ..
5.146.m: How did that fair-smiling woman obtain a son, Kapiñjala, from Vyāsa?

5.146.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
āsīdvyāsasya vipreṃdrāḥ kalatrārthaṃ matiḥ kvacit .
niṣkāmasya praśāṃtasya sarvajñasya mahātmanaḥ .. 5 ..
5.146.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
आसीद्व्यासस्य विप्रेंद्राः कलत्रार्थं मतिः क्वचित् .
निष्कामस्य प्रशांतस्य सर्वज्ञस्य महात्मनः .. 5 ..
5.146.m:
Sūta said:
O foremost among brahmins, at one time Vyāsa, who was desireless, tranquil,
omniscient, and great-souled, turned his mind toward [taking] a wife.

5.146.s:
tataḥ kṣayamanuprāpte vaṃśe kurusamudbhave ..
vicitravīryamāsādya pārthivaṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 6 ..
5.146.d:
ततः क्षयमनुप्राप्ते वंशे कुरुसमुद्भवे ..
विचित्रवीर्यमासाद्य पार्थिवं द्विजसत्तमाः .. 6 ..
5.146.m:
Then, when the lineage sprung from Kuru had met destruction,
after King Vicitravīrya [perished], O best of the twice-born,

5.146.s:
satyavatyāḥ samādeśāttasya kṣetre tataḥ param ..
sa putrāñjanayāmāsa trīñchūrānpāṃḍupūrvakān .. 7 ..
5.146.d:
सत्यवत्याः समादेशात्तस्य क्षेत्रे ततः परम् ..
स पुत्राञ्जनयामास त्रीञ्छूरान्पांडुपूर्वकान् .. 7 ..
5.146.m:
at the command of Satyavatī, in his field [his wives], thereafter
he fathered three heroic sons, beginning with Pāṇḍu,

5.146.s:
vānaprasthavrate tiṣṭhansakṛnmaithunatatparaḥ ..
kṣetrajaistanayairvaṃśe kurostasmādupasthite .. 8 ..
5.146.d:
वानप्रस्थव्रते तिष्ठन्सकृन्मैथुनतत्परः ..
क्षेत्रजैस्तनयैर्वंशे कुरोस्तस्मादुपस्थिते .. 8 ..
5.146.m:
abiding by the vow of a forest-dweller, engaged in union only once.
When the lineage of Kuru was thus sustained by those sons born of the field,

5.146.s:
tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa bhāryāmadya karomyaham ..
gārhasthyenātha dharmeṇa sādhayāmi śubhāṃ gatim .. 9 ..
5.146.d:
ततः स चिंतयामास भार्यामद्य करोम्यहम् ..
गार्हस्थ्येनाथ धर्मेण साधयामि शुभां गतिम् .. 9 ..
5.146.m:
he then thought: "Now I shall take a wife,
and through the duty of a householder I shall attain an auspicious destination."

5.146.s:
tataḥ sa prārthayāmāsa jābāliṃ tu sutāṃ śubhām ..
vaṭikākhyāṃ śubhāṃ kanyāṃ sa dadau tasya satvaram .. 6.147.10 ..
5.146.d:
ततः स प्रार्थयामास जाबालिं तु सुतां शुभाम् ..
वटिकाख्यां शुभां कन्यां स ददौ तस्य सत्वरम् .. 6.147.10 ..
5.146.m: Then he asked Jābāli for his auspicious daughter. / He quickly gave him the auspicious maiden named Vaṭikā.

5.146.s:
tatastayā sametaḥ sa vanavāsaṃ samāśritaḥ ..
vānaprasthāśrame tiṣṭhankṛtamaithunatatparaḥ .. 11 ..
5.146.d:
ततस्तया समेतः स वनवासं समाश्रितः ..
वानप्रस्थाश्रमे तिष्ठन्कृतमैथुनतत्परः .. 11 ..
5.146.m: Then, together with her, he took up residence in the forest, / staying in the hermitage of the forest-dweller stage of life, devoted to performing intercourse.

5.146.s:
tato garbhavatī jajñe piṃjalā tasya pārśvataḥ ..
ṛtau mohanamāsādya vyāsātsatyavatīsutāt .. 12 ..
5.146.d:
ततो गर्भवती जज्ञे पिंजला तस्य पार्श्वतः ..
ऋतौ मोहनमासाद्य व्यासात्सत्यवतीसुतात् .. 12 ..
5.146.m: Then the tawny-eyed woman became pregnant by him; / having experienced pleasure in her fertile period from Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī,

5.146.s:
atha yāti parāṃ vṛddhiṃ sa garbhastatra saṃsthitaḥ ..
udare vyāsabhāryāyāḥ śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī .. 13 ..
5.146.d:
अथ याति परां वृद्धिं स गर्भस्तत्र संस्थितः ..
उदरे व्यासभार्यायाः शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी .. 13 ..
5.146.m: that embryo staying there attained great growth / in the womb of Vyāsa's wife, like the moon in the bright fortnight.

5.146.s:
evaṃ saṃgacchatastasya vṛddhiṃ garbhasya nityaśaḥ ..
dvādaśābdā atikrāṃtā na janma samavāpnuyāt .. 14 ..
5.146.d:
एवं संगच्छतस्तस्य वृद्धिं गर्भस्य नित्यशः ..
द्वादशाब्दा अतिक्रांता न जन्म समवाप्नुयात् .. 14 ..
5.146.m: As that embryo continuously grew in this manner, / twelve years passed, yet it did not take birth.

5.146.s:
yatkiṃcicchṛṇute tatra garbhastho'hi vacaḥ kvacit ..
tatsarvaṃ hṛdisaṃsthaṃ ca cakre prajñāsamanvitaḥ .. 15 ..
5.146.d:
यत्किंचिच्छृणुते तत्र गर्भस्थोऽहि वचः क्वचित् ..
तत्सर्वं हृदिसंस्थं च चक्रे प्रज्ञासमन्वितः .. 15 ..
5.146.m: Whatever words he heard anywhere while remaining in the womb, / he, endowed with great intellect, kept them all in his heart.

5.146.s:
vedāḥ sāṃgāḥ samādhītā garbhavāse'pi tena ca ..
smṛtayaśca purāṇāni mokṣaśāstrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 16 ..
5.146.d:
वेदाः सांगाः समाधीता गर्भवासेऽपि तेन च ..
स्मृतयश्च पुराणानि मोक्षशास्त्राणि कृत्स्नशः .. 16 ..
5.146.m: Even while residing in the womb, he fully studied / the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs, the Smṛtis, the Purāṇas, and the treatises on liberation.

5.146.s:
tatrastho'pi divā naktaṃ svādhyāyaṃ prakaroti saḥ ..
na ca janmotthajāṃ buddhiṃ kathaṃcidapi ciṃtayet .. 17 ..
5.146.d:
तत्रस्थोऽपि दिवा नक्तं स्वाध्यायं प्रकरोति सः ..
न च जन्मोत्थजां बुद्धिं कथंचिदपि चिंतयेत् .. 17 ..
5.146.m: Staying there, he recited the sacred texts day and night, / and he did not even think of taking birth in any way.

5.146.s:
sāpi mātā parā pīḍāṃ nityaṃ yāti tathākulā ..
yathāyathā sa saṃyāti vṛddhiṃ jaṭharamāśritaḥ .. 18 ..
5.146.d:
सापि माता परा पीडां नित्यं याति तथाकुला ..
यथायथा स संयाति वृद्धिं जठरमाश्रितः .. 18 ..
5.146.m: The mother too suffered great torment constantly, thus distressed, / as he grew larger and larger within her womb.

5.146.s:
tataśca vismayāviṣṭo vyāso vacanamabravīt ..
kastvaṃ madgṛhiṇīkukṣau praviṣṭo garbharūpadhṛk .. 19 ..
na niṣkrāmasi kasmāttvaṃ kimetāṃ sūdayiṣyasi .. ..
.. garbha uvāca .. ..
rākṣaso'haṃ piśācohaṃ devo'haṃ mānuṣastathā ..6.147.2...
5.146.d:
ततश्च विस्मयाविष्टो व्यासो वचनमब्रवीत् ..
कस्त्वं मद्गृहिणीकुक्षौ प्रविष्टो गर्भरूपधृक् .. 19 ..
न निष्क्रामसि कस्मात्त्वं किमेतां सूदयिष्यसि .. ..
.. गर्भ उवाच .. ..
राक्षसोऽहं पिशाचोहं देवोऽहं मानुषस्तथा ..6.147.2...
5.146.m:
Then Vyāsa, filled with wonder, spoke [these] words: / "Who are you, who have entered my wife's womb in the form of an embryo?
Why do you not come out? Will you kill her?" / The embryo said: / "I have been a rākṣasa, a piśāca, a deva, and likewise a human.

5.146.s:
gajo'haṃ turagaścāpi kukkuṭaśchāga eva ca ..
yonīnāṃ caturāśītisahasrāṇi ca saṃkhyayā .. 21 ..
5.146.d:
गजोऽहं तुरगश्चापि कुक्कुटश्छाग एव च ..
योनीनां चतुराशीतिसहस्राणि च संख्यया .. 21 ..
5.146.m: I have been an elephant, a horse, a cock, and a goat. / Numbering eighty-four hundred thousand wombs,

5.146.s:
bhrāṃto'haṃ teṣu sarveṣu tatko'haṃ prabravīmi kim ..
sāṃprataṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā jaṭharaṃ samupāśritaḥ .. 22 ..
5.146.d:
भ्रांतोऽहं तेषु सर्वेषु तत्कोऽहं प्रब्रवीमि किम् ..
सांप्रतं मानुषो भूत्वा जठरं समुपाश्रितः .. 22 ..
5.146.m: I have wandered through them all; so who am I? What can I say? / Now, having become human, I have entered a womb.

5.146.s:
mānuṣaṃ na kariṣyāmi niṣkāmaṃ ca kathaṃcana ..
nirviṣṭo bhramamāṇo'tra saṃsāre dāruṇe tataḥ ..23 ..
5.146.d:
मानुषं न करिष्यामि निष्कामं च कथंचन ..
निर्विष्टो भ्रममाणोऽत्र संसारे दारुणे ततः ..23 ..
5.146.m: I will not make human life desireless in any way; / therefore, weary from wandering in this terrible cycle of worldly existence,

5.146.s:
atrastho bhavanirmukto yogābhyāsarataḥ sadā ..
mokṣamārgaṃ prayāsyāmi sthānānmokṣamasaṃśayam.. 24 ..
5.146.d:
अत्रस्थो भवनिर्मुक्तो योगाभ्यासरतः सदा ..
मोक्षमार्गं प्रयास्यामि स्थानान्मोक्षमसंशयम्.. 24 ..
5.146.m: freed from worldly existence while staying here, always devoted to the practice of yoga, / I shall surely attain the path of liberation from this place—liberation without doubt.

5.146.s:
tāvajjñānaṃ ca vairāgyaṃ pūrvajātismṛtiryathā ..
yāvadgarbhasthito jantuḥ sarvo'pi dvijasattama .. 25 ..
5.146.d:
तावज्ज्ञानं च वैराग्यं पूर्वजातिस्मृतिर्यथा ..
यावद्गर्भस्थितो जन्तुः सर्वोऽपि द्विजसत्तम .. 25 ..
5.146.m: Knowledge, dispassion, and recollection of previous births / remain only as long as every living creature stays in the womb, O best of brahmins.

5.146.s:
yadā garbhādviniṣkrāṃtaḥ spṛśyate viṣṇumāyayā ..
tadā nāśaṃ vrajatyāśu satyametadasaṃśayam .. 26 ..
5.146.d:
यदा गर्भाद्विनिष्क्रांतः स्पृश्यते विष्णुमायया ..
तदा नाशं व्रजत्याशु सत्यमेतदसंशयम् .. 26 ..
5.146.m: When one emerges from the womb, touched by Viṣṇu's māyā, / then it immediately perishes; this is true without doubt.

5.146.s:
tasmānnāhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha niṣkramiṣye kathaṃcana ..
garbhādasmātprayāsyāmi sthānānmokṣamasaṃśayam .. 27 ..
5.146.d:
तस्मान्नाहं द्विजश्रेष्ठ निष्क्रमिष्ये कथंचन ..
गर्भादस्मात्प्रयास्यामि स्थानान्मोक्षमसंशयम् .. 27 ..
5.146.m: Therefore, O best of brahmins, I will not come out by any means; / from this womb, from this place, I will surely attain liberation without doubt."

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
na bhaviṣyati te māyā vaiṣṇavī sā kathaṃcana ..
sughorānnarakādasmānniṣkramasva vigarhitāt .. 28 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
न भविष्यति ते माया वैष्णवी सा कथंचन ..
सुघोरान्नरकादस्मान्निष्क्रमस्व विगर्हितात् .. 28 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / "That Vaiṣṇava māyā will not affect you in any way. / Come out from this very terrible, condemned hell.

5.146.s:
garbhavāsāttato yogaṃ samāśritya śivaṃ vraja ..
tasmāddarśaya me vaktraṃ svakīyaṃ yena me bhavet ..
ānṛṇyaṃ pitṛlokasya tava vaktrasya darśanāt .. 29 ..
5.146.d:
गर्भवासात्ततो योगं समाश्रित्य शिवं व्रज ..
तस्माद्दर्शय मे वक्त्रं स्वकीयं येन मे भवेत् ..
आनृण्यं पितृलोकस्य तव वक्त्रस्य दर्शनात् .. 29 ..
5.146.m: From residing in the womb, take refuge in yoga and attain what is auspicious. / Therefore, show me your face, so that by seeing your face / I may be freed from my debt to the world of the ancestors."

5.146.s:
.. garbha uvāca .. ..
vāsudevaṃ pratibhuvaṃ yadi me tvaṃ prayacchasi ..
idānīṃ yatsvayaṃ tanme janma syānnānyathā dvija .. 6.147.30 ..
5.146.d:
.. गर्भ उवाच .. ..
वासुदेवं प्रतिभुवं यदि मे त्वं प्रयच्छसि ..
इदानीं यत्स्वयं तन्मे जन्म स्यान्नान्यथा द्विज .. 6.147.30 ..
5.146.m: The embryo said: / "If you give me Vāsudeva as a guarantor, / only then will my birth take place by myself now, not otherwise, O brahmin."

5.146.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tato vyāso drutaṃ gatvā dvārakāṃ prati duḥkhitaḥ ..
kathayāmāsa vṛttāṃtaṃ vistarāccakrapāṇine .. 31 ..
5.146.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततो व्यासो द्रुतं गत्वा द्वारकां प्रति दुःखितः ..
कथयामास वृत्तांतं विस्तराच्चक्रपाणिने .. 31 ..
5.146.m: Sūta said: / Then Vyāsa, sorrowful, went quickly to Dvārakā, / and told the whole matter in detail to the wielder of the discus.

5.146.s:
tenaiva sahitaḥ paścātsvagṛhaṃ punarāgataḥ ..
vyāsaḥ pratibhuvaṃ tasmai dātuṃ viṣṇuṃ niraṃjanam .. 32 ..
5.146.d:
तेनैव सहितः पश्चात्स्वगृहं पुनरागतः ..
व्यासः प्रतिभुवं तस्मै दातुं विष्णुं निरंजनम् .. 32 ..
5.146.m: Accompanied by him, Vyāsa then returned to his own home / to give him the immaculate Viṣṇu as a guarantor.

5.146.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
pratibhūrasmi nāśāya māyāyāstava nirgame ..
madvākyānniṣkramaṃ kṛtvā gaccha mokṣamanuttamam .. 33 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीकृष्ण उवाच .. ..
प्रतिभूरस्मि नाशाय मायायास्तव निर्गमे ..
मद्वाक्यान्निष्क्रमं कृत्वा गच्छ मोक्षमनुत्तमम् .. 33 ..
5.146.m: The venerable Kṛṣṇa said: / "I am your guarantor against the destruction caused by māyā upon your emergence. / Having come out at my word, go to unexcelled liberation."

5.146.s:
tato drutaṃ viniṣkrāṃto viṣṇuvākyena sa dvijāḥ ..
dvādaśābdapramāṇastu yauvanasya samīpagaḥ .. 34 ..
5.146.d:
ततो द्रुतं विनिष्क्रांतो विष्णुवाक्येन स द्विजाः ..
द्वादशाब्दप्रमाणस्तु यौवनस्य समीपगः .. 34 ..
5.146.m: Then, O brahmins, at the word of Viṣṇu, he quickly came out, / twelve years old in stature and approaching youth.

5.146.s:
tataḥ praṇamya daityāriṃ vyāsaṃ ca jananīṃ tathā ..
prasthito vanavāsāya tatkṣaṇādvyāsanaṃdanaḥ .. 35 ..
5.146.d:
ततः प्रणम्य दैत्यारिं व्यासं च जननीं तथा ..
प्रस्थितो वनवासाय तत्क्षणाद्व्यासनंदनः .. 35 ..
5.146.m: Then, having bowed to the enemy of the Daityas, to Vyāsa, and likewise to his mother, / that son of Vyāsa immediately set out to live in the forest.

5.146.s:
atha taṃ sa muniḥ prāha tiṣṭha putrātmamaṃdire ..
saṃskārāñjātakādyāṃśca yena te prakaromyaham .. 36 ..
5.146.d:
अथ तं स मुनिः प्राह तिष्ठ पुत्रात्ममंदिरे ..
संस्काराञ्जातकाद्यांश्च येन ते प्रकरोम्यहम् .. 36 ..
5.146.m: Then that sage said to him, "Stay in your own house, son, / so that I may perform the life-cycle rites for you, beginning with the birth ritual."

5.146.s:
.. śiśuruvāca .. ..
saṃskārāḥ śataśo jātā mama janmanijanmani ..
bhavārṇave parikṣipto yairahaṃ bandhanātmakaiḥ .. 37 ..
5.146.d:
.. शिशुरुवाच .. ..
संस्काराः शतशो जाता मम जन्मनिजन्मनि ..
भवार्णवे परिक्षिप्तो यैरहं बन्धनात्मकैः .. 37 ..
5.146.m: The child said: / "Hundreds of life-cycle rites have been performed for me in birth after birth, / through which, having the nature of bonds, I have been thrown into the ocean of worldly existence."

5.146.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
śukavajjalpate yasmāttavāyaṃ putrako mune ..
tasmācchuko'yaṃ nāmnāstu yogavidyāvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 38 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
शुकवज्जल्पते यस्मात्तवायं पुत्रको मुने ..
तस्माच्छुकोऽयं नाम्नास्तु योगविद्याविचक्षणः .. 38 ..
5.146.m: The Blessed One said: / "Since this son of yours prattles like a parrot, O sage, / therefore let him be Śuka by name, skilled in the science of yoga.

5.146.s:
nāyaṃ sthāsyati harmye sve mohamāyāvivarjitaḥ ..
tasmādgacchatu mā snehaṃ tvaṃ kuruṣvāsya saṃbhavam .. 39 ..
5.146.d:
नायं स्थास्यति हर्म्ये स्वे मोहमायाविवर्जितः ..
तस्माद्गच्छतु मा स्नेहं त्वं कुरुष्वास्य संभवम् .. 39 ..
5.146.m: He will not stay in his mansion, being free from delusion and māyā. / Therefore, let him go; do not form an attachment to him.

5.146.s:
ahaṃ gṛhaṃ prayāsyāmi tvaṃ muktaḥ paitṛkādṛṇāt..
darśanādeva putrasya satyametanmayoditam .. 6.147.40 ..
5.146.d:
अहं गृहं प्रयास्यामि त्वं मुक्तः पैतृकादृणात्..
दर्शनादेव पुत्रस्य सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 6.147.40 ..
5.146.m: I shall go home; you are freed from the ancestral debt / merely by seeing your son; this that I have spoken is true."

5.146.s:
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśo vyāsamāmaṃtrya satvaram..
vihagādhipamārūḍhaḥ prayayau dvārakāṃ prati .. 41 ..
5.146.d:
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशो व्यासमामंत्र्य सत्वरम्..
विहगाधिपमारूढः प्रययौ द्वारकां प्रति .. 41 ..
5.146.m: Having spoken thus and quickly taken leave of Vyāsa, Hṛṣīkeśa, / mounted on the king of birds, departed for Dvārakā.

5.146.s:
tato gate hṛṣīkeśe vyāsaḥ putramuvāca ha ..
prasthitaṃ vanavāsāya niḥspṛhaṃ svagṛhaṃ prati .. 42 ..
5.146.d:
ततो गते हृषीकेशे व्यासः पुत्रमुवाच ह ..
प्रस्थितं वनवासाय निःस्पृहं स्वगृहं प्रति .. 42 ..
5.146.m: Then, when Hṛṣīkeśa had gone, Vyāsa indeed said to his son, / who had set out to dwell in the forest and had no attachment to his own home:

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca.. ..
gṛhasthadharmariktānāṃ pitṛvākyaṃ praṇaśyati ..
pitṛvākyaṃ tu yo mohānnaiva samyaksamācaret..
sa yāti narakaṃ tasmānmadvākyātputra mā vraja .. 43 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच.. ..
गृहस्थधर्मरिक्तानां पितृवाक्यं प्रणश्यति ..
पितृवाक्यं तु यो मोहान्नैव सम्यक्समाचरेत्..
स याति नरकं तस्मान्मद्वाक्यात्पुत्र मा व्रज .. 43 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / "The father's command is destroyed for those devoid of the duties of a householder. / But whoever, through delusion, does not properly follow his father's command / goes to hell; therefore, at my word, son, do not go."

5.146.s:
.. śuka uvāca .. ..
yathādyāhaṃ tvayā jāto mayā tvaṃ cānyajanmani ..
saṃjāto'si muniśreṣṭha tathāhamapi te pitā .. 44 ..
5.146.d:
.. शुक उवाच .. ..
यथाद्याहं त्वया जातो मया त्वं चान्यजन्मनि ..
संजातोऽसि मुनिश्रेष्ठ तथाहमपि ते पिता .. 44 ..
5.146.m: Śuka said: / "Just as I am born from you today, so you in another birth / were born from me, O best of sages; thus I too am your father.

5.146.s:
tasmādvākyaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ yadyeṣā dharmasaṃsthitiḥ ..
nāhaṃ niṣedhanīyastu vrajamānastapovanam .. 45 ..
5.146.d:
तस्माद्वाक्यं त्वया कार्यं यद्येषा धर्मसंस्थितिः ..
नाहं निषेधनीयस्तु व्रजमानस्तपोवनम् .. 45 ..
5.146.m: Therefore you must obey my word, if this is the established rule of dharma. / I must not be forbidden as I go to the forest of austerities."

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
brāhmaṇasya gṛhe janma puṇyaiḥ saṃprāpyate nṛbhiḥ ..
saṃskārānyatra saṃprāpya vedoktānmunirāpyate .. 46 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
ब्राह्मणस्य गृहे जन्म पुण्यैः संप्राप्यते नृभिः ..
संस्कारान्यत्र संप्राप्य वेदोक्तान्मुनिराप्यते .. 46 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / "Birth in the house of a brahmin is attained by men through merits; / having received in it the rites prescribed in the Veda, one attains the state of a sage."

5.146.s:
.. śuka uvāca .. ..
saṃskārairāpyate muktiryadi karma śubhaṃ vinā ..
pākhaṃḍino'pi yāsyaṃti tanmuktiṃ vratadhāriṇaḥ .. 47 ..
5.146.d:
.. शुक उवाच .. ..
संस्कारैराप्यते मुक्तिर्यदि कर्म शुभं विना ..
पाखंडिनोऽपि यास्यंति तन्मुक्तिं व्रतधारिणः .. 47 ..
5.146.m: Śuka said: / "If liberation is attained through life-cycle rites without good action, / then even heretics observing vows would attain liberation.

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
brahmacārī bhavetpūrvaṃ gṛhasthaśca tataḥ param ..
vānaprastho yatiścaiva tato mokṣamavāpnuyāt .. 48 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
ब्रह्मचारी भवेत्पूर्वं गृहस्थश्च ततः परम् ..
वानप्रस्थो यतिश्चैव ततो मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् .. 48 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / "One should first be a student, and after that a householder; / then a forest-dweller, and then an ascetic; thereby one would attain liberation."

5.146.s:
.. śuka uvāca .. ..
brahmacaryeṇa cenmokṣastatṣaṇḍhānāṃ sadā bhavet ..
gṛhasthāśramiṇāṃ cetsyāttatsarvaṃ mucyate jagat .. 49 ..
5.146.d:
.. शुक उवाच .. ..
ब्रह्मचर्येण चेन्मोक्षस्तत्षण्ढानां सदा भवेत् ..
गृहस्थाश्रमिणां चेत्स्यात्तत्सर्वं मुच्यते जगत् .. 49 ..
5.146.m: Śuka said: / "If liberation came through celibacy, then eunuchs would always have it. / If it belonged to those in the householder's stage, then the entire world would be liberated.

5.146.s: athavā vanaraktānāṃ tanmṛgāṇāṃ prajāyate .. 6.147.50 ..
5.146.d: अथवा वनरक्तानां तन्मृगाणां प्रजायते .. 6.147.50 ..
5.146.m: Or, if [it comes] to those delighting in the forest, then it would happen to wild beasts.

5.146.s:
athavā yatidharmāṇāṃ yadi mokṣo bhavennṛṇām ..
daridrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tanmuktiḥ prathamā bhavet .. 51 ..
5.146.d:
अथवा यतिधर्माणां यदि मोक्षो भवेन्नृणाम् ..
दरिद्राणां च सर्वेषां तन्मुक्तिः प्रथमा भवेत् .. 51 ..
5.146.m: Or if liberation belonged to mortals who observe the duties of an ascetic, / then liberation would belong first of all to the poor.

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
gṛhasthadharmaraktānāṃ nṛṇāṃ sanmārgagāminām ..
iha lokaḥ paraścaiva manunā saṃprakīrtitaḥ .. 52 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
गृहस्थधर्मरक्तानां नृणां सन्मार्गगामिनाम् ..
इह लोकः परश्चैव मनुना संप्रकीर्तितः .. 52 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / For men delighted in the duties of a householder and walking on the virtuous path, / this world and also the next have been declared by Manu.

5.146.s:
.. śrīśuka uvāca .. ..
gṛhaguptau suguptānāṃ baṃdhānāṃ baṃdhubaṃdhanaiḥ ..
moharāgasamāveśātsanmārga gamanaṃ kutaḥ .. 53 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीशुक उवाच .. ..
गृहगुप्तौ सुगुप्तानां बंधानां बंधुबंधनैः ..
मोहरागसमावेशात्सन्मार्ग गमनं कुतः .. 53 ..
5.146.m: Śrī Śuka said: / For those who are well hidden within the prison of the home, bound by the bonds of kinsmen, / absorbed in delusion and passion, how can there be journeying on the virtuous path?

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. .
kaṣṭaṃ vane nivasato'tra sadā narasya no kevalaṃ nijatanuprabhavaṃ bhavecca .
daivaṃ ca pitryamakhilaṃ na vibhāti kṛtyaṃ tasmādgṛhe nivasatātmahitaṃ pracintyam .. 54 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. .
कष्टं वने निवसतोऽत्र सदा नरस्य नो केवलं निजतनुप्रभवं भवेच्च .
दैवं च पित्र्यमखिलं न विभाति कृत्यं तस्माद्गृहे निवसतात्महितं प्रचिन्त्यम् .. 54 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / Miserable is it for a man living constantly in the forest here, and not only does it spring from one's own body; / but the rites for the gods and all those for the ancestors do not shine forth; therefore, dwelling at home, one should reflect on the welfare of the self.

5.146.s:
.. śrīśukadeva uvāca .. ..
bhāvena bhāvitamahātapasāṃ munīnāṃ tiṣṭhanti tāvadakhilāni tapaḥphalāni ..
yatte nikāśaśaraṇāḥ puruṣā na jātu paśyaṃtyasajjanamukhāni sukhaṃ tadeva .. 55 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीशुकदेव उवाच .. ..
भावेन भावितमहातपसां मुनीनां तिष्ठन्ति तावदखिलानि तपःफलानि ..
यत्ते निकाशशरणाः पुरुषा न जातु पश्यंत्यसज्जनमुखानि सुखं तदेव .. 55 ..
5.146.m: Śrī Śukadeva said: / For sages of great austerity refined by meditation, all the fruits of austerity remain, / since those men, having daylight for their shelter, never look upon the faces of wicked people—that alone is happiness.

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
gṛhaṃ parigrahaḥ puṃsāṃ gṛhasthāśramadharmiṇām ..
ihaloke pare caiva sukhaṃ yacchati śāśvatam .. 56 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
गृहं परिग्रहः पुंसां गृहस्थाश्रमधर्मिणाम् ..
इहलोके परे चैव सुखं यच्छति शाश्वतम् .. 56 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / A home and family for men who observe the duty of the householder's stage of life / grant perpetual happiness both in this world and in the next.

5.146.s:
.. śrīśuka uvāca .. ..
śītaṃ hutāśādapi daivayogātsañjāyate candramaso'pi tāpaḥ ..
parigrahātsaukhyasamudbhavo'tra bhūto'bhavadbhāvi na martyaloke .. 57 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीशुक उवाच .. ..
शीतं हुताशादपि दैवयोगात्सञ्जायते चन्द्रमसोऽपि तापः ..
परिग्रहात्सौख्यसमुद्भवोऽत्र भूतोऽभवद्भावि न मर्त्यलोके .. 57 ..
5.146.m: Śrī Śuka said: / Even cold might arise from fire through the play of fate, or heat even from the moon; / but happiness arising from possessions and family in this mortal world never was, is not, and will not be.

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
supuṇyairlabhyate kṛcchrānmānuṣyaṃ bhuvi durlabham ..
tasmim̐llabdhe na kiṃ labdhaṃ yadi syādgṛhadharmavit .. 58 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
सुपुण्यैर्लभ्यते कृच्छ्रान्मानुष्यं भुवि दुर्लभम् ..
तस्मिम्̐ल्लब्धे न किं लब्धं यदि स्याद्गृहधर्मवित् .. 58 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / Human birth, rare on earth, is attained with difficulty through great merits; / when that is attained, what has not been attained if one knows the duty of a householder?

5.146.s:
.. śrīśukadeva uvāca .. ..
yadi syājjñānasaṃyukto janmakāletra mānavaḥ ..
nijāvasthāṃ samālokya tajjñānaṃ hi vilīyate .. 59 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीशुकदेव उवाच .. ..
यदि स्याज्ज्ञानसंयुक्तो जन्मकालेत्र मानवः ..
निजावस्थां समालोक्य तज्ज्ञानं हि विलीयते .. 59 ..
5.146.m: Śrī Śukadeva said: / Even if a man here were endowed with knowledge at the time of birth, / upon beholding his own condition, that knowledge indeed dissolves.

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
muditasyāpi putrasya gardabhasyārbhakasya ca ..
bhasmalolasya lokasya śabdo'pi raṭato mude .. 6.147.60 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
मुदितस्यापि पुत्रस्य गर्दभस्यार्भकस्य च ..
भस्मलोलस्य लोकस्य शब्दोऽपि रटतो मुदे .. 6.147.60 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / Even of a son, or a donkey, or an infant / playing in the dust, the sound of one crying out brings joy to a person.

5.146.s:
.. śrīśuka uvāca .. ..
rasatā sarpatā dhūli loke tvaśucinā ciram ..
mune'tra śiśunā lokastuṣṭiṃ yāti sa bāliśaḥ .. 61 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीशुक उवाच .. ..
रसता सर्पता धूलि लोके त्वशुचिना चिरम् ..
मुनेऽत्र शिशुना लोकस्तुष्टिं याति स बालिशः .. 61 ..
5.146.m: Śrī Śuka said: / With an infant screaming, crawling, rolling in dust, and filthy for a long time, / O sage, a person here finds pleasure—such a fool is he!

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
puṃnāmāsti mahāraudro narako yamamandire ..
putrahīno vrajettatra tena putraḥ praśasyate .. 62 ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
पुंनामास्ति महारौद्रो नरको यममन्दिरे ..
पुत्रहीनो व्रजेत्तत्र तेन पुत्रः प्रशस्यते .. 62 ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / There is a terrible hell named Put in the abode of Yama; / one without a son goes there; therefore a son is praised.

5.146.s:
.. śrīśuka uvāca .. ..
yadi syātputrataḥ svargaḥ sarveṣāṃ syānmahāmune ..
śūkarāṇāṃ śunāṃ caiva śalabhānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. .. 63 ..
5.146.d:
.. श्रीशुक उवाच .. ..
यदि स्यात्पुत्रतः स्वर्गः सर्वेषां स्यान्महामुने ..
शूकराणां शुनां चैव शलभानां विशेषतः .. .. 63 ..
5.146.m: Śrī Śuka said: / If heaven came from having a son, O great sage, it would belong to all— / especially to pigs, dogs, and locusts.

5.146.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
pitṝṇāmanṛṇo martyo jāyate putradarśanāt ..
pautrasyāpi ca devānāṃ prapautrasya divāśrayaḥ .. 64 .. ..
5.146.d:
.. व्यास उवाच .. ..
पितॄणामनृणो मर्त्यो जायते पुत्रदर्शनात् ..
पौत्रस्यापि च देवानां प्रपौत्रस्य दिवाश्रयः .. 64 .. ..
5.146.m: Vyāsa said: / From the sight of a son, a mortal becomes free from debt to the ancestors; / from a grandson, to the gods; and from a great-grandson, he finds an abode in heaven.

5.146.s:
śuka uvāca .. ..
cirāyurjjāyate gṛdhraḥ saṃtatiṃ paśyate nijām ..
krameṇa saṃtataṃ kiṃ na sa mokṣaṃ pratipadyate .. 65 ..
5.146.d:
शुक उवाच .. ..
चिरायुर्ज्जायते गृध्रः संततिं पश्यते निजाम् ..
क्रमेण संततं किं न स मोक्षं प्रतिपद्यते .. 65 ..
5.146.m: Śuka said: / A vulture lives long and beholds its own progeny / continually in succession; does it not attain liberation?

5.146.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā parityajya pitaraṃ sa vanaṃ gataḥ ..
mātaraṃ ca suduḥkhārtāṃ pralapantīmanekadhā .. 66 ..
5.146.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा परित्यज्य पितरं स वनं गतः ..
मातरं च सुदुःखार्तां प्रलपन्तीमनेकधा .. 66 ..
5.146.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, he abandoned his father and his mother, / who was afflicted with great sorrow and lamenting in many ways, and went to the forest.

5.146.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhito vyāso nirāśaḥ putradarśane ..
putraśokābhisaṃtapto bhāryayā sahito'bhavat .. 67 ..
5.146.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा दुःखितो व्यासो निराशः पुत्रदर्शने ..
पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तो भार्यया सहितोऽभवत् .. 67 ..
5.146.m: Seeing him [leave], Vyāsa, grieved, hopeless of seeing his son again / and consumed by grief for his son, remained with his wife.

5.146.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye vyāsaśukasaṃvādavarṇanaṃnāma saptacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamodhyāyaḥ .. 147 .. cha ..
5.146.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये व्यासशुकसंवादवर्णनंनाम सप्तचत्वारिंशदुत्तरशततमोध्यायः .. 147 .. छ ..
5.146.m: Thus ends the one hundred forty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Dialogue of Vyāsa and Śuka', in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the description of the glorious Hāṭakeśvarakṣetra. // 147

5.147.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ taṃ niḥspṛhaṃ jñātvā gṛhaṃ prati nijātmajam ..
piṃgalā duḥkhasaṃyuktā vyāsametaduvāca ha .. 1 ..
5.147.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं तं निःस्पृहं ज्ञात्वा गृहं प्रति निजात्मजम् ..
पिंगला दुःखसंयुक्ता व्यासमेतदुवाच ह .. 1 ..
5.147.m: Sūta said: / Knowing thus that her son was free from desire for domestic life, / Piṅgalā, filled with sorrow, addressed Vyāsa in this way:

5.147.s:
ahaṃ tapaścariṣyāmi putrārthaṃ dvijasattama ..
anujñāṃ dehi me yena toṣayāmi maheśvaram ..
putro yena bhavenmahyaṃ vaṃśavṛddhikaraḥ paraḥ .. 2 ..
5.147.d:
अहं तपश्चरिष्यामि पुत्रार्थं द्विजसत्तम ..
अनुज्ञां देहि मे येन तोषयामि महेश्वरम् ..
पुत्रो येन भवेन्मह्यं वंशवृद्धिकरः परः .. 2 ..
5.147.m: 'I will perform austerity for the sake of a son, O best of the twice-born; / grant me permission, so that I may propitiate Maheśvara, / so that a son may be born to me, an excellent perpetuator of the lineage.'

5.147.s:
evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā labdhvānujñāṃ munestataḥ ..
kṣetrametatsamāsādya tapastepe pativratā .. 3 ..
5.147.d:
एवं सा निश्चयं कृत्वा लब्ध्वानुज्ञां मुनेस्ततः ..
क्षेत्रमेतत्समासाद्य तपस्तेपे पतिव्रता .. 3 ..
5.147.m: Having thus made her resolve and obtained permission from the sage, / the devoted wife approached this sacred field and performed austerity,

5.147.s:
saṃsthāpya śaṃkaraṃ devaṃ tadagre nirmalodakam ..
kṛtvā vāpīṃ suvistīrṇāṃ snānātpātakanāśanīm .. 4 ..
5.147.d:
संस्थाप्य शंकरं देवं तदग्रे निर्मलोदकम् ..
कृत्वा वापीं सुविस्तीर्णां स्नानात्पातकनाशनीम् .. 4 ..
5.147.m: having installed the god Śaṃkara and, in front of him, / made a very large step-well of clear water, destroying sins upon ritual ablution.

5.147.s:
tatastasyā gatastuṣṭiṃ bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ ..
varado'smīti tāṃ prāha prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā .. 5 ..
5.147.d:
ततस्तस्या गतस्तुष्टिं भगवांस्त्रिपुरांतकः ..
वरदोऽस्मीति तां प्राह प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना .. 5 ..
5.147.m: Then the blessed slayer of Tripura, having attained satisfaction with her, / with a delighted heart spoke to her, saying, 'I am the granter of boons.'

5.147.s:
.. śrīmahādeva uvāca .. ..
parituṣṭo'smi te bhadre varaṃ varaya suvrate ..
yaḥ sthito hṛdaye nityaṃ nādeyaṃ vidyate mama .. 6 ..
5.147.d:
.. श्रीमहादेव उवाच .. ..
परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भद्रे वरं वरय सुव्रते ..
यः स्थितो हृदये नित्यं नादेयं विद्यते मम .. 6 ..
5.147.m: Śrī Mahādeva said: / 'I am well-pleased with you, auspicious lady of good vows; choose a boon / that has dwelt continually in your heart; there is nothing that cannot be given by me.'

5.147.s:
.. vaṭikovāca .. ..
sutaṃ dehi suraśreṣṭha mama vaṃśavivardhanam ..
cittāhlādakaraṃ nityaṃ suśīlaṃ vinayānvitam .. 7 .. ..
5.147.d:
.. वटिकोवाच .. ..
सुतं देहि सुरश्रेष्ठ मम वंशविवर्धनम् ..
चित्ताह्लादकरं नित्यं सुशीलं विनयान्वितम् .. 7 .. ..
5.147.m: Vaṭikā said: / 'Grant me a son, O best of gods, who will multiply my lineage, / constantly delighting my heart, well-behaved, and endowed with humility.'

5.147.s:
.. śrīmahādeva uvāca .. ..
bhaviṣyati na saṃdehastava putraḥ suśobhane ..
yādṛktvayā mahābhāge prārthitastadviśeṣataḥ .. 8 ..
5.147.d:
.. श्रीमहादेव उवाच .. ..
भविष्यति न संदेहस्तव पुत्रः सुशोभने ..
यादृक्त्वया महाभागे प्रार्थितस्तद्विशेषतः .. 8 ..
5.147.m: Śrī Mahādeva said: / 'There will be a son to you without a doubt, O beautiful woman, / just as he was requested by you, O fortunate one, and even better.

5.147.s:
anyāpi mānuṣī yā'tra vāpyāṃ snātvā samāhitā ..
pañcamyāṃ vatsaraṃ yāvacchuklapakṣe hyupasthite ..
pūjayiṣyati malliṃgaṃ yaccādya sthāpitaṃ tvayā .. 9 ..
5.147.d:
अन्यापि मानुषी याऽत्र वाप्यां स्नात्वा समाहिता ..
पञ्चम्यां वत्सरं यावच्छुक्लपक्षे ह्युपस्थिते ..
पूजयिष्यति मल्लिंगं यच्चाद्य स्थापितं त्वया .. 9 ..
5.147.m: Any other mortal woman who, composed in mind, bathes here in the step-well / on the fifth day when the bright fortnight has arrived, throughout a year, / and worships my liṅga that has been established by you today,

5.147.s:
sātha lapsyati satputraṃ dattvā phalamanuttamam ..
yā ca daurbhāgyasaṃyuktā tṛtīyādivase'tra vai .. 6.148.10 ..
5.147.d:
साथ लप्स्यति सत्पुत्रं दत्त्वा फलमनुत्तमम् ..
या च दौर्भाग्यसंयुक्ता तृतीयादिवसेऽत्र वै .. 6.148.10 ..
5.147.m: having offered an unsurpassed fruit, she shall obtain a virtuous son. / And whatever woman, afflicted with misfortune, on the third lunar day here indeed,

5.147.s:
snātvā'tra salile paścānmalliṃgaṃ pūjayiṣyati ..
sā saubhāgya samopetā varṣāṃte ca bhaviṣyati .. 11 ..
5.147.d:
स्नात्वाऽत्र सलिले पश्चान्मल्लिंगं पूजयिष्यति ..
सा सौभाग्य समोपेता वर्षांते च भविष्यति .. 11 ..
5.147.m: having bathed here in the water, shall then worship my liṅga, / she will be endowed with good fortune at the end of the year.

5.147.s:
yaḥ punaḥ puruṣaścātra snātvā māṃ pūjayiṣyati ..
sakāmo lapsyate kāmānvikāmo mokṣameva ca .. 12 ..
5.147.d:
यः पुनः पुरुषश्चात्र स्नात्वा मां पूजयिष्यति ..
सकामो लप्स्यते कामान्विकामो मोक्षमेव च .. 12 ..
5.147.m: Moreover, whatever man, having bathed here, will worship me, / if full of desire, he will obtain his desires, and if free from desire, liberation itself.'

5.147.s:
evamuktvā mahādevastataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ ..
sā'pi lebhe sutaṃ vyāsātkapiṃjalamiti śrutam .. 13 ..
5.147.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महादेवस्ततश्चादर्शनं गतः ..
साऽपि लेभे सुतं व्यासात्कपिंजलमिति श्रुतम् .. 13 ..
5.147.m: Having spoken thus, Mahādeva vanished from there; / and she too obtained from Vyāsa a son renowned as Kapiñjala,

5.147.s:
yādṛktena purā prokto devadevena śūlinā ..
yenaiva sthāpitā cātra devī kelīvarī purā ..
sarvasiddhipradā loke tatra yā''rādhitā purā .. 14 ..
5.147.d:
यादृक्तेन पुरा प्रोक्तो देवदेवेन शूलिना ..
येनैव स्थापिता चात्र देवी केलीवरी पुरा ..
सर्वसिद्धिप्रदा लोके तत्र या'ऽराधिता पुरा .. 14 ..
5.147.m: just as was formerly stated by the god of gods, the spear-wielder, / by whom also the goddess Kelīśvarī was formerly installed here, / the granter of all perfections in the world, where she was formerly worshipped.

5.147.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye vaṭikeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 148 .. .. cha ..
5.147.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये वटिकेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः .. 148 .. .. छ ..
5.147.m: Thus ends the one hundred forty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Vaṭikeśvara', in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. // 148
